nodes.label: §2 Stack (the same in every app)
nodes.text:
· Rust + Tauri 2 desktop shell (src-tauri), Windows first (NSIS per-user installer, WebView2).
· Engine in a pure-Rust crate (crates/core): all calculation lives there, with unit tests. The window only shows what the engine computes.
· UI: SolidJS + Vite + strict TypeScript in ui/src/*.tsx, built to ui/dist (embedded at compile time). State in ui/src/store.ts. Plain CSS with tokens (no CSS framework).
· Charts: Chart.js in the family chart style (see §7). An app may add its own SVG plot engine for publication graphs, but must keep this look.
· Spreadsheet formulas: the GridCraft crates (pinned git dependency, attribution in NOTICE) where the app needs them.
· Sheets inside an app (from Datum Plan 0.5.0) behave like a spreadsheet through GridCraft (references by clicking, suggestions, fill and paste that move references, insert and delete rows) and read the app's data by name: GridCraft tables and workbook names, not copied values. Countries show as flags from bundled SVGs (flag-icons, MIT), never emoji.
· No Python inside the apps (size and second runtime). The one exception is Datum Plot, which bundles its own Python (numpy, SciPy, matplotlib) for statistics and graphs; the decision is recorded in Plot's docs/MEMORY.md.
· Small, compact code that matches the surrounding style.

nodes.label: §4 Type
nodes.text:
· IBM Plex Sans for text, IBM Plex Mono for uppercase spaced labels, tabs, buttons, numbers and IDs (@fontsource, Latin subsets only, about 200 kB).
· Group captions, card headings and buttons: Plex Mono, 9.5–11 px, letter-spacing: .1em, uppercase.
· Body 12–13 px; page titles 23 px, 600–700 weight.
· Tables and grids: 12–13 px; numbers right-aligned.

nodes.label: §5 Logo and branding
nodes.text:
· Tile: 256×256 viewBox, a rounded square (x=8 y=8 w=240 h=240 rx=56), a white→accent-tint diagonal gradient, and a 4 px border in a light accent tint.
· Glyph: drawn in the accent with 11 px strokes, round caps. It may use one light tint fill (the --sky colour). It always has one amber #F2B233 diamond (the family mark).
· Files: ui/public/logo.svg (in the app) and docs/brand/datum-<app>-icon.svg (README). Windows icons are generated from it (npx tauri icon). Copies of every icon, and the family mark, are in this repo's brand/.
· The family mark ("Continuum", designed by the user): two concentric D's drawn as one continuous line, with the amber #F2B233 datum square where the line starts. Navy #0C1A2B (or light #E6EDF5) ink only, never an app colour, so it stays right however many apps the family has. Files, construction and rules: brand/BRAND.md (datum-logo.svg, datum-mark.svg, datum-icon.svg and light versions).
· Name: "Datum <App>" in Plex Sans 600. Tagline in the README.
· README: the logo, the name, a one-line tagline, shields.io badges (release, CI, downloads, license MIT, platform Windows 10/11, Rust, Tauri 2, SolidJS), then for-the-badge buttons (Download for Windows · What's new · Memory & roadmap), then a screenshot.

nodes.label: §6 Window layout
nodes.text:
· Title bar: quick access (save, undo, redo, print), document name, "Tell me what you want to do" (Ctrl+K), a Theme button (Auto/Light/Dark).
· Ribbon: a FILE button in the accent, then tabs. Groups have a mono uppercase caption. Big buttons have an icon above the label; split buttons have the command on top and the menu on the bottom ▾. Contextual tabs carry a small label above them. The ribbon never scrolls sideways: it tightens, then folds groups from the right (icons only).
· Left sidebar: icon + mono label per view, with Setup first. Groups are separated by rules.
· File page (backstage): a sidebar in the accent colour (Home, New, Open, Import, Save, Save As, Export, Print; Options and Updates at the bottom).
· Home: template tiles, recent files, a Roadmap tile, and the updates card. The card has Check again with a spinner and the time it checked, and the GitHub, Releases and Report an Issue buttons.
· Status bar: Ready, key facts, view switches, zoom.
· Options page: sections (General, Start-up and saving, New <documents>, Printing and branding, Updates). Each option has a name plus a one-line hint on the left and the control on the right.
· Help tab:
· Getting Started: written for people coming from other tools, in plain words;
· Glossary: plain-language terms, searchable;
· Shortcuts, Tell Me, What Is This Tool?;
· the GitHub links.
· ? help beside the tools: a small ? beside each ribbon group, page, panel and main dialog opens a card (what it is for, how to use it) from one HELP table in ui/src/help.tsx.

nodes.label: §7 Components
§8 Printing
nodes.text:
· File › Print (Ctrl+P) shows settings on the left and a live page preview on the right, for every view.
· The settings: paper, orientation, scaling or fit-to-pages, margins, page ranges, header and footer (left/centre/right) with codes and logos, legend, and view options.
· Pages are drawn as SVG at real size and printed with the WebView dialog ("Save as PDF").
· Report-type pages print as flowing documents with the header and footer on every page and page numbers.
· Reuse Plan's print.tsx (Frame, Slot, codes).

nodes.label: §9 Updates and releases
nodes.text:
· Updater: src-tauri/src/update.rs.
· Set REPO to the app's repo. It checks GitHub releases at start, and beta versions when turned on.
· It downloads the installer, checks SHA256SUMS and installs.
· The CHANGELOG section becomes the in-app "What's new".
· Versions: small numbered releases (0.1.0, 0.1.1, …), always three numbers (the updater compares three), consecutive with no jumped numbers.
· Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml, windows-latest):
· builds the UI and the app and creates the tag;
· publishes Datum<App>-x.y.z-setup.exe + SHA256SUMS.txt.
· Run it with workflow_dispatch when tag pushes are blocked.
· CI (ci.yml, ubuntu): clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, npm run check:ui, the Playwright UI tests.
· Options and recovery files in the app's data folder (com.edgarmendonca.datum<app>).
· Datum Home (home/ in DATUM) installs and updates every app from one window. It relies on this release shape: a per-user NSIS installer named Datum<App>-x.y.z-setup.exe that accepts /S, a SHA256SUMS.txt beside it, the Windows display name equal to the app's name in apps.json ("Datum Plan") and the publisher "Datum" (bundle.publisher in tauri.conf.json; apps released before 2026-10-29 used "Edgar Mendonca", which Datum Home still accepts). A release without SHA256SUMS.txt is never installed by Datum Home.
· The family site rebuilds every hour and on every push to DATUM, so a release appears there within the hour (or at once: run the "Pages" workflow in DATUM).

nodes.label: §10 Docs in every repo
nodes.text:
· CLAUDE.md: read MEMORY first; update it at the end of every session; the user's preferences; the checks; the release steps.
· docs/MEMORY.md: product table, architecture (files), decisions (version | decision | why), roadmap (✅ 🔜 ⬜), session log, known limits, and the "How we work" workflow.
· CHANGELOG.md: ## x.y.z — date, a one-line summary, then bold sections in plain language for users. The site shows the last five sections.
· docs/site.json: the app's public summary, read by the family site at build time and by File › Roadmap in the app:
json
{
"id": "plan", "name": "Datum Plan", "accent": "#0B5CAD",
"logo": "docs/brand/datum-plan-icon.svg",
"tagline": "…", "for": "…",
"about": ["One or two plain paragraphs: what the app is and how it helps."],
"steps": [{ "title": "Enter the tasks", "text": "…" }, { "title": "…", "text": "…" }, { "title": "…", "text": "…" }],
"highlights": ["…"],
"screenshots": ["docs/images/gantt.png"],
"roadmap": [{ "v": "0.3.11", "title": "Fixes", "when": "Next", "items": ["…"] }]
}
when is one of Next, Soon, Later, Goal. Screenshots are 1440×900 PNGs in docs/images/; the app's page on the site shows the first four. about and steps (three steps: how the app is used) fill the Overview of the app's page (/apps/<id>); until an app sets them, the hub's apps.json supplies them.
· The brain: DATUM's brain/graph.json is generated from these files (node brain/brain.mjs); keep the MEMORY tables (Files, Decisions, Roadmap, Session log, How we work) in the same shape so it can read them.
· docs/PLAN-x.y.md: feedback → diagnosis → proposal → size → question

nodes.label: §11 How we work (from Datum Plan)
nodes.text:
· The user reviews a release and sends screenshots.
· Reproduce first.
· Big asks get a plan file and questions; build after the answers.
· Engine first (with a test), then the UI.
· Check every change in the real app (Xvfb screenshots).
· Add a UI test for every bug.
· Run all checks: clippy -D warnings, cargo test (with the hardening tests below), the UI type-check and UI tests, cargo deny check.
· Release.
· Report in plain language: what changed, what was checked, what is not done.
Hardening standard (every app, from Datum Plan 0.3.11). Each app's engine has a hardening test module that proves:
· a failed edit leaves the document exactly as it was;
· random documents (a small built-in generator, no extra crate) never panic and keep their invariants;
· damaged files for every reader (cut short, garbled bytes, loops) never panic: they open or give a clear error;
· a speed gate on a large document (a looser limit in debug builds).
· trust in the results (from Datum Plan 0.3.12): hand-worked cases for each core rule, with the expected values worked out before running (cases.rs); parity files that carry their own results, checked value by value (tests/parity, where real exports from other tools can be dropped in); random-input checks of the rules themselves (for Plan: every link holds, no task starts later than its links need, row order does not matter), and random sequences of edits.
· hostile values (from Datum Plan 0.4.2): a battery that runs every engine function the window or a script can reach (exercise) on documents with deliberately impossible values (huge or negativ

nodes.label: §12 Starting a new Datum app (checklist)
nodes.text:
· Create the repo Edgar-Mendonca/Datum-<Name> (MIT).
· Copy the skeleton from Datum Plan:
· the workspace Cargo.toml, crates/core (empty engine), src-tauri (main, update.rs, tauri.conf);
· ui/ (index.html with the icon sprite, styles.css, store.ts, ui.tsx, help.tsx, ribbon/backstage/options/print/roadmap patterns);
· package.json, .github/workflows, tests_ui/run.cjs, CLAUDE.md, NOTICE, LICENSE.
· Rename: product name, identifier, file extension, REPO in update.rs, installer name in release.yml.
· Apply the accent set from §3 and draw the logo per §5; copy the icon into DATUM brand/.
· Write docs/MEMORY.md and docs/PLAN-0.1.md (brainstorm and questions) before building features.
· Release 0.1.0 (shell, updater, Home, one working view) so the updater works from day one.
· Add the hardening standard (§11): the hardening tests, deny.toml, the Windows/macOS CI jobs, SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.
· Publish docs/site.json (§10) and add one line to DATUM's apps.json; the site picks the app up on its next build.

nodes.label: §13 Principles and public words
nodes.text:
Datum: free, open-source desktop tools for engineers, scientists, researchers and analysts. Small, fast apps that do serious technical work, written from scratch in Rust, with one look and one way of working. No accounts, no subscriptions, no telemetry: your files stay on your computer.
· Small and fast. Quick to install; opens in a moment; smooth with large files.
· Private. Files stay on the user's computer. The only network call is the update check.
· Built for real technical work. Each app has its own engine in a pure Rust crate, with tests.
· One design. The same window, ribbon, help, printing and updater in every app (§5–9).
· Small releases. One release is one small numbered version, shown in the in-app updater.
· Written down. Docs and memory are kept in every repo (§10).
· Free forever. MIT licence.
Rules for all public text (README, site, release notes, CHANGELOG):
· Describe what each app does and who it helps. Never name or compare with commercial products, and never say an app copies, clones or replaces one. Every Datum app has its own engine and its own design. (The family site leaves out any CHANGELOG or site.json line that names one, and lists it in the build log.)
· Say "free and open source (MIT)", "Windows first", "installs in seconds", "updates itself".
· Write plainly: short sentences, active verbs, no marketing filler. A visitor should know in ten seconds what each app is for.

nodes.label: A guide per app, per language, downloaded on demand (FAMILY…
nodes.text:
A guide per app, per language, downloaded on demand (FAMILY §10): Markdown in docs/guide/<lang>.md with numbered screenshots, built to PDF (scripts/guide.cjs), attached to every release as Datum<App>-Guide-<lang>.pdf (in SHA256SUMS.txt), and fetched by Help › Guide (verify, save to Downloads, open). Translations keep the English UI names in bold with the meaning beside them

Why: Datum Plan 0.4.4: users (some Chinese-speaking) needed a guide; the installer stays small and the guide always matches the version.

nodes.label: Spreadsheets inside an app read the app's data by name…
nodes.text:
Spreadsheets inside an app read the app's data by name: GridCraft tables (Tasks[Finish]) and workbook names (ProjectFinish), with Excel habits (click cells into formulas, suggestions, fill/paste moving references, insert/delete rows) taken from GridCraft rather than re-written; country flags are a cell format drawn from bundled SVGs (flag-icons, MIT), never emoji

Why: Datum Plan 0.5.0: users built client dashboards in Excel by copying values; Windows does not draw flag emoji.

nodes.label: Charts: Chart.js, in the style of its own samples (smooth…
nodes.text:
Charts: Chart.js, in the style of its own samples (smooth monotone lines, faded fill under actuals, rounded bars, light horizontal grid only, round legend markers, dark rounded tooltip); every chart resizes with its box and before printing; empty charts say so. Plotly only where an app needs scientific plots (Datum Plot)

Why: Datum Plan 0.5.2: the user found the old charts plain and saw them cropped in PDFs.

nodes.label: FAMILY.md moves to DATUM and becomes the source of truth…
nodes.text:
FAMILY.md moves to DATUM and becomes the source of truth; section numbers 1–12 are kept so "FAMILY §3" means the same everywhere; §13 "Principles and public words" added

Why: The brief. App repos keep a short docs/FAMILY.md that links here.

nodes.label: Commercial product names removed from FAMILY.md ("What it…
nodes.text:
Commercial product names removed from FAMILY.md ("What it replaces" column → "What it is for"; ribbon, sidebar, chart style and grid wording made neutral)

Why: The user's rule: never name, compare with, or say we copy any commercial product.

nodes.label: The site leaves out any CHANGELOG, highlight or roadmap line…
nodes.text:
The site leaves out any CHANGELOG, highlight or roadmap line that names another product (NAMES in github.ts) and lists it in the build log

Why: The apps' older CHANGELOG sections still compare with other tools; the public site must not, whatever the app repos say. File formats and interoperability words (Excel, Word, CSV) are not filtered.

nodes.label: Base path /Datum (the repo's real name), not /DATUM as in the…
nodes.text:
Base path /Datum (the repo's real name), not /DATUM as in the brief

Why: Pages URLs follow the repository name.

nodes.label: Astro 7.3.8 (Node ≥ 22.12) and marked 18.1.1; Node 22 in Actions
nodes.text:
Astro 7.3.8 (Node ≥ 22.12) and marked 18.1.1; Node 22 in Actions

Why: Current versions; marked 18.0.x has a DoS advisory.

nodes.label: apps.json branch HEAD (default branch) instead of naming…
nodes.text:
apps.json branch HEAD (default branch) instead of naming branches

Why: The app repos' default branches are claude/* working branches that may change.

nodes.label: Pages workflow runs on every push but deploys only from the…
nodes.text:
Pages workflow runs on every push but deploys only from the default branch (if: on the job)

Why: The repo has no main; this keeps working if the default branch changes.

nodes.label: Text and filled buttons use an --ink token: the accent, or a…
nodes.text:
Text and filled buttons use an --ink token: the accent, or a darker shade where white on it is below 4.5:1 (Plot's teal → #0B7468)

Why: WCAG AA contrast.

nodes.label: Family mark brand/datum-icon.svg: grey-tint tile, navy "D"…
nodes.text:
Family mark brand/datum-icon.svg: grey-tint tile, navy "D" with blue, teal and violet dots, amber diamond

Why: The brief (§1).

nodes.label: The site is one landing page plus the Datum network; the app…
nodes.text:
The site is one landing page plus the Datum network; the app, family and about pages are gone

Why: The user: the site is only for people to see the apps and download them; memory, roadmap and design stay in the repo.

nodes.label: Look taken from the user's zhuojia site (paper-and-ink grid…
nodes.text:
Look taken from the user's zhuojia site (paper-and-ink grid, framed column, numbered bars, wide display type, serif italic accent, mono labels), but its own quiet header (mark, word, three links, theme) and a datum drawing instead of the orbit

Why: The user asked for that layout and style, not a copy, and did not like the reference headers. Artcraft could not be opened from the build sandbox.

nodes.label: The logo is the user's own design, "Continuum": two concentric…
nodes.text:
The logo is the user's own design, "Continuum": two concentric D's as one line, amber datum square where it starts, with a geometric DATUM wordmark. Refined only in geometry (one centre, true arcs, even 16 gap, optical letter spacing); guide in brand/BRAND.md, generator in brand/source/build-logo.py

Why: The user designed it and asked us to improve on it, not replace it; no app colours in the brand.

nodes.label: The site is simple and technical: IBM Plex Sans and Mono only…
nodes.text:
The site is simple and technical: IBM Plex Sans and Mono only (Archivo and Instrument Serif removed), no giant display words, no floating tiles or orbit rings, no repeated "free · open source · Windows" slogans

Why: The user: the site looked artistic and too close to the reference sites; it must look professional and attract engineers and scientists.

nodes.label: Datum Sim joins the family: in apps.json, icon in brand/…
nodes.text:
Datum Sim joins the family: in apps.json, icon in brand/, orange #C2410C added to FAMILY §1 and §3; the hero's "Reports" tile becomes Sim's "Control loop"; the network places any number of apps round the hub (anchors and lanes from apps.json)

Why: Requested from the Datum Sim chat after its 0.1.0 release (the user pasted it here).

nodes.label: Datum Sim is the next app (system simulation and control…
nodes.text:
Datum Sim is the next app (system simulation and control design), ahead of Datum Calc; Datum Field is the name for the future FEA/CFD/multiphysics app, parked

Why: The user: two big apps in the long run; Sim first. "Sim" now means system simulation; FEA is Field.

nodes.label: Briefs for new apps live in the hub's briefs/ (DATUM-SIM.md…
nodes.text:
Briefs for new apps live in the hub's briefs/ (DATUM-SIM.md, DATUM-FIELD.md) and are pasted into the new app's chat

Why: The hub is the memory every new app starts from.

nodes.label: pages.yml waits for GitHub's branch-based Pages build of the…
nodes.text:
pages.yml waits for GitHub's branch-based Pages build of the same commit, then deploys

Why: While the Pages source is "Deploy from a branch", that build publishes the raw repo and caused a 404 whenever it finished last.

nodes.label: Bench tiles are real capabilities of the apps (Plan: schedule…
nodes.text:
Bench tiles are real capabilities of the apps (Plan: schedule, progress; Plot: curve fit, statistics; Atlas: property chart, ranking; reports; more to come), not disciplines; the left side gets app chips from apps.json

Why: The user: the hero did not define our work; never say "3 apps".

nodes.label: The changing blue words use Instrument Serif italic (.it)…
nodes.text:
The changing blue words use Instrument Serif italic (.it), everything else stays IBM Plex

Why: The user preferred that font for the changing text (session 3).

nodes.label: Artcraft-like scrolling: glass sticky section bars, an index…
nodes.text:
Artcraft-like scrolling: glass sticky section bars, an index by the ruler with a scroll %, heading words coming into focus and cards rising (CSS scroll timelines, no library)

Why: The user's Artcraft screenshots and answer 5.

nodes.label: Theme: three visible buttons (Auto, Light, Dark) instead of a…
nodes.text:
Theme: three visible buttons (Auto, Light, Dark) instead of a cycling button

Why: The user wanted all three; a cycle looked broken (Auto → Light changes nothing on a light system).

nodes.label: Status badges (Stable / Beta / Alpha) from apps.json status or…
nodes.text:
Status badges (Stable / Beta / Alpha) from apps.json status or the version; figures strip, "Get started" and the network teaser removed; latest releases = one per app; the network page has no visible title

Why: The user's answers and list.

nodes.label: The workbench hero (HeroWorkbench.astro, replaces…
nodes.text:
The workbench hero (HeroWorkbench.astro, replaces HeroPanel.astro): left "Datum" + "Tools to <blue phrase>"; right a 3×3 bench of small SVG instruments (Plan, Engineering, Plot, Analysis, Science, Atlas, Research, More to come) around the datum origin (amber square, dial, needle). The active tile animates, the needle turns to it and the phrase changes; hover/focus/tap takes over, app tiles open their app, idle it cycles every 3.2 s; a pointer-following inspection light; a small script (the rule now allows JS for the hero)

Why: The user: the instrument panel was slow, could not be clicked and looked empty mid-fade; they liked the rotating "Tools to …" line and the small animated icons of session 3, but not floating around the title as on the reference sites.

nodes.label: Two-panel hero (HeroPanel.astro): "Datum" with the amber…
nodes.text:
Two-panel hero (HeroPanel.astro): "Datum" with the amber square, one lead line, and a write-up that cycles Plan → Plot → Atlas → More to come, beside an instrument panel with one animated technical scene per item (schedule with critical path, fitted curve with band and readout, property chart with selection line, a drawing being drafted); one CSS clock keeps text and scene in step; hover pauses

Why: The user's layout: writing on the left, animated icons on the right, the text changing with what is shown.

nodes.label: Family mark replaced by a "D" that is a protractor (ruler…
nodes.text:
Family mark replaced by a "D" that is a protractor (ruler stem, graduated bowl, needle from the amber datum origin), navy ink only

Why: The user: no app colours in the logo (more apps will come); a generalized, unique, vector-style symbolic D.

nodes.label: The hero is a field of animated SVG tiles around the wordmark…
nodes.text:
The hero is a field of animated SVG tiles around the wordmark: one per app (links to it), five for the kinds of work (engineering, computation, analysis, science, research) and two "more to come"; orbit rings with moving dots; a rotating "Tools to …" line; CSS/SMIL only, a scrolling strip on phones, still under reduced motion

Why: The user asked for illustrations placed around the header like the reference site, small animations, room for more apps, and not the same as before.

nodes.label: New family mark: the GD&T datum feature symbol (framed "D"…
nodes.text:
New family mark: the GD&T datum feature symbol (framed "D", leader, datum triangle) on a reference line of the three app accents, amber diamond beside the frame

Why: The user was not satisfied with the "D with dots"; a datum symbol says what the name means.

nodes.label: The brain: brain/brain.mjs builds one graph (nodes: hub, apps…
nodes.text:
The brain: brain/brain.mjs builds one graph (nodes: hub, apps, FAMILY sections, technologies, workflow, decisions, files, releases, plans, sessions) from the repos; brain/graph.json is committed; the site draws it

Why: The user wants a complete, interactive map of the whole portfolio, and one file Claude reads in every new project so nothing is lost.

nodes.label: The public network removes sentences that name other products…
nodes.text:
The public network removes sentences that name other products and leaves out nodes whose title does; graph.json keeps everything

Why: FAMILY §13 for the site; the memory itself must stay complete.

nodes.label: Fonts self-hosted with @fontsource (Archivo with the width…
nodes.text:
Fonts self-hosted with @fontsource (Archivo with the width axis, IBM Plex Sans and Mono, Instrument Serif); screenshots converted to 1440 px WebP at build with sharp

Why: No third-party requests; smaller pages.

nodes.label: Safety rules for every app's shell and hostile values join the…
nodes.text:
Safety rules for every app's shell and hostile values join the hardening standard (FAMILY §11): unwind + guard + crash.log, atomic saves and read limits, an updater that requires checksums, the CSP baseline, CSV formula guard, npm audit; a battery that runs every engine function on impossible values

Why: Datum Plan 0.4.2's audit found real faults with these: release builds aborted on any panic, the updater installed unverified when a release had no checksum file, calendar arithmetic panicked on huge spans, century-long plans froze the S-curve, and the CSP silently blocked progress-report photos.

nodes.label: Apps may ship a command line and an MCP server for AI…
nodes.text:
Apps may ship a command line and an MCP server for AI assistants, changing documents only through the engine's named operations and saving only when asked (Datum Plan's datum-cli)

Why: One way to change a document; safe for scripts and assistants.

nodes.label: In SolidJS, a <select> whose options load later marks <option…
nodes.text:
In SolidJS, a <select> whose options load later marks <option selected> rather than setting value on the select (it showed the first option)

Why: Found in Datum Plan 0.4.1; applies to every app's window (FAMILY §7).

nodes.label: Every import is a parity check: an app that opens files…
nodes.text:
Every import is a parity check: an app that opens files carrying their own results (dates, values) recomputes them and lists the differences in an import report, alongside what it changed or left out

Why: Datum Plan 0.4.0; it reuses the parity-test code, so users see the same check the tests run.

nodes.label: Trust in the results joins the hardening standard (FAMILY…
nodes.text:
Trust in the results joins the hardening standard (FAMILY §11): hand-worked cases for the engine's core rules (expected values worked out before running), parity files that carry their own results (drop in real exports from other tools), and random-input checks of the rules themselves, not only "no panic"

Why: Datum Plan 0.3.12: the hand-worked cases and the random link check found two real scheduling mistakes (ALAP used total float; late dates of work under way used the whole duration).

nodes.label: Hardening standard for every app (FAMILY §11): hardening tests…
nodes.text:
Hardening standard for every app (FAMILY §11): hardening tests (failed edits change nothing, random documents, damaged files, speed gate), cargo deny, CI on Windows + macOS, poisoned-lock recovery, SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. First shipped in Datum Plan 0.3.11; rustfmt is not enforced

Why: A quick look at another open-source scheduler showed our apps lead on features but trail on rigour (tests, CI gates). In Plan the new tests found two real crashes on damaged P6 files on their first run.

nodes.label: Datum Plot's bundled Python is recorded in FAMILY §2 as the…
nodes.text:
Datum Plot's bundled Python is recorded in FAMILY §2 as the one exception to "no Python"

Why: Plot's own decision (its MEMORY, session 1); the guide must not contradict a shipped app.

nodes.label: Hero = four app tiles (Hero.astro + AppGlyph.astro: Gantt…
nodes.text:
Hero = four app tiles (Hero.astro + AppGlyph.astro: Gantt, curve fit, property chart, control loop, looping gently) around the amber datum square, replacing the 3×3 workbench; the italic phrase cycles by itself (two phrases per app), hover holds, leaving resumes. One page per app (/apps/<id>); about and steps added to the site.json spec (FAMILY §10), with fallbacks in apps.json

Why: The user: the bench was too much; four animated icons for the current apps are enough; each app needs a page that explains the software.

nodes.label: Datum Home, a desktop app in this repo (home/) that installs…
nodes.text:
Datum Home, a desktop app in this repo (home/) that installs, updates, opens and removes every Datum app; checks only when opened; the site offers it and each app on its own. List from the site's home.json, versions from each app's GitHub releases, installed apps from HKCU Uninstall; installs only installers from the app's own releases that match SHA256SUMS.txt; uninstall keeps the user's files; updates itself from home-v* releases

Why: The user: one place to install and update all the apps, without forcing it on people who want one app. Kept in the hub so the family's own tools live together; the release shape it relies on is in FAMILY §9.

nodes.label: Datum Calc and Datum Mesh are built this week for a large…
nodes.text:
Datum Calc and Datum Mesh are built this week for a large engineering convention. "Datum Field" is renamed Datum Mesh (clear to every engineer; covers stress, heat and later flow). Accents: Calc = Amber #A8650F, Mesh = Crimson #B83250 (the two spares). Mesh 0.1 is 2D only (frames, trusses, plane stress/strain, heat) with an own solver and a verification report; 3D/CFD later with open solvers as separate programs. Briefs pre-answer every question so the app chats build at once

Why: The user: Calc and Mesh fit their work best (process, rotating equipment, mechanical, project controls, inferred from the apps' worked examples); the convention needs both this week.

nodes.label: Datum Pipe (pipe stress analysis) is the next app, built in…
nodes.text:
Datum Pipe (pipe stress analysis) is the next app, built in one overnight run from briefs/DATUM-PIPE.md; accent Moss #4D7C0F (new, FAMILY §3). Codes: implement published equations only, allowables are user inputs pre-filled with typical values; never claim certification. Commercial piping software is never named anywhere (repo, briefs, memory, site), at the user's explicit request

Why: Session 15 research found no open-source pipe stress tool; the user has used the commercial ones for years and finds them expensive and hard to use.

nodes.label: No shared code kit for now: every app stays self-contained.…
nodes.text:
No shared code kit for now: every app stays self-contained. Shared pieces (shell, ribbon, File page, updater, printing, styles, icon set, units engine, solver parts) keep being copied from the reference app, never linked. When a shared piece is fixed or improved in one app, that app's chat records it in this hub (FAMILY or MEMORY), and the user passes it to the other apps' chats. Reference copies: shell, updater, print, icons → Datum Plan; units → Datum Calc; frame/sparse solver → Datum Mesh; Python runtime → Datum Plot

Why: The user: a shared kit could break every app at once; separate apps are safer. Revisit only if drift becomes a real cost. The graph stays the map of what exists where.

nodes.label: Datum Home reads releases from the site, not GitHub. home.json…
nodes.text:
Datum Home reads releases from the site, not GitHub. home.json (written by the hourly site build, which has a token) carries each app's newest release with installer, checksum list and notes, and Datum Home's own (home). Home calls the GitHub API only for an app the site does not cover, or for its own update if the site has none

Why: Users saw "GitHub is busy (rate limit)": unauthenticated API calls are limited to about 60 an hour per network, and Home made one per app plus one for itself on every open. A release now reaches Home within the hour (or at once: run Pages).

nodes.label: The Windows publisher of every app is "Datum"…
nodes.text:
The Windows publisher of every app is "Datum" (bundle.publisher in tauri.conf.json), not the author's name; the copyright line keeps the author ("© 2026 Edgar Mendonca"), who holds it. Datum Home accepts both publisher names, so apps installed earlier are still recognised

Why: The user: Settings › Apps showed their name for every app; it should show the brand. Home went first (0.1.4) so no app is ever missed during the switch.

nodes.label: Datum Schema (intelligent P&IDs and process flow diagrams) is…
nodes.text:
Datum Schema (intelligent P&IDs and process flow diagrams) is the eighth app, for the exhibition; name chosen over "Datum P&ID" (the & breaks file and repo names; "PID" means the controller in Sim; P&ID is narrower than the app) and "Flowsheet"; tagline names P&IDs. Accent Magenta #9C1F84 (FAMILY §3). Bench (DAQ) waits: it depends on hardware and is too risky for a one-day build

Why: Session 15 research: no open-source P&ID tool with proper symbols; an open P&ID data standard (DEXPI) exists with no free desktop app. Schema's edge over a drawing: data, connectivity, checks, lists and hydraulics, plus links to Pipe and Sim.

nodes.label: Datum Schema aims at the enterprise class of plant engineering…
nodes.text:
Datum Schema aims at the enterprise class of plant engineering tools (object-based, plant hierarchy, class library, many disciplines and users), not at drawing tools. From 0.1: objects are the master and symbols are views; plant hierarchy; class library as data; the project is one SQLite file with a change history; names follow DEXPI. Roadmap 0.2–0.7 adds DEXPI, datasheets, PFD stream tables, revisions, instrumentation, multi-user, electrical (brief addendum)

Why: The user has used the enterprise tools (one object-based one especially) and wants that class; the core must be object-based now or it would need rebuilding later. Sent to the running Schema chat as a course correction.

nodes.label: Session 1 (the hub)
nodes.text:
· Read the brief, FAMILY.md, and each app's README and MEMORY (read-only clones of Plan, Plot, Atlas).
· Wrote README, FAMILY.md (neutral wording, §13 principles, site.json spec in §10, step 7 of the new-app checklist), MEMORY.md, apps.json, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE; copied the three app icons into brand/ and drew datum-icon.svg.
· Built the Astro site and pages.yml. Checked locally (no token: the release API is unavailable in the build sandbox, so the CHANGELOG fallback was used) with Playwright at 1280 and 375 px, light and dark: no horizontal overflow; fixed the family page's overflow at 375 px and the theme button label.
· Found: Plan's CHANGELOG lost its ## 0.3.7 … ## 0.3.3 headings (they read 2026-10-24), so the site jumps from 0.3.8 to 0.3.2. Plan's 0.3.6 and Plot's 0.1.0 sections name other products (left out by the filter).
· Plot and Atlas have no docs/site.json yet: gave the user a snippet for each.

nodes.label: Session 2 (landing page, network, logo)
nodes.text:
· User: the Pages build failed with Jekyll YAML errors (the Pages source was "Deploy from a branch", so GitHub ran Jekyll over the .astro files; our own Actions build had passed but could not deploy because Pages was not set to GitHub Actions). Added .nojekyll; the fix is Settings › Pages › Source = GitHub Actions.
· User: not happy with the design or the logo; wants the zhuojia look (not a copy, not its header), a one-page landing site with downloads, everything else kept in the repo as the brain, and an interactive "neural network" map of the whole portfolio that Claude can use in every project.
· Built: brain/brain.mjs + graph.json + BRAIN.md (336 nodes, 575 edges); the landing page; the network page (Network and Flow layouts, search, filters, details, pulses); the datum-symbol logo (brand/datum-icon.svg, brand/datum-mark.svg). Removed the app, family and about pages.
· Checked: build without a token; Playwright at 1280 and 375 px, light and dark, no overflow, no console errors; every image loads; network search (help.tsx), selection panel, Flow layout and mobile checked by screenshot.

nodes.label: Session 3 (logo and hero)
nodes.text:
· User: the logo's three app colours do not scale to more apps; wants a generalized, unique, vector-style symbolic D, used everywhere. And a new page header: illustrations placed around it as on the reference site, some text, small animations, not the same as before.
· Built: the protractor D (brand/datum-icon.svg, brand/datum-mark.svg, Mark.astro, favicon); site/src/components/HeroField.astro (10 tiles: Plan Gantt with growing bars, caliper with a sliding jaw, scrolling signal, Plot curve drawing itself, gears, Atlas bubbles with a marching selection line, flask with rising bubbles, turning molecule, two dashed "more to come"); rotating headline; the header strip now says "3 apps · more to come".
· Checked: build; Playwright at 1280, 1440 (dark) and 375 px: no overflow, no console errors, tiles clear of the wordmark; the phone strip scrolls.

nodes.label: Session 4 (the user's logo, a simple technical…
nodes.text:
· User: sent their own logo ("Continuum", brand/source/datum-continuum-original.svg) and asked to improve on it and use it everywhere; more branding guidance to follow. The hero must be simple: two panels, writing on the left (big "Datum", a write-up that changes with the animation), animated icons on the right; no "free · open source · Windows" line; professional and techy, not artistic, not like the reference sites. Reminded that this repo is the hub memory every new app plugs into.
· Built: brand/ (logo, light logo, mark, light mark, icon, BRAND.md, generator); Mark.astro and Logo.astro; header and footer use the logo; HeroPanel.astro replaces HeroField.astro; site type is IBM Plex only; figures strip under the hero; app names, releases and the closing section in plain headings; screenshots flat.
· Checked: build; Playwright at 1280 (light), 1440 (dark) and 375 px at several points of the cycle (Plan, Plot, Atlas, Next): no overflow, no console errors.

nodes.label: Session 5 (the workbench hero)
nodes.text:
· User: the instrument panel loaded slowly, could not be clicked, and looked empty while fading; bring back the rotating blue "Tools to …" line and the small animated icons, but in the right pane, playable, not like the reference sites. Logo and the rest unchanged. Asked to look at other sites for ideas: a web search turned up hover-reactive grids, cursor spotlights and tiles linked to text (Framer / 21st.dev components), used as ideas only.
· Built: HeroWorkbench.astro (tiles reuse the session 3 drawings; animations run only on the active tile; the origin dial's needle points at it; the phrase swaps with a short slide); HeroPanel.astro removed; CLAUDE.md hero rule updated.
· Checked: build; Playwright: the bench cycles idle, hover on Science takes over ("run experiments."), holds while hovered, resumes after; 1280, 1440 (dark), 375 px: no overflow, no console errors.

nodes.label: Session 17 (from Datum Plan's chat: 0.4.2…
nodes.text:
· Plan 0.4.2: a full security and robustness pass (see decisions), datum-cli with an MCP server and a catalogue of named operations, costs exact to the cent, and Schedule Risk / Look-ahead / Manpower printing as themselves (they printed the Dashboard). Its roadmap's next stage is 0.5 (schedule quality and scenarios).
· Recorded here: FAMILY §11 (hostile values, safety rules for every shell), two decisions, Plan at 0.4.2. Other apps should adopt the new safety rules in their own chats. Brain regenerated.

nodes.label: Session 15 (from Datum Plan's chat: 0.4.1…
nodes.text:
· Plan 0.4.1 shipped actual S-curves through the stored periods, earned schedule (SPI(t), finish at this pace), Manpower by trade (planned / done / forecast), rules of credit and installed quantities, and a look-ahead with a constraint log. Its roadmap's next stage is 0.4.2 (command line and automation).
· Recorded here: Plan at 0.4.1, the <select> rule (§3 and FAMILY §7). Brain regenerated.

nodes.label: Session 26 (from Datum Plan's chat: 0.5.0…
nodes.text: · Plan 0.5.0: Sheets work like Excel (point-and-click formulas, 490 functions suggested, AutoSum, fill and paste with formulas, rows and columns) and read the plan live through Tasks/Resources tables and names; Plan Data lists; country flags and a resource Country. Then 0.5.1 fixed a scroll echo between the task sheet and the chart (felt stuck) and the Tell Me overlay hiding the window (a class name colliding with the title bar's). 0.5.2 restyled every chart (still Chart.js: smooth lines, faded fills, rounded bars, light grid, dark tooltip) and stopped charts being cropped (resize with their box and for printing). Next in Plan: 0.5.3 custom dashboards. Recorded the decision and the FAMILY note; brain regenerated.

nodes.label: Session 25 (from Datum Plan's chat: 0.4.4, the…
nodes.text: · Plan 0.4.4 shipped the Datum Plan Guide in English and Simplified Chinese (about 30 pages each, numbered screenshots), downloaded from the release by Help › Guide; 0.4.3 had changed the Windows publisher to "Datum". Recorded the guide pattern (decision, FAMILY §10) and Plan at 0.4.4. Brain regenerated.

nodes.label: Session 24 (Datum Schema joins the family…
nodes.text:
· Datum Schema released 0.1.3 (site.json, icon, SHA256SUMS, publisher "Datum").
· Hub: apps.json (schema #9C1F84), brand icon, --schema (#9C1F84 / dark #E07BC9), AppGlyph "schema" (a vessel, a process line with a valve and flow arrow to a pump, an LIC bubble with dashed signal lines, a "0 errors" badge; classes g-vessel, g-procline, g-bowtie, g-pumpc, g-pumpt, g-sig, g-bubble), phrases "draw P&IDs. / check the plant.", lead mentions intelligent P&IDs. The 3×3 hero is now full (eight apps around the Datum mark; no "More to come"); a ninth app needs a new layout (4 columns, or a 4×3 bench). FAMILY §1, README, CLAUDE.md, MEMORY §1.
· Datum Home 0.1.5: Schema in its built-in list with its icon; released.
· Checked: site build, Playwright 1280/375 (home, Schema page, network): no overflow; Schema drawing light and dark; Home core tests, clippy, UI.

nodes.label: Session 23 (Schema's direction: enterprise…
nodes.text:
· User (Schema chat already running) asked which tools exist and said the target is the enterprise class, not drawing tools. Listed the market in chat only (no names in files): enterprise object-based suites, mid-range P&ID tools, general diagramming. Explained what makes the enterprise class (object as master, plant hierarchy, class library, many disciplines, many users, open exchange) and where 0.1 stands.
· Gave the user a course correction for the running Schema chat (objects master, hierarchy, class library, SQLite project with history, DEXPI naming) and appended it to briefs/DATUM-SCHEMA.md with an enterprise roadmap (0.2–0.7). Decision recorded.

nodes.label: Session 22 (Datum Schema brief)
nodes.text:
· User needs an eighth app for next week's exhibition; asked Bench vs P&ID, and what a P&ID app adds over plain CAD. Research: intelligent P&IDs carry data per item (automatic line/equipment/instrument/valve lists, integrity checks) and only expensive plant suites do it; the open DEXPI standard (OPC 30250) has an open Python model (pyDEXPI) but no free desktop app. Recommended the P&ID app (visual, links Pipe, Sim and Calc) over Bench (hardware risk).
· Name: Datum Schema (user's choice). Copyright question answered (keep "© Edgar Mendonca": MIT needs an owner; Datum is a brand, not a legal entity).
· Wrote briefs/DATUM-SCHEMA.md: decisions up front (magenta accent, .dschema, publisher "Datum", layout, own symbols following ISO 10628-2 / ISA-5.1), ~80 symbols, data on everything, 13 live checks, line hydraulics, four lists, PDF/SVG/DXF, three examples + "Find the faults", tests, a 7-step day plan (0.1.0 → 0.1.4), cut order, roadmap (DEXPI, send to Pipe/Sim, PFD stream tables, loop diagrams). FAMILY §3: Magenta. Bucket list: Flowsheet → Schema.
· Hub tasks when Schema releases: apps.json (schema #9C1F84; --schema #9C1F84 / dark #E07BC9), icon to brand/, AppGlyph "schema" (classes never g-schema!), phrases ("draw P&IDs.", "check the plant."), the hero then has eight tiles: the 3×3 bench is full (no "More to come"), FAMILY §1, README, Datum Home built-in list, brain.

nodes.label: Session 21 (publisher "Datum")
nodes.text:
· User (screenshot of Windows Settings › Apps): every Datum app lists "Edgar Mendonca" as publisher; wanted "Datum". The value is bundle.publisher in each app's tauri.conf.json.
· Datum Home 0.1.4: its own publisher "Datum"; core::PUBLISHERS = ["Datum", "Edgar Mendonca"] so installs from both eras are found (test added). FAMILY §9 says the publisher is "Datum". Gave the user paste-in text for the seven app chats (change publisher, keep copyright, release).
· Note for code signing later: the signing certificate names its legal owner; Windows then shows that name in security prompts, separately from this field.

nodes.label: Session 20 (Datum Home: no more rate-limit…
nodes.text:
· User (screenshot): Datum Home showed "GitHub is busy (rate limit)" on every card. Cause: GitHub allows about 60 unauthenticated API calls an hour per network (shared by everyone behind one connection); Home made eight per open, and the apps' own updaters add more. The versions shown were still right (the site's copy).
· Fix (Home 0.1.3): core::installable, core::parse_home; catalog also returns the site's copy of Home's release; card skips GitHub when the site's release is installable; home_update(site) uses the site's copy first. Site: home.json gains home (Home's newest release with SHA256SUMS) and release notes per app (the CHANGELOG section as plain text). New core test site_copy_of_releases.
· Not changed: each app's own in-app updater still asks GitHub once at start (one call per app opened; fine in practice). If that ever shows the same message, the apps can read home.json too (paste-in text for their chats).
· Checked: core tests (10), clippy Linux and Windows target, UI check and build, site build with home.json.

nodes.label: Session 19 (brainstorm: the brain, AI and…
nodes.text:
· User: is the network a neural network that can be "trained" as Datum's brain, and could an AI assistant use it? Answer: brain/graph.json is a knowledge graph (facts and links, rebuilt hourly, exact, explainable), not a neural network; training our own model would be costly, imprecise and stale. The right pattern is retrieval: the graph and docs hold the facts, an existing language model reads and answers with citations. Ideas (not started): an "ask the brain" tool for the app chats; offline help search shared by the apps; later an opt-in assistant (local model or the user's own key), citing sources and never producing engineering numbers itself (results only from the tested engines). Privacy promise (no telemetry) rules out a default cloud assistant.
· User: is code and icon reuse real? Answer: decisions come from the hub, code is copied from the reference apps (not rewritten), the graph is the map. Proposed a shared kit (crates + UI package + one icon library in the hub); the user declined for now: separate apps are safer (decision above).

nodes.label: Session 18 (Datum Pipe joins the family)
nodes.text:
· Session 17 (brainstorm, no files): a data-acquisition, control and test app (the user used a graphical DAQ tool for control and ADC work). Recommended a separate app, "Datum Bench", not part of Sim: real-time I/O, drivers, logging, alarms and safety are a different engine from simulated time; share Sim's block canvas, scopes and Python; hardware in the loop joins them later. Hardware first: microcontroller boards over serial (with a small Datum firmware), Modbus RTU/TCP, bench instruments over USB/LAN, the sound card; front panel, logging, triggers, calibration, PID with interlocks; vibration analysis (the old "Signal" idea) as a module. After Pipe 0.1 and the 1.0s. Not yet in the bucket list (add it with the user's go-ahead).
· Session 18: Datum Pipe released 0.1.4 overnight from briefs/DATUM-PIPE.md (site.json, icon, SHA256SUMS in releases). Hub: apps.json (pipe #4D7C0F), brand icon, --pipe (#4D7C0F / dark #A3D65C), AppGlyph "pipe" (a pipe run with an expansion loop between anchors, guides, the deflected shape drawing itself in moss, the loop corners highlighted, "SE/SA 0.74"). Bug found and fixed: a class named g-pipe collided with the SVG's own g-<id> class and faded the whole drawing; glyph classes must never be g-<app id>.
· Hero for seven apps: a 3×3 bench: seven app tiles, the Datum mark in the centre cell and "More to come" in the last place (nine mode; up to six apps keep the earlier layouts; phones show two columns without the centre cell). Lead mentions pipe stress analysis. FAMILY §1, README (row, issue link, briefs line), CLAUDE.md (repos, hero rule), MEMORY §1 versions refreshed.
· Datum Home 0.1.2: Pipe in its built-in list with its icon; released with the workflow.
· Checked: site build (seven apps), Playwright 1280/375, light and dark (home, Pipe and Calc pages, network): no overflow; Pipe drawing still and animated; Home core tests, clippy, UI build.

nodes.label: Session 16 (Datum Pipe brief)
nodes.text:
· Session 15 (brainstorm, no files): researched where engineers, students and researchers lack free tools. Already covered by open source: process simulation, statistics and SPC, chromatography, load flow. Real gaps: pipe stress analysis (none), reliability GUI (Weibull, RBD, FMEA, RCM), P&ID with data, shell-and-tube thermal design, vibration/condition monitoring, DOE with a window, control valve sizing, pressure vessels (copyrighted codes), rotor dynamics GUI. Recommended Pipe, Reliability, Flowsheet, and more Calc packs; maturity (1.0s) before quantity.
· Session 16: the user chose Datum Pipe and asked for a brief for an overnight run: a 0.1 with many features that "looks like an app". Wrote briefs/DATUM-PIPE.md (no commercial names): element table + 3D view, pipe library, bends/tees/reducers/rigids, linear supports, three operating cases, automatic SUS/OPE/EXP/HYD cases, the process piping code equations, results on the model, support and nozzle loads, automatic isometric drawing, stress report, six examples, eight benchmarks; releases 0.1.0 → 0.1.4 in seven steps; cut order; roadmap 0.2–1.0. FAMILY §3: Moss accent for Pipe. Bucket list: Pipe, Reliability, Flowsheet.
· Hub tasks when Pipe releases (as for Calc and Mesh): apps.json (pipe #4D7C0F; site.css --pipe #4D7C0F / dark #A3D65C), icon to brand/, an AppGlyph drawing (a pipe run with an expansion loop growing, coloured by stress), phrases ("analyse piping.", "check pipe stresses."); the hero then has seven tiles: decide the layout (four columns, or 3×3 with a "more to come" tile and the datum square in the centre); FAMILY §1, README, Datum Home built-in list (next Home release), brain.

nodes.label: Session 14 (from Datum Plan's chat: 0.4.0…
nodes.text:
· Plan 0.4.0 shipped Schedule Risk (Monte Carlo: P50/P80/P90 finish and cost, criticality, drivers, risk-register delays, optimistic/pessimistic durations), workload by trade (resource Group) in hours or people, a levelling preview, and an import report that compares every task's dates with the file. Its docs/site.json now has a Schedule Risk screenshot third, so the app page shows it.
· Recorded here: decision (§3), FAMILY §7 chart rules (autoSkip: false on horizontal bars; <Index> for numbers), Plan at 0.4.0. Brain regenerated.

nodes.label: Session 14 (Calc and Mesh join the family)
nodes.text:
· Both apps were built in their own chats from the session 13 briefs: Calc 0.1.3 and Mesh 0.1.1, each with docs/site.json (about, steps), icons, and releases with SHA256SUMS.txt.

nodes.label: load.rs

nodes.label: check.rs

nodes.label: network.rs

nodes.label: parse.rs

nodes.label: doc.rs

bench.rs (20k-task timing), dump.rs (JSON fixtures for UI tests).

nodes.label: tests.rs
