nodes.text: Commands listed in the diagram; options (date format, autosave, beta, default currency, company, logo, workspace, setup panel); backups of format < 3 files; recovery.

nodes.label: update.rs
nodes.text: Updater; check(beta) reads /releases when beta is on; versions compare with pre-release tags.

nodes.label: index.html
nodes.text: Root and the icon sprite (about 65 icons). ui/public/logo.svg.

nodes.label: api.ts
nodes.text: Types matching the Rust JSON, invoke, date and money helpers.

nodes.label: store.ts
nodes.text: Global signals, built-in tables, query(), refresh(), act(), menus, dialogs, toast, theme (applyTheme, themeTick).

nodes.label: cmds.ts
nodes.text: Command functions C and the ALL_CMDS list for Tell Me.

nodes.label: ui.tsx
nodes.text: Icon, Menu (with submenus), Dialog (optional help key puts a ? in its header), Tabs, form helpers.

nodes.label: help.tsx
nodes.text: "?" help: the HELP table ({ t, what, how?, tip? } per topic), <Help k> (the small ? button, .help), helpCard(k) (the card dialog, .helpcard). Ribbon groups take h= on G, pages help= on Page/Tools. Help › What Is This Tool? lists every topic.

nodes.label: grid.tsx
nodes.text: Excel-like task sheet: one scroller with sticky header and frozen ID/name, ranges (ranges signal), fill handle, TSV clipboard via copy/paste events, Cells op for range edits, AutoFilter menus, header rename (Title op), FormulaBar.

nodes.label: charts.tsx
nodes.text: Chart.js wrapper used by every chart: modern style (smooth lines, faded fill, rounded bars, light grid), status pill, hover line, resize with box and for print, empty-data text, PNG save.

nodes.label: sheets.tsx
nodes.text: Sheet tabs, Excel-like: point-and-click references with coloured boxes, suggestions + argument hints, AutoSum, fill/paste moving formulas (formula_shift), insert/delete rows/cols (SheetInsert), number formats, column widths, error tips, flag cells.

nodes.label: formulas.ts
nodes.text: Pure formula-text helpers for the editor: refs, canPoint, suggest, callAt/sigArgs, cycleAnchor (F4), ERRORS.

nodes.label: sheetdlg.tsx
nodes.text: Insert Function (search, categories) and Plan Data (live FILTER/SORT/CHOOSECOLS list of Tasks or Resources).

nodes.label: flags.tsx
nodes.text: Country flags (flag-icons SVGs, MIT, lazy assets): countryCode (code/name/alias), Flag, FlagText, CountryList.

nodes.label: print.tsx
nodes.text: File › Print (every view; pkind() = gantt / net / cal / table / flow; Frame draws paper + header/footer/legend; vdata/vpages/ViewPage for network tiles, calendar months and tables; FlowDoc prints report pages in a table whose thead/tfoot repeat, with page numbers from @page margin boxes): PageSetup (saved in project.ui.page), layout() makes one strip (table columns + chart) and cuts it into page windows (across then down), Strip draws a window, Sheet draws one page as SVG (table + Gantt + legend) with header/footer codes and logos; printNow renders #printroot and sets @page size, then window.print(). PAPERS.

nodes.label: roadmap.tsx
nodes.text: File › Roadmap: the ROADMAP list (keep it in step with the roadmap table and "Pending and next" in this file).

nodes.label: selection.ts
nodes.text: The grid engine's selection, shared by the task sheet and Sheets: createSel (ranges, active cell, pick/drag/rows/cols/all/each), aggregate (Sum/Average/Count).

nodes.label: cells.ts
nodes.text: Shared by both grids: parseTsv/toTsv/transpose, series (Excel fill rules), clip (last copy: values + styles for Paste Special).

nodes.label: fmt.ts
nodes.text: Text formatting: style strings b;i;u;s;c:#hex;f:#hex;z:12;a:c, css(), the focused grid registers a Target (get/set selected cells), toggle/setProp/clear, Format Painter.

nodes.label: tools.tsx
nodes.text: Update Progress page, Relationship Diagram (SVG), Report Builder (sections, TEMPLATES, saved in ui.reports).

nodes.label: run.cjs
nodes.text: Playwright UI tests against the built UI with a mocked shell and dump fixture (alignment, ranges, menus, ribbon, sidebar, every view). Runs in CI.

nodes.label: gantt.tsx
nodes.text: As in the diagram. styles.css holds the light theme and print styles.

nodes.label: Name Datum Plan, file extension .dplan
nodes.text:
Name Datum Plan, file extension .dplan

Why: The user chose it.

nodes.label: Rust engine in crates/core; Cairn is only a reference
nodes.text:
Rust engine in crates/core; Cairn is only a reference

Why: The user wants everything in Rust for a small, robust app.

nodes.label: UI in plain TypeScript with no framework, split into 7 script…
nodes.text:
UI in plain TypeScript with no framework, split into 7 script files joined by tsc

Why: Small bundle; modules without a bundler.

nodes.label: Custom updater (GitHub API + SHA-256 + NSIS /S); per-user…
nodes.text:
Custom updater (GitHub API + SHA-256 + NSIS /S); per-user install

Why: Needs no signing secrets; silent updates.

nodes.label: Windows only; no .mpp (closed format)
nodes.text:
Windows only; no .mpp (closed format)

Why: The user's choice. Exchange formats are dplan, XML, XER, XLSX and CSV.

nodes.label: Light theme, new logo, Cairn-style sidebar, general templates
nodes.text:
Light theme, new logo, Cairn-style sidebar, general templates

Why: The user's feedback on 0.1.0.

nodes.label: Minute-precision engine with real calendars (replacing whole…
nodes.text:
Minute-precision engine with real calendars (replacing whole days)

Why: Needed for hours, shifts, holidays and P6/MSP exchange. Old files migrate (day × 480).

nodes.label: Several roadmap steps shipped as one release (0.1.2–0.1.4…
nodes.text:
Several roadmap steps shipped as one release (0.1.2–0.1.4, calendars, constraints, logic, exchange, resources, baselines/progress)

Why: The user asked for all of it in 0.2.

nodes.label: Links on summaries apply to every leaf under them; links to…
nodes.text:
Links on summaries apply to every leaf under them; links to one's own summary are dropped

Why: Simple and close to MSP. P6 has no summary links anyway.

nodes.label: Status date semantics: progress up to the end of that day…
nodes.text:
Status date semantics: progress up to the end of that day; remaining work starts the next day

Why: MSP-like status date. XER last_recalc_date maps to status = data date − 1.

nodes.label: Work-resource units: 50%, 0.5 or 50; material: quantity; cost…
nodes.text:
Work-resource units: 50%, 0.5 or 50; material: quantity; cost: amount

Why: Matches MSP habits.

nodes.label: Predecessor IDs typed with new rows (quick add, paste) mean…
nodes.text:
Predecessor IDs typed with new rows (quick add, paste) mean the IDs shown before the insert

Why: What the user sees on screen.

nodes.label: XML reader written by hand instead of quick-xml
nodes.text:
XML reader written by hand instead of quick-xml

Why: The quick-xml API changes a lot between versions; MSPDI only needs elements and text.

nodes.label: Recovery copy in AppData, not autosave over the user's file
nodes.text:
Recovery copy in AppData, not autosave over the user's file

Why: Safe: never overwrites a file without asking.

nodes.label: SolidJS + Vite for the UI (not Astro)
nodes.text:
SolidJS + Vite for the UI (not Astro)

Why: Small reactive components for MSP-level dialogs, ribbon and report designer. Astro targets content sites.

nodes.label: Local-first: .dplan files plus a workspace file; no server, no…
nodes.text:
Local-first: .dplan files plus a workspace file; no server, no cloud, no telemetry (the only network call is the update check)

Why: Open source, everything stays on the user's computer.

nodes.label: Betas through an opt-in updater channel; slipped items go to…
nodes.text:
Betas through an opt-in updater channel; slipped items go to 0.3.1

Why: The user wants to check the big release step by step.

nodes.label: Datum scheduling style (PLAN-0.3 §3.P): fixed duration, single…
nodes.text:
Datum scheduling style (PLAN-0.3 §3.P): fixed duration, single Progress field, retained logic, slack ≤ 0 critical with a longest-path switch, auto actuals, an Explain panel, calculated cells marked

Why: The user wants something easier than both MSP and P6.

nodes.label: Project Setup panel (skippable, docked right) as step one of…
nodes.text:
Project Setup panel (skippable, docked right) as step one of every new plan; all ISO currencies; logo and company branding; Activity IDs A1000+10; MSP-style network; MSP density; English only; beta backups

Why: The user's answers, 2026-10-24.

nodes.label: docs/reference/MSP-P6-feature-reference.md (from the user) is…
nodes.text:
docs/reference/MSP-P6-feature-reference.md (from the user) is the behaviour spec; its C2 scenarios become tests and a checklist

Why: A shared, written definition of done.

nodes.label: Shipped as one release (no betas) because the user asked to…
nodes.text:
Shipped as one release (no betas) because the user asked to "build and release 0.3"

Why: Betas stay available through the opt-in channel for later versions.

nodes.label: The engine owns fields, filters, groups and sorts (Calc +…
nodes.text:
The engine owns fields, filters, groups and sorts (Calc + query); the window asks for rows per view

Why: One place for values, exports use the same text; 20k tasks query in ~50 ms.

nodes.label: Print/PDF through the WebView print dialog ("Save as PDF")…
nodes.text:
Print/PDF through the WebView print dialog ("Save as PDF") with print CSS, instead of a PDF library

Why: No extra dependency; works for every view and report.

nodes.label: Templates still use the Project Setup panel (setup_done = false)
nodes.text:
Templates still use the Project Setup panel (setup_done = false)

Why: Setup is step one of every new plan, as agreed.

nodes.label: Keep the MS Project ribbon and layout; adopt only…
nodes.text:
Keep the MS Project ribbon and layout; adopt only CentriForge's styling (IBM Plex, palette, square controls, mono labels)

Why: The user's answer: improve the current UI, don't replace the command bar.

nodes.label: Light / Dark / Auto theme via CSS tokens on :root[data-theme]…
nodes.text:
Light / Dark / Auto theme via CSS tokens on :root[data-theme]; canvas colours read the tokens

Why: The user asked for all three.

nodes.label: Formulas are per column (MS Project style) in Excel syntax…
nodes.text:
Formulas are per column (MS Project style) in Excel syntax with [Field] names, evaluated by GridCraft; cell references only in sheet tabs

Why: The user's answer. GridCraft gives ~400 Excel functions without writing them.

nodes.label: GridCraft as a pinned git dependency (calc, model, core), not…
nodes.text:
GridCraft as a pinned git dependency (calc, model, core), not a fork

Why: Small surface (one module), easy upgrades, attribution in NOTICE.

nodes.label: Grid stays DOM (virtual rows) with a single scroller and…
nodes.text:
Grid stays DOM (virtual rows) with a single scroller and sticky header, not canvas

Why: Fixes the alignment bug at the root; real inputs for editing.

nodes.label: Reporting periods per plan (week end day, month close day…
nodes.text:
Reporting periods per plan (week end day, month close day, weighting) chosen by the user

Why: The user's answer: it varies by project.

nodes.label: Charts with Chart.js in a Prism style; PNG save on every chart
nodes.text:
Charts with Chart.js in a Prism style; PNG save on every chart

Why: The user asked for elegant, hoverable charts like Prism/plotly; Chart.js is small.

nodes.label: Period notes and photos stored inside the .dplan (photos…
nodes.text:
Period notes and photos stored inside the .dplan (photos downscaled to 1400 px JPEG)

Why: Portable single file; the user left it to us.

nodes.label: Big ribbon buttons with both a command and a menu are MS…
nodes.text:
Big ribbon buttons with both a command and a menu are MS Project split buttons; contextual tabs carry their group label above the tab

Why: The user's screenshots of 0.3.1.

nodes.label: Report Builder reports and conditional-format rules live in…
nodes.text:
Report Builder reports and conditional-format rules live in project.ui (no format change)

Why: Saved with the plan, no migration.

nodes.label: Recurring tasks are a summary with SNET-constrained occurrences
nodes.text:
Recurring tasks are a summary with SNET-constrained occurrences

Why: Same as MS Project; occurrences stay ordinary tasks.

nodes.label: Effects that mirror outside selection into the grid use…
nodes.text:
Effects that mirror outside selection into the grid use on(sel, …) with untrack, never track cur/ranges

Why: Tracking cur made the effect run before the sel sync and snap the row back (the 0.3.3 bug).

nodes.label: Task sheet and Sheets tabs should share one grid component…
nodes.text:
Task sheet and Sheets tabs should share one grid component (selection, clipboard, fill, formula bar); GridCraft stays the formula engine underneath; scheduling stays in crates/core

Why: The user asked to use the Sheets grid for scheduling. Task rows are not free cells (they carry types, links, outline, validation), so the shared part is the UI grid, not the data model.

nodes.label: ? help beside the tools in every Datum app: a small ? beside…
nodes.text:
? help beside the tools in every Datum app: a small ? beside each ribbon group, page, panel and main dialog opens a card (what it is for, how to use it) from one HELP table in ui/src/help.tsx; Help › What Is This Tool? lists them all. No separate teaching mode

Why: The user's words: "at some of the tools, we can add a small question mark icon… we should do it in all of our applications." Built first in Datum Atlas 0.1.1; same code and styles in every app.

nodes.label: The guide is a PDF per language, downloaded on demand (not in…
nodes.text:
The guide is a PDF per language, downloaded on demand (not in the installer): update::guide(lang) fetches DatumPlan-Guide-{lang}.pdf from this version's release (else latest), requires a matching line in that release's SHA256SUMS.txt and a %PDF header, caps 60 MB, saves to Downloads ("Datum Plan Guide.pdf" / "Datum Plan 使用指南.pdf") with write_atomic, opens it

Why: The user: keep the installer small; inside the app, one click. Same trust rules as updates.

nodes.label: Sheets read the plan through GridCraft tables and names…
nodes.text:
Sheets read the plan through GridCraft tables and names (Tasks[Finish], Resources[Country], ProjectFinish, SPI), not copied values; the Plan sheet keeps its first 18 columns (A–R) so Plan!M:M formulas still work; percentages stay 0–100 like the task sheet

Why: The user built Excel dashboards by copying MSP values by hand. Names are readable and survive column changes; old files keep working.

nodes.label: Excel habits come from GridCraft, not re-implemented…
nodes.text:
Excel habits come from GridCraft, not re-implemented: shift_relative for fill/paste, adjust for insert/delete rows/cols, rename_sheet/delete_sheet, numfmt for formats, functions::all() for suggestions

Why: The user: use GridCraft's engine. Small bridge in sheet.rs.

nodes.label: Flags are a cell format ("flag") and a resource country field…
nodes.text:
Flags are a cell format ("flag") and a resource country field, drawn from flag-icons SVGs bundled as separate lazy files (not emoji)

Why: Windows does not draw flag emoji. Files load only when shown; 271 SVGs ≈ 2.7 MB.

nodes.label: Custom dashboards are 0.5.3 (0.5.1 and 0.5.2 became fix and…
nodes.text:
Custom dashboards are 0.5.3 (0.5.1 and 0.5.2 became fix and chart releases), built on the 0.5.0 sheets

Why: Sheets first so dashboard tiles can read sheet ranges and plan names.

nodes.label: Charts stay on Chart.js (not Plotly), restyled like the…
nodes.text:
Charts stay on Chart.js (not Plotly), restyled like the Chart.js samples: Tailwind-like palette replaces Okabe-Ito, no black axes, cubicInterpolationMode: monotone (no overshoot on S-curves), per-period lines straight; every chart registers in live and resizes on beforeprint/afterprint and with a ResizeObserver; the canvas is absolutely positioned so it never sizes its box

Why: The user found the old Prism-style charts unattractive and saw charts cropped (printed canvases kept their screen width). Chart.js is small (~200 KB) and prints well; Plotly (~3.5 MB) suits Datum Plot.

nodes.label: Guide text in Markdown in the repo; the Chinese guide keeps…
nodes.text:
Guide text in Markdown in the repo; the Chinese guide keeps English UI names in bold with the Chinese meaning beside them; screenshots stay in English with numbered orange markers

Why: The app is English-only; readers must find the buttons. Easy to keep up to date each release (CLAUDE.md step 3).

nodes.label: Windows publisher is "Datum" (bundle.publisher; the copyright…
nodes.text:
Windows publisher is "Datum" (bundle.publisher; the copyright stays "© 2026 Edgar Mendonca"). src-tauri/windows/hooks.nsh (NSIS_HOOK_PREINSTALL) reads the old Software\Edgar Mendonca\Datum Plan install-folder key, installs there if it differs, and deletes the old key

Why: Family rule (FAMILY §9 in the hub). Tauri's NSIS remembers the folder under Software\<publisher>\<product>; the uninstall entry and the default folder use only the product name, so default installs update in place.

nodes.label: Release builds unwind (not abort); guard() in the shell turns…
nodes.text:
Release builds unwind (not abort); guard() in the shell turns a panic in apply/open/import/risk/level preview into an error message; a panic hook appends to crash.log in the app data folder

Why: Abort closed the app on any panic and made the poisoned-lock recovery useless.

nodes.label: Project::normalize clamps spans to MAX_SPAN (10,000,000…
nodes.text:
Project::normalize clamps spans to MAX_SPAN (10,000,000 working minutes ≈ 80 years), lags in % to ±10,000, units to 0–1000, non-finite numbers to 0, splits to 100, day_min to 1–1440; parse::dur caps at MAX_SPAN; WorkCal saturates at a horizon (1800–2600), date_of saturates

Why: Hostile values panicked in calendar arithmetic (succ_opt().unwrap() past the last date).

nodes.label: WorkCal::between counts whole weeks arithmetically (plus…
nodes.text:
WorkCal::between counts whole weeks arithmetically (plus exception corrections) for spans over 28 days; daily S-curves fall back to weeks beyond ~10 years

Why: A task spanning centuries froze the S-curve (O(days²)).

nodes.label: Saves use doc::write_atomic (temp file + rename) for plans…
nodes.text:
Saves use doc::write_atomic (temp file + rename) for plans, autosave, recovery, options, recent, exports; reads use doc::read_limited (300 MB)

Why: No half-written files; no out-of-memory on giant files.

nodes.label: Updater: SHA256SUMS.txt is required; exact file-name match…
nodes.text:
Updater: SHA256SUMS.txt is required; exact file-name match; installer name *-setup.exe of safe characters; unique download folder; 200 MB cap

Why: A release without checksums used to install unverified.

nodes.label: CSV export prefixes ' to text starting with = + - @ (unless a…
nodes.text:
CSV export prefixes ' to text starting with = + - @ (unless a plain number)

Why: Formula (CSV) injection.

nodes.label: Money: each task's cost and actual cost rounded to the…
nodes.text:
Money: each task's cost and actual cost rounded to the currency's minor unit before roll-up (rates keep their decimals); typed fixed costs rounded

Why: Totals equal the sum of shown amounts, without changing the f64 model.

nodes.label: CLI and MCP change plans only through Op (the window's…
nodes.text:
CLI and MCP change plans only through Op (the window's operations); the MCP server writes only plan/export extensions and only on save_plan; panics in a tool call are caught

Why: One way to change a plan; safe for an assistant.

nodes.label: Print: Schedule Risk, Look-ahead and Manpower are flow views…
nodes.text:
Print: Schedule Risk, Look-ahead and Manpower are flow views (FLOWS), named in VIEW_NAMES; the last risk run is stored in project.ui.risk

Why: They printed the Dashboard (the FLOWS fallback).

nodes.label: Actual progress between stored periods is a straight line…
nodes.text:
Actual progress between stored periods is a straight line through each snapshot's % (then to today's % at the status date); tasks no snapshot recorded keep the old working-time line (report::history, along)

Why: The actual S-curve should show when progress really happened; snapshots already stored each task's %.

nodes.label: Manpower "Done" is earned hours (planned hours × progress)…
nodes.text:
Manpower "Done" is earned hours (planned hours × progress), not booked hours; planned spreads work evenly over baseline (or current) dates; people = hours ÷ one person's working hours in the period

Why: There are no timesheets in the model; earned hours are honest and consistent with the S-curve.

nodes.label: Earned schedule uses the same weights and curves as the…
nodes.text:
Earned schedule uses the same weights and curves as the S-curve, in working days on the project calendar

Why: One definition of progress everywhere; works without costs.

nodes.label: Rules of credit are step templates (CreditRule) that…
nodes.text:
Rules of credit are step templates (CreditRule) that ApplyCredit copies into a task's steps and sets % Complete Type to Physical; quantities set physical % = installed ÷ planned. Physical % now drives the S-curve for physical tasks

Why: Reuses steps and physical %, which already drove earned value.

nodes.label: Constraint log is Project.log (LogItem), edited with Op::Log…
nodes.text:
Constraint log is Project.log (LogItem), edited with Op::Log; ready = no open items; overdue = open with a need-by date before the status date

Why: Look-ahead planning needs readiness, not just dates.

nodes.label: <select> whose options load later marks the chosen <option…
nodes.text:
<select> whose options load later marks the chosen <option selected> instead of value= on the select

Why: Solid sets the select's value before async options exist, so it showed the first option.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo uses triangular draws (min, planned, max) and the…
nodes.text:
Monte Carlo uses triangular draws (min, planned, max) and the full scheduler per run; a fixed seed (same plan + settings = same answer); risks 1–5 → 10/30/50/70/90 %; Risk.days = working days added to each linked task (opportunities subtract); cost scales with duration except fixed cost

Why: Simple, explainable, and exact to the engine's own rules (calendars, constraints, progress).

nodes.label: Trades are the resources' Group; usage("group") sums work…
nodes.text:
Trades are the resources' Group; usage("group") sums work resources per group with capacity; rows carry cap, Usage.person = one person's hours per bucket (hours → people)

Why: No new model field; the window shows the engine's capacity instead of computing it.

nodes.label: Levelling always previews (level::preview levels a clone and…
nodes.text:
Levelling always previews (level::preview levels a clone and diffs the dates)

Why: See what moves before changing the plan.

nodes.label: Imports return notes (Imported::Plan(p, notes)): reader notes…
nodes.text:
Imports return notes (Imported::Plan(p, notes)): reader notes plus a date comparison with the file (io::stated_dates, shared with the parity test)

Why: The import report the user asked for in 0.3.12; the comparison makes every import a parity check.

nodes.label: Charts over plain numbers use <Index>, not <For>
nodes.text:
Charts over plain numbers use <Index>, not <For>

Why: <For> reuses nodes by value, so bars with equal values kept stale positions.

nodes.label: ALAP uses free float only: the largest shift (≤ free float)…
nodes.text:
ALAP uses free float only: the largest shift (≤ free float) that every successor link still allows, found by bisection with the forward pass's own rule

Why: Standard rule; using total float pushed ALAP tasks past their successors (found by the random-plan link check).

nodes.label: A started task's late start is that of its remaining work…
nodes.text:
A started task's late start is that of its remaining work; finished successors (and, with progress override, started ones) do not limit a predecessor's late dates

Why: Standard progress rules; the old backward pass gave false negative float under retained logic (found by a hand-worked case).

nodes.label: Parity files are hand-made until real exports are added; the…
nodes.text:
Parity files are hand-made until real exports are added; the README says "checked against hand-worked cases and plan files", never names another product

Why: Honest claim; FAMILY §13.

nodes.label: docs/site.json carries about (two paragraphs) and steps…
nodes.text:
docs/site.json carries about (two paragraphs) and steps (three) for the family site's app page; keep them true to the app and update them with every release; never name commercial products

Why: The user, for the hub's /apps/plan page (FAMILY §10, §13).

nodes.label: rustfmt is not enforced; the code stays in its compact hand…
nodes.text:
rustfmt is not enforced; the code stays in its compact hand style

Why: cargo fmt would add about 3,000 lines to ~7,400 and undo the compact style the user asked for. Clippy -D warnings stays the gate.

nodes.label: Hardening gates in CI: cargo deny, Windows + macOS cargo test…
nodes.text:
Hardening gates in CI: cargo deny, Windows + macOS cargo test, hardening tests in cargo test

Why: Match the rigour of other open-source schedulers before adding features.

nodes.label: Without a status date, progress reports (Dashboard, period…
nodes.text:
Without a status date, progress reports (Dashboard, period reports, S-curves) measure at max(today, latest recorded progress) (Calc::progress_date/progress_at), and the window says so (Summary.measured_at). Earned value and the fields still use the status date or today (status_at)

Why: A plan updated ahead of time showed 0 % done.

nodes.label: The window's state lock recovers from a poisoned mutex…
nodes.text:
The window's state lock recovers from a poisoned mutex (St::lock)

Why: One panicking command used to lock every later command out.

nodes.label: The Datum apps share one design and workflow in FAMILY.md…
nodes.text:
The Datum apps share one design and workflow in FAMILY.md; each app only changes its accent and logo glyph

Why: The user is building a family of tools (next: Datum Plot = Prism + OriginPro) that must look and ship the same.

nodes.label: Templates carry people/assign/costs; Work is titled "Man-hours"
nodes.text:
Templates carry people/assign/costs; Work is titled "Man-hours"

Why: New users see loading, cost and man-hours immediately (the user's Cairn did this).

nodes.label: One grid *engine* (selection, clipboard, fill, formatting…
nodes.text:
One grid *engine* (selection, clipboard, fill, formatting, keys) with two renderers (task outline vs A1 sheet)

Why: The views differ in what a row is; sharing the behaviour removes the duplication without forcing one layout on both.

nodes.label: Network: layout_with(rows, sums, wbs); bands returned with the…
nodes.text:
Network: layout_with(rows, sums, wbs); bands returned with the layout

Why: WBS banding and summary boxes come from the engine, so screen and print agree.

nodes.label: Other views print through one Frame; reports print as flowing…
nodes.text:
Other views print through one Frame; reports print as flowing documents (thead/tfoot repeat the header/footer, @page @bottom-center numbers pages)

Why: Exact pages where the layout is ours (Gantt, network, calendar, tables); flowing pages where it is HTML.

nodes.label: Fill series follow Excel (numbers, text+number, dates by step…
nodes.text:
Fill series follow Excel (numbers, text+number, dates by step; Ctrl copies) but durations, links and resources copy as in MS Project

Why: Matches what users of both tools expect.

nodes.label: open_url only opens github.com/Edgar-Mendonca/Datum-Plan links
nodes.text:
open_url only opens github.com/Edgar-Mendonca/Datum-Plan links

Why: The window cannot be used to open arbitrary URLs.

nodes.label: Ribbon tabs: Task, Schedule, Progress (user rejected "Home")…
nodes.text:
Ribbon tabs: Task, Schedule, Progress (user rejected "Home"); the ribbon shrinks in steps (data-fit 0–3) and never scrolls

Why: User feedback: crowded Task tab and a sideways scrollbar.

nodes.label: Hidden columns stay in the table with a negative width…
nodes.text:
Hidden columns stay in the table with a negative width (Project.columns is now i32); cols() = shown, allCols() = all

Why: Hide/unhide without losing the position; files stay compatible.

nodes.label: Print lays the table and chart out as one strip; pages are…
nodes.text:
Print lays the table and chart out as one strip; pages are windows on it; ID + name repeat; column edges snap

Why: Every column prints, like MS Project, with no overlap.

nodes.label: Printing lays out pages in the UI (SVG) and uses the WebView…
nodes.text:
Printing lays out pages in the UI (SVG) and uses the WebView print dialog (Save as PDF), not a Rust PDF writer

Why: Vector output, exact page sizes via @page, no new dependency; works the same on every view we lay out.

nodes.label: Cell formatting reuses the task's existing style JSON field…
nodes.text:
Cell formatting reuses the task's existing style JSON field (column key → style string); sheets get SheetData.style

Why: No file-format change; old files load unchanged.

nodes.label: Every user-reported bug gets a UI test that fails on the…
nodes.text:
Every user-reported bug gets a UI test that fails on the broken build before the fix ships

Why: Two clicks in a row were never tested; the 0.3.2 suite missed it.

nodes.label: No Python; a separate future app "Datum Plot"…
nodes.text:
No Python; a separate future app "Datum Plot" (Prism/Origin-like) may use Python

Why: The user's answer.

nodes.label: 1. The user reviews the last release in…
nodes.text: The user reviews the last release in the app and sends screenshots with bugs and wishes.

nodes.label: 2. Diagnose first
nodes.text: Diagnose first. Reproduce the problem in the test harness or the real app before changing code. Small fixes go straight to a release.

nodes.label: 3. Bigger asks get a plan file (docs/PLAN-x
nodes.text: Bigger asks get a plan file (docs/PLAN-x.y.z.md): feedback, diagnosis, proposal by area, size, and questions. The plan is logged in this file and pushed. Build only after the user answers.

nodes.label: 4. Build in small steps, engine first…
nodes.text: Build in small steps, engine first (crates/core, with a unit test), then the UI. Keep code compact and in the surrounding style.

nodes.label: 5. Check in the real app under Xvfb…
nodes.text: Check in the real app under Xvfb (scratchpad/app.sh restarts Xvfb and the app, opens the Engineering template and skips Setup), with screenshots of each change. Fix what looks wrong.

nodes.label: 6. Add a UI test for every reported bug…
nodes.text: Add a UI test for every reported bug and new feature (tests_ui/run.cjs, Playwright against ui/dist with the dump fixture). Make sure it fails on the old code where possible.

nodes.label: 7. Run the checks
nodes.text: Run the checks: clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, npm run check:ui, and the UI tests after npm run build:ui + cargo run -p datum-core --example dump > tests_ui/fixture.json.

nodes.label: 8. Release
nodes.text: Release: bump both Cargo.toml files, write the CHANGELOG (it becomes the in-app "What's new"), update this file (version, roadmap, files, decisions, session log, limits), commit, push, run release.yml (workflow_dispatch), then watch CI + Release and confirm the installer.

nodes.label: 9. Report to the user in plain language
nodes.text: Report to the user in plain language: what changed, what was checked, what is not done, and anything to check on Windows.

nodes.label: Session 1 (brainstorm + 0.1.0)
nodes.text:
· Read Cairn and CentriForge. Wrote the brainstorm and a draft logo.
· The user approved the name, Windows only, no .mpp, Rust/Tauri 2, and small releases. They sent MS Project screenshots.

nodes.label: Session 3 (0.2.0)
nodes.text:
· The user asked for 0.1.2, 0.1.3, 0.1.4 and the "0.2 onwards" items (calendars, constraints, exchange, resources) all in 0.2. They shared a "P6 planning basics" chart (EPS/WBS/activities/calendars/relationships/F9/critical path/resource loading/baseline/update progress).
· Rewrote the engine on minutes with real calendars. Added constraints, deadlines, ALAP, manual and inactive tasks, summary links, status date and actuals, resources and costs, workload, and baselines.
· Added IO: MSPDI, XER, XLSX/CSV, all with round-trip tests.
· Split the UI into 7 files. Added the column picker, clipboard, fill, move, find/replace, context menus, timeline strip, progress drag, details pane, Resource Sheet, Workload, Change Working Time, Options, recovery, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+J.
· Bugs fixed during testing:
· dialogs lost their inputs on OK (also present in 0.1.x)
· camelCase fields were missing in the view JSON
· the details pane overlapped the Gantt canvas (fixed with a ResizeObserver)
· pressing Enter in Ctrl+K also clicked the dialog it opened
· quick-add IDs were shifted by the new row
· CSV header guessing put two columns on the same field
· alphanumeric predecessor IDs were dropped
· Checked by running the real app under Xvfb: Gantt, right-click menu, timeline, details (General/Relationships/Resources), Resource Sheet, Workload, palette, Change Working Time (Saturday working moved the finish from 08-Feb to 21-Jan), CSV import with mapping, baseline bars, Dashboard. 13 core tests and clippy -D warnings pass.
· Released 0.2.0.

nodes.label: Session 4 (0.3 brainstorm)
nodes.text:

· too few fields, and no custom fields, formulas or Field Settings
· weak information dialogs and reporting
· ribbon buttons such as "Gantt Chart" should be dropdowns
· wants MSP's timeline and more save formats

· Agreed that 0.2.1 → 0.5.2 become a single 0.3 release. Wrote PLAN-0.3.md (audit, principles, feature catalogue A–O, architecture changes, beta milestones, open decisions). Waiting for the user's review and decisions before building.

nodes.label: Session 5 (0.3.0)
nodes.text:

· Engine: model format 3; scheduler upgrades (elapsed, % lags, splits, LOE/WBS summary, retained logic/progress override, schedule from finish, longest path, float paths, lag calendars); leveling; task types; formula language; field registry with EV; query API; usage/curves/compare; DCMA + P6 checks; network layout; new export formats. Benchmark: 20k tasks schedule 36 ms, calc 44 ms, grid 49 ms (release).
· Shell: new commands, beta channel, backups of older plans, logo picker, file saving for pictures and HTML.
· UI: rewritten in SolidJS + Vite (10 TSX files). Ribbon with dropdowns, Tell Me, grid with header menus, Gantt + timeline, P6 details tabs, all views, reports, dialogs, Project Setup panel.
· Tested in the real app under Xvfb: templates, Project Setup, inline edits rescheduling, context menu, Task Information, baseline + progress, Tracking Gantt, weekly report, Network Diagram, Calendar, Task Usage, Checks, Dashboard. Bugs fixed: a global svg size rule hid the network diagram; Enter in a dialog's first select did not press OK; select text clipped in WebKitGTK; keys only worked with focus inside the app div.
· UI test harness: cargo run -p datum-core --example dump > fix.json, then a Playwright script that serves ui/dist with a mocked window.TAURI (kept in the session scratchpad; rebuild it from this note if needed).

nodes.text:

· Wrote PLAN-0.3.1.md: diagnosis, Gridcraft crates as pinned dependencies, canvas spreadsheet grid, CentriForge shell and modules, period reporting, Python recommendation (none in 0.3.x), release steps 0.3.1–0.3.3, 10 questions. Waiting for answers and the user's bug write-up.

nodes.text:
· User: could not click or select cells (row stuck on the first selection). · User asked why not use the Sheets (GridCraft) grid for the schedule too. Answer: GridCraft is a calculation engine, not a UI grid; the Sheets view and the task sheet are both our own DOM grids. Plan: one shared grid component for both (0.4.x), keeping the scheduler's task rows. See decision log.

nodes.label: Session 9 (0.3.11, hardening quick wins)
nodes.text:
· User: build 0.3.11 with the two bugs and the hardening quick wins; record everything here, in the CHANGELOG and in the DATUM hub memory.
· Built crates/core/src/hardening.rs (4 tests). On first run it found real faults: a damaged XER calendar sliced past the end (pnode, now clamped and depth-limited) and a WBS that loops back on itself recursed for ever (stack overflow; walk now visits each WBS node once). A random-plan "late before early" report turned out to be 17:00 vs 08:00 next morning (same working moment); the test compares in working time.
· Fixed the Dashboard 0 % (Calc::progress_date, Summary.measured_at, label and report header say the date used) and the date picker (input blurs after the pick; UI test). St::lock() recovers a poisoned mutex. deny.toml + license = "MIT" in both crates; CI jobs deny and platforms (Windows, macOS). SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md. Decided not to enforce rustfmt (compact style).
· Roadmap renumbered: 0.3.12 Trust in the dates, 0.4.0 Risk & resources, 0.4.1 Progress history, 0.4.2 Command line & automation (also in docs/site.json). Stale "templates have no resources" limit removed.

nodes.label: Session 14 (0.4.2, hardening, command line…
nodes.text:
· User: build 0.4.2 and 0.4.3 together overnight, with a complete security, robustness and hardening pass of the whole app.
· Audit and fixes. Probing hostile values found panics in calendar arithmetic (huge durations, lags, splits, delays) and a divide-by-zero (zero-length day); fixed with clamping in normalize, a calendar horizon and saturating dates. A battery (hardening::exercise) now runs every engine function on hostile plans, extreme edits and the random plans; it found the S-curve freezing on century-long plans (fast whole-week between, weekly fallback). Also: atomic saves, 300 MB read limit, unwind + guard() + crash.log (release builds aborted on any panic), updater requires checksums (it installed unverified without SHA256SUMS.txt), stricter CSP (and blob: images: progress-report photos were blocked), CSV formula injection, ics line breaks, allowed_url, npm audit in CI. Hostile sheet formulas were already safe (#CIRC!, #NUM!).
· Built ops.rs (catalogue), crates/cli (datum-cli + MCP server, tests drive a whole assistant session), money to the cent, the release ships datum-cli-X.Y.Z.exe. Print: the three views printed the Dashboard (fixed); risk charts full width on paper; last risk run in project.ui.risk. Found on the way: "-0 hrs" on an empty plan (float sum of nothing is -0).
· Not done: JSON schemas for every op (examples only); Tell Me still lists window commands; the CLI cannot import spreadsheets (column mapping is in the window).

nodes.label: Datum Plot
nodes.text:
Analyse data and make publication-ready graphs: statistics, regression, curve fitting and page layouts, in one app for Windows.

For: Scientists, researchers, lab teams and students.

Stack: Rust shell (src-tauri) + Rust project engine (crates/core), Tauri 2, WebView2, SolidJS + Vite UI in strict TypeScript, plain CSS tokens, IBM Plex. Python worker (py/) with numpy, SciPy and matplotlib for every calculation and every graph; the installer bundles embeddable CPython 3.13.

nodes.label: model.rs
nodes.text: Format 1. Project (name, info, tables, graphs, analyses, nextId, ui), Analysis (id, table, name, kind, sets, options JSON), GraphSettings.overlays (analysis ids drawn on the graph: curves, or brackets on column graphs), GraphSettings.column (scatter/bars/box/violin/mean/paired), GraphSettings.palette (scheme name or "#hex, …"), Info, Table (kind "xy" or "column"; a column table keeps the X column but never uses or shows it; Table::column(n); X column + sets; cols is the flat column list, column 0 = X; rows, rowTitles, excluded [row, col], style "r:c" → style string), DataSet (entry rep/msn/mesn, reps), Graph + GraphSettings (error, errorDir, points, line, cap, width/height mm, font, fontSize, boldTitles, style prism/frame, title, legend, x/y Axis, sets SetStyle). normalize, add_table, from_json (refuses newer formats).

nodes.label: doc.rs
nodes.text: Op: NewTable, Delete, Rename, Duplicate, Cells (col −1 = row title), Import (rows → new table + graph; titles from the first row; sets of reps), AddAnalysis (overlay → drawn on the table's graphs, joining lines off), SetAnalysis, Overlay, Sort (rows by a column, empty last, titles/exclusions/styles move), CopyLook (look of one graph onto others, keeping titles, axis titles and ranges, overlays, line), Paste (first row of words = titles; grows rows and data sets), Exclude, TableSet, SetDef (add/replace/remove a data set, remapping columns, exclusions and styles), Rows (insert/delete, remapping), Style, AddGraph, GraphSet, Info, ProjectName, Ui, Batch. number() parses 1,234.5 / −4 / 12% / 1e-3.

nodes.label: hardening.rs
nodes.text: FAMILY §11 tests (0.3.0): invariants (unique ids < next_id < ID_LIMIT, table shapes, setting ranges, links), random hostile documents (300, with a save/load round trip), random edit sequences with full undo, damaged files (truncated, garbled, deeply nested, binary, newer), atomic saves, hostile values clamped, a speed gate (one edit of a 1M-row table < 250 ms release).

nodes.label: templates.rs
nodes.text: Blank XY, Growth curve, Standard curve (mean/SD/N), Dose-response (log X), Tensile test (modulus fit 0–0.003 + tensile analysis), Arrhenius (activation energy, log Y), Compare groups (column table, ANOVA + Tukey brackets), Weibull strength (column table, box plot, Weibull analysis), DSC peak (area above a straight baseline); list() gives tile pictures (column tables: the group means).

nodes.label: dump.rs
nodes.text: Fixture for the UI tests.

nodes.label: main.rs
nodes.text: Commands in the diagram plus result (an analysis via the Calc engine, cached), models, export_all (folder picker, every graph, unique file names), export_excel (save dialog → Python excel), new_table(kind) (column tables), graph requests carry overlays; copy_graph (PNG → Windows clipboard via tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager), copy_text, read_clipboard, import_file, restart_engine; Options (theme, autosave, beta, openLast, decimals, reps, entry, error, width, height, font, fontSize, style, dpi, paper, landscape, company, logo, styles = saved graph styles); new_project keeps a sample graph's x, y, line, error, overlays, points, column, sets, palette; new tables/graphs follow the options; recovery; recent files; open_url only for this repo.

nodes.label: py.rs
nodes.text: Finds Python (DATUM_PYTHON, the runtime pack, else python/python3); a reader thread lets requests time out (start 180 s, request 60 s → kill and report); restart(); and py/worker.py (bundled or the source tree), MPLCONFIGDIR in the app cache, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, restart once on failure, cache of the last 24 requests. Two workers (I3): Engine draws graphs, Calc runs results, models and Excel export, so a long fit never holds up drawing; both start in a thread at launch (Calc after Engine is ready); Restart Engine restarts both; emits engine with versions or the error.

nodes.label: update.rs
nodes.text: Datum Plan's updater with REPO = Edgar-Mendonca/Datum-Plot; downloads the release's -setup.exe; download() (progress + SHA-256).

nodes.label: runtime.rs
nodes.text: The Python runtime pack: %LOCALAPPDATA%/com.edgarmendonca.datumplot/runtime/N (N = py/runtime.txt); unpacked from resources/runtime.zip (in every installer); unzips with progress (engine status event), removes older runtimes, the zip and 0.1.0's resources/python. Release Windows builds only; dev builds use the PATH Python. 1 test.

nodes.label: tauri.conf.json
nodes.text: Bundles py/worker.py and py/datum/*.py; the release config adds runtime.zip.

nodes.label: runtime.txt
nodes.text: The runtime pack number: bump it whenever py/requirements.txt changes, so installed apps download the new pack.

nodes.label: analysis.py
nodes.text: Analyses: run(kind, table, sets, options) → {title, answer, tabs of formatted tables, checks, methods, legend, code, plots (small SVGs), curves (for graphs), cells (outliers)}. Kinds: describe, normality (Shapiro, D'Agostino, Anderson-Darling, Lilliefors + QQ), outliers (iterative Grubbs), linear (OLS/WLS via statsmodels, origin, polynomial, Deming with jackknife SEs, fit range, compare lines F tests, runs test, CI/PI bands, interpolation), fit (lmfit ExpressionModel, library or own equation, init/fixed, CIs, AICc, correlations, bands), arrhenius (ln k vs 1/T, Ea, A). g() formats numbers, pv() APA P values.

nodes.label: groups.py
nodes.text: Compare groups (B4–B8, B16, B23): column (values by row, for pairing), summary (values, or entered mean/SD/N), pairs_of; ttest (unpaired Welch/Student from stats, paired, ratio, one-sample; effect sizes; Shapiro and Brown-Forsythe checks), nonparam (Mann-Whitney + Hodges-Lehmann, Wilcoxon (approximate with ties, as R), KS, Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn (Bonferroni), Friedman), anova (ordinary, Welch/Brown-Forsythe via statsmodels anova_oneway, repeated measures with Geisser-Greenhouse; posthoc Tukey (scipy.stats.tukey_hsd), Dunnett (scipy.stats.dunnett), Holm-Šidák, Šidák, Bonferroni, LSD; trend; η², ω²), correlation (Pearson + Fisher-z CI, Spearman, Kendall, matrix), power (statsmodels power solvers, curve). Results carry brackets [set, set, P].

nodes.label: console.py
nodes.text: Console and notebook (H1, H5): frame (a table as a DataFrame: X, then sets; replicates Name 1…, msn Name mean/SD/N), Tables (lazy mapping), to_table (new_table → engine JSON), run (one namespace NS; last expression shown; stdout/stderr captured; figures as SVG; errors with the console line; output ≤ 100 000 chars), reset, notebook (nbformat 4; tables inline or as CSV beside it above 5000 cells; analyses' code without [...] placeholders). Worker console/notebook; shell console (adds new tables, returns the state; timeout message) and export_notebook.

nodes.label: imports.py
nodes.text: Import (A13, A14): read_pzfx (namespace-free ElementTree: Table/HugeTable, TableType → kind, YFormat → entry, X/Y columns and subcolumns, Excluded="1", row titles), plates (96/384 blocks → grouped tables), numeric_table, read_many (one set per file, joined when X matches). io.read_file returns tables for .pzfx and plates for sheets.

nodes.label: region.py
nodes.text: Region tool (E5): region(table, x0, x1, y0, y1) per curve: points, mean, SD, range, area, slope, highest (worker region, shell region).

nodes.label: report.py
nodes.text: Slides and reports (G5): parts (each graph as 300 dpi PNG with its overlays), results, slides (python-pptx, 16:9) and word (python-docx: figures with captions, results with tables, methods). Worker report, shell export_report.

nodes.label: surface.py
nodes.text: Surface fits (B26): points3 (a matrix grid, or X, Y, Z from three data sets), design/TERMS (plane, quad, cubic by statsmodels OLS; the quadratic's stationary point and its kind from the Hessian), gauss2d (curve_fit), surface (tables, residual plots; surface key with a 40 × 40 grid for the graph). graph.py gained with_break (Y breaks for column/grouped/nested graphs by drawing twice), polar_figure, matrix_grid and matrix_figure (contour/heatmap/surface/wireframe, colour bar, fit overlay).

nodes.label: sheet.py
nodes.text: Worksheets and formulas (A9, A11): evaluate (AST-checked formula: names A, B… (row means), X, i, col("title"), numbers made float, text only inside col(); FUNCS whitelist; results rounded to 15 significant digits), recalc (formula columns left to right, each seeing the ones before; worker cmd formula), sheet_view (worksheet → XY table: first X column, Y + following Y-error column → mean ± SD entry, other columns hidden but kept in place).

nodes.label: thermal.py
nodes.text: Materials curves (B30, B31): dsc (peaks above a line/poly baseline found on a smoothed copy; onset/endset from the steepest tangents meeting the baseline; area; ΔH = area ÷ (rate/60)), tga (DTG peaks; onset/end from the tangent at the fastest loss meeting the plateaus; mass lost; residue; T at 5 % loss), thermal, life_text, sn (Basquin on log S vs log N or 2N, run-outs left out and marked →, fatigue strength at chosen lives). Curve marks take a 4th element: below the point (dips).

nodes.label: signal.py
nodes.text: Peaks and signals (B24, B25): baseline (none/min/line/poly: polynomial refitted to the points within the noise of the fit), peaks (detection on a Savitzky-Golay copy, heights/FWHM/areas on the data, areas split at valleys, optional lmfit Gaussian/Lorentzian/Voigt sum; curves: dashed baseline with numbered marks, fitted sum), even, signal (rfft amplitude spectrum, Butterworth sosfiltfilt low/high/band, resample). draw_overlays draws curve marks.

nodes.label: nested.py
nodes.text: Nested (A8, B20): subgroups (each sub-column of a group), nested (hierarchical ANOVA: groups tested against subgroups within groups; t from F for two groups; variance components from MixedLM REML with group dummies, ANOVA estimators as the fallback; ICC). graph.nested_figure draws subgroup dot columns with means, the group mean and error across subgroup means.

nodes.label: survival.py
nodes.text: Survival (A5, B19, D9): subjects (time in X, 1/0 in the group's column), km (Kaplan-Meier with Greenwood log CIs; upper limit NaN once S = 0, as R), median (R's rule, incl. CI limits), logrank (k groups, O−E with the variance matrix), survival (summary, log-rank, Cox HRs via statsmodels PHReg Efron), steps. graph.survival_figure draws the staircases, censor ticks and the CI band (error == "ci").

nodes.label: regress.py
nodes.text: Many variables (B21, B22): pca (SVD of the scaled or centred matrix, signs fixed so the largest loading is positive, Kaiser or 80 % rule, scree + biplot, scores table), cluster (Ward/average/complete linkage or k-means best of 10 seeded starts, clusters numbered by first row, silhouette, dendrogram with the cut line), scores_table (results → a multi table aligned to the original rows); xy_view (a multi table seen as XY, first variable on X, fromMulti flag so XY analyses skip it by default), frame (complete rows), multireg (OLS / GLM binomial / GLM Poisson: coefficients, VIF, odds or rate ratios, fit table, checks, two small plots).

nodes.label: tools.py
nodes.text: Data tools and materials (A15, A18, D4, B14, B27, B29): transform (X/Y functions, baseline, normalise, replicates → mean/SD/N), check, frequency (common bins, histogram/QQ/ECDF plots), auc (trapezoid, baselines incl. a straight line, peaks; curves with fill), smooth (Savitzky-Golay, LOWESS, moving average; derivatives, cumulative integral), tensile (per specimen: modulus by least squares in a range or 10–40 % of UTS, offset yield, UTS, elongations, toughness; dashed offset line), weibull (MLE with Hessian CIs, median-rank regression, Weibull plot). Results that make tables carry table (Results › New table from result → NewTable).

nodes.label: models.py
nodes.text: The curve-fit model library (15 models: equation, first guess, description).

nodes.label: io.py
nodes.text: File › Import readers: CSV/TSV/TXT (delimiter sniffing, decimal commas with ;, encodings) and XLSX (openpyxl, every sheet); all cells as text. write_excel (G6): a sheet per table (excluded values blue italic) and per result (title, answer, every table, methods).

nodes.label: files.py
nodes.text: atomic(path) (temp file beside the target, fsync, os.replace, cleanup on failure), write_bytes, safe_text (CSV text starting = + - @ gets '). Every export goes through it.

nodes.label: worker.py
nodes.text: The protocol loop: warm-up render, {"ready": true}, then one answer line per request; stdout reserved for the protocol.

nodes.label: stats.py
nodes.text: set_columns, value, describe (n, mean, SD, SEM, CI via scipy.stats.t), from_summary, summarize.

nodes.label: graph.py
nodes.text: PALETTES + palette() (schemes, colour maps spread over the sets, own #hex lists), rc_for (fonts, Prism or framed axes), draw_overlays (fitted curves, dashed lines, shaded areas (fill), CI/PI bands, equations in the emptiest corner; brackets on column graphs via draw_brackets, stacked), column_figure (dots with swarm, bars, box, violin, mean, before–after; y from 0), axes (shared axis code), figure (means ± error bars or each replicate, lines, log axes, ranges, ticks, grid, legend, title), geometry, render (SVG + geometry + points), export (png/svg/pdf/tiff/eps, dpi, transparent; base64 for the clipboard).

nodes.label: test_analysis.py
nodes.text: Linear regression vs R lm() on Anscombe's data; NIST StRD Misra1a; model recovery for 6 library models; fixed parameters; Arrhenius Ea; describe; Shapiro vs R; Grubbs cells; compare lines; interpolation; Deming; replicates.

nodes.label: test_groups.py
nodes.text: 0.2.2 analyses vs R: Welch/Student/paired t (sleep), from mean/SD/N, Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis, ANOVA + Tukey (PlantGrowth), every ANOVA variant, Pearson CI (Anscombe), power.t.test; transforms, AUC, derivative/integral, tensile on an ideal curve, Weibull recovery, frequency, checks, global fit, every column graph with brackets and palettes.

nodes.label: test_engine.py
nodes.text: Statistics vs R, exclusions, mean/SD/N entry, renders, log axes, every export format, the worker protocol.

nodes.label: test_hardening.py
nodes.text: Damaged files for every reader, the worker answering bad requests and continuing, xlsx without live formulas, atomic exports, random tables through every analysis and graph.

nodes.label: smoke.py
nodes.text: Engine smoke test (CI): cargo run -p datum-core --example dump all → every template through the real worker: analyses, every graph type on every table, every export format, layouts, xlsx/ipynb/console, slides and report (532 requests).

nodes.label: requirements.txt
nodes.text: numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, matplotlib 3.11.2, openpyxl 3.1.5, statsmodels 0.15.0, lmfit 1.3.4 (pinned; runtime 2).

nodes.label: index.html
nodes.text: Root and the icon sprite (Plan's ~90 icons recoloured teal + Plot icons: xy, graph, sheet, results, layout, infosheet, err, axis, log, legend, symbol, image, addset, addrow, delrow, exclude, sigma, curve, size, line, frame).

nodes.label: api.ts
nodes.text: Types matching the Rust JSON, Render, spans/width/letter/num.

nodes.label: store.ts
nodes.text: Signals: out, item {section, id}, backstage, tab, navOpen, engine, options, theme; act, call, loadOut, open; menus, dialogs, toasts.

nodes.label: tools.tsx
nodes.text: Sort, Find (Ctrl+F; goto signal selects the cell), Exclude Rows by a rule, Test Chooser (questions → kind + preset), Statistics Guide, STYLES + applyStyle/saveStyle/styleMenu (D13), PALETTES + colour-blind preview (Machado matrices) paletteDialog (D16), copyLook (D14), exportAll (G4), exportExcel (G6), significance (D3).

nodes.label: datatable.tsx
nodes.text: The XY or column grid (column tables hide the X column: width 0, skipped by the cursor) (selection column 0 = row title, k ≥ 1 = grid column k − 1): two-row headings by data set, typing, ranges, TSV copy/cut/paste (→ Paste op), fill handle + Ctrl+D/R, Paste Special, Ctrl+B/I/U, Ctrl+E exclude, context menu (insert/delete rows, format/add data set); TableHead (titles and units); setDialog, addSet, rename.

nodes.label: Default graph look is Prism's (open axes, ticks out, bold…
nodes.text:
Default graph look is Prism's (open axes, ticks out, bold titles, Arial 10 pt, 80 × 60 mm, Y from zero); framed (Origin) is one click

Why: Most likely users are Prism users; both looks available (question 6 still open).

nodes.label: Format Graph is docked on the right and applies each change…

Format Graph is docked on the right and applies each change immediately (each is an undo step)

Why: The graph stays visible, as in Prism's live formatting.

nodes.label: Excluded values: blue italic, struck through; stored as [row…

Excluded values: blue italic, struck through; stored as [row, col] in the table

Why: Prism's convention, plus a strike so it reads in greyscale.

nodes.label: Brainstorm the full feature set first (catalogue A–J with IDs…
nodes.text:
Brainstorm the full feature set first (catalogue A–J with IDs and releases in PLAN-0.2), then build release by release

nodes.label: Python runtime as a numbered pack unpacked to the user's data…
nodes.text:
Python runtime as a numbered pack unpacked to the user's data folder (runtime/N); bump py/runtime.txt when requirements change

Why: Starts stay fast; Python is unpacked only when its libraries change.

nodes.label: One installer per release (-setup.exe with runtime.zip inside)…
nodes.text:
One installer per release (-setup.exe with runtime.zip inside) for installs and updates; no update-only installer, no separate runtime download

Why: The user: separate files confuse people; the 87 MB in-app update was quick and fine.

nodes.label: Materials ideas B27–B31 added to the catalogue

Materials ideas B27–B31 added to the catalogue

Why: The user's background.

nodes.label: Equation and R² on the graph by default; regression uses every…

Lay out the whole UI first: every catalogue feature has its place now (ribbon, galleries, navigator, Roadmap); planned ones are dimmed and explain what and when; then build feature by feature

Release order: 0.2 statistics and regression, then 0.3 compare groups

Help shipped as its own release (0.2.1) and the planned 0.2.1–0.2.5 moved up one number, so releases stay consecutive

The 28 features became 0.2.2 (0.2.1 had shipped ? help meanwhile); the rest regrouped into 0.2.3–0.2.7 and 1.0 (PLAN-0.2 §11). Numbers stay consecutive

nodes.label: Small steps again: the remaining 49 features in releases of…

Small steps again: the remaining 49 features in releases of one to four (0.2.3–0.2.24, then 1.0; PLAN-0.2 §12)

nodes.label: Grouped table = kind "grouped" (same model; row titles name…
nodes.text:
Grouped table = kind "grouped" (same model; row titles name the row factor, data sets the other, X column hidden); two-way ANOVA with statsmodels Type III (sum contrasts); brackets carry a 4th element (row) for grouped graphs

Why: Same reuse as column tables; Type III handles unequal replicates as Prism and R car::Anova do.

nodes.label: Contingency table = kind "contingency" (a grouped table with…
nodes.text:
Contingency table = kind "contingency" (a grouped table with one count per cell, Table::contingency); graphs go through grouped_figure (new "percent" = stacked to 100 % of each row)

Why: Reuse; nothing new in the model.

nodes.label: Parts of whole = kind "parts" (Table::parts, built on the…
nodes.text:
Parts of whole = kind "parts" (Table::parts, built on the contingency table); graph.parts_figure draws a pie/donut per data set in one axes (no hover points) or 100 % bars

Why: Reuse; one axes keeps export and geometry unchanged.

nodes.label: Second Y axis = SetStyle.right + GraphSettings.y2; axis break…
nodes.text:
Second Y axis = SetStyle.right + GraphSettings.y2; axis break = Axis.breakFrom/breakTo (Y, linear, XY graphs, not together with a right axis), drawn as two stacked axes; hover points of right-axis sets carry a 7th value (their height in left-axis units)

Why: Settings stay plain data; the window's hover keeps one coordinate system.

nodes.label: Annotations = GraphSettings.notes (Note: kind, x, y, x2, y2…
nodes.text:
Annotations = GraphSettings.notes (Note: kind, x, y, x2, y2, text, color, size, bold) in data units; graph.figure = build + draw_notes with the axis limits restored

Why: Notes follow the data and never rescale the graph.

nodes.label: Users' feedback first: comments from users (via the owner) are…
nodes.text:
Users' feedback first: comments from users (via the owner) are discussed, judged and built as their own small release before the planned one (0.2.10 = four requests; layouts moved to 0.2.11, later releases +1)

Why: The user: "first let us discuss… then build it in one version, and I can inform that these updates are there."

nodes.label: Layouts: Project.layouts (Layout page mm, letters, items…
nodes.text:
Layouts: Project.layouts (Layout page mm, letters, items LayoutItem graph/text in mm), ops AddLayout/LayoutSet; Python graph.page draws each graph twice (alone at its panel size with constrained layout to find its axes, then into a SubFigure whose bbox_relative is set to its place, axes positions copied), so pages stay vector

Why: Matplotlib subfigures in overlapping gridspecs or with constrained layout put panels in the wrong places; the two-pass copy is exact.

nodes.label: zip 9 and deny.toml (security and hardening): zip 2.x had…
nodes.text:
zip 9 and deny.toml (security and hardening): zip 2.x had three advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0367, 0368, 0369: unsafe symlinks and permissions in extract()); Plot's own loop in runtime.rs never calls extract() and only opens its bundled runtime.zip, so the risk was low, but the version moved to 9.1.3. deny.toml (Datum Plan's, plus BSL-1.0 for clipboard-win/error-code under the clipboard plugin) and a deny CI job, as FAMILY §11's hardening standard asks

Why: Found by Datum Sim's chat with cargo deny check on a copy of 0.2.12.

nodes.label: docs/site.json (FAMILY §10) (with about and steps for the…
nodes.text:
docs/site.json (FAMILY §10) (with about and steps for the family site's Overview) is updated in every release together with the roadmap above; public text (CHANGELOG, README, site.json, the in-app roadmap) never names, compares with or claims to copy a commercial product (FAMILY §13): file formats are named by extension (.xlsx, .pzfx, .pptx)

Why: The Datum family site and network read site.json and leave out lines that name other products.

nodes.label: Many variables = kind "multi" (Table::multi, one value per…
nodes.text:
Many variables = kind "multi" (Table::multi, one value per cell, row titles name the samples); graphs and XY analyses see it through regress.xy_view (first variable on X, hidden as a data set); multireg takes the outcome as options.y and the other ticked sets as predictors, listwise deletion; Wald CIs for GLMs (R's confint.default)

Why: Reuse of the XY path; no new graph code.

nodes.label: How to cite: CITATION.cff at the root (GitHub's "Cite this…
nodes.text:
How to cite: CITATION.cff at the root (GitHub's "Cite this repository") and a README section; bump its version and date-released in every release

Why: A user asked how to cite the app.

nodes.label: PCA and clustering run on any table's data sets (one value per…
nodes.text:
PCA and clustering run on any table's data sets (one value per row: the first sub-column), scaled to SD 1 by default; results offer a multi table (scores, or the data plus a Cluster column) with one row per original row, empty where a row was left out

Why: Keeps row titles lined up; reuses New table from result.

nodes.label: Survival table = kind "survival" (Table::survival): X is shown…
nodes.text:
Survival table = kind "survival" (Table::survival): X is shown and holds the time; each row is one subject with 1 (event) or 0 (censored) in its group's column, the other groups empty (the usual layout); the graph is drawn from the table (no overlay), Y fixed 0–105 % while the axis is automatic; Gehan-Breslow-Wilcoxon and the number-at-risk table are left for later

Why: One value per row keeps entry simple; reuses the XY X column.

nodes.label: Nested table = kind "nested" (Table::nested): a column-style…
nodes.text:
Nested table = kind "nested" (Table::nested): a column-style table whose sub-columns are subgroups (reps = subgroups per group); the nested test is the classic hierarchical F (groups / subgroups-within-groups MS), equal to ANOVA on subgroup means when balanced, with REML variance components

Why: Exact for balanced designs, simple to explain; the mixed model supplies the variance split.

nodes.label: Peaks are found on a lightly smoothed copy (Savitzky-Golay…
nodes.text:
Peaks are found on a lightly smoothed copy (Savitzky-Golay, window ≈ n/30) with width ≥ 2 points and prominence ≥ 10 % of the range, then measured on the raw data; polynomial baselines refit to the points within one residual SD of the fit (no endless sinking); no pybaselines dependency

Why: Noise must not become peaks; keeps the Python pack unchanged.

nodes.label: DSC/TGA and S–N are XY analyses (no new table kinds): DSC…
nodes.text:
DSC/TGA and S–N are XY analyses (no new table kinds): DSC endotherms down by default, onsets by the steepest tangent (exactly centre − 2σ for a Gaussian), ΔH needs the heating rate (default 10 K/min); S–N run-outs come from a cycle limit, not a separate column

Why: Users already keep these curves in XY tables; simple to enter.

nodes.label: Worksheet = kind "sheet" (Table::sheet): every data set one…
nodes.text:
Worksheet = kind "sheet" (Table::sheet): every data set one column, DataSet.role (x, "", yerr, skip), units, comment; graphs/XY analyses via sheet.sheet_view (hidden sets keep their index so styles stay put). Formulas live in DataSet.formula, values in the column; Python works them out (shell formula command, Op::Formula); after any op on a table with formulas the UI calls formula with merge, which uses Doc::merge so the edit and its recalculation are one undo step

Why: Keeps the model plain (values stored, nothing recomputed on open); formulas in Python as the user wants; one undo step feels right.

nodes.label: Second round of users' requests in the same release as planned…
nodes.text:
Second round of users' requests in the same release as planned work (0.2.21 = requests + 3D): the user asked for fewer, bigger releases to finish this week. Column widths live in the project's ui["colw.<table>"] (display column → px) via Op::Ui; the heading × went (delete stays in the right-click menu and Remove Data Set); empty data sets are unticked by default in analysis dialogs. Matrix = kind "matrix" (Table::matrix): X column = X, data set titles = Y values, cells = Z, yTitle/yUnits = Z; GraphSettings.polar/levels/elev/azim

Why: Friendlier and reliable (a project reopens as it was left); reuses the X column and data sets, no new storage.

nodes.label: Bigger releases to finish this week: 0.2.22 = data in and out…
nodes.text:
Bigger releases to finish this week: 0.2.22 = data in and out (D17, E5, A13, A14, G5, F3), 0.2.23 = Python and automation (H1–H5), then 1.0. Large data: stats.summarize_fast above 2000 rows, graph.thin (min/max per stretch) and rasterized markers above 5000 points, hover sample ≤ ~2000, small plots rasterize big lines. Imported tables go through shell import_tables (one undo step, each with graph_for(kind)). Layout panels use max(graph font, layout font) so posters read from afar. python-pptx 1.0.2 and python-docx 1.2.0 join the Python pack (runtime 3)

Why: The user's deadline; reuse of existing paths; journal layouts unchanged (8 pt < 10 pt).

nodes.label: Security posture (0.2.23 review): code runs only from the…
nodes.text:
Security posture (0.2.23 review): code runs only from the console on Run; My Analyses live in the app's options (snippets), never in projects; the updater refuses releases without SHA256SUMS and matches the exact file name; open_url only this repo's pages without odd characters; Table::normalize caps (1000 sets, 50 reps, 1M rows, 20M cells), Doc::open refuses > 1 GB, imports > 300 MB; undo budget 60M cells (≥ 10 steps); put/Rows/Paste refuse beyond the caps; analysis.run turns ZeroDivision/Overflow into plain messages and stats.value treats NaN/inf as empty; the worker cleans NaN from replies; CI runs npm audit and pip-audit beside cargo deny; the release checks the bundled Python imports pptx, docx, statsmodels and lmfit

Why: The user asked for a full security, robustness and hardening pass before 1.0; each item has a test (core: hostile files, impossible edits, undo budget; Python: awkward data, console errors; shell: checksum matching).

nodes.label: Column table = Table.kind = "column", same model (X column…
nodes.text:
Column table = Table.kind = "column", same model (X column kept, hidden in the UI, unused by Python); each group a data set with reps 1 (or mean/SD/N)

Why: No new table code in Rust; every op (paste, sort, exclude, sets) works unchanged.

nodes.label: Significance brackets are analysis overlays: t-test…
nodes.text:
Significance brackets are analysis overlays: t-test, nonparametric and ANOVA results carry brackets; drawn only on column graphs (draws()); options brackets sig/all/none and stars/P

Why: Same live chain as fitted curves; nothing stored on the graph.

nodes.label: Transforms, histograms and smoothing are analyses whose result…
nodes.text:
Transforms, histograms and smoothing are analyses whose result can become a table (Results › New table from result), not live linked tables

Why: Keeps the core simple; the analysis itself stays live.

nodes.label: Second Python worker (Calc) for results and Excel; graphs keep…
nodes.text:
Second Python worker (Calc) for results and Excel; graphs keep their own

Why: Long fits never block drawing; memory cost ~100 MB.

nodes.label: Samples and wording lean to materials science and engineering…
nodes.text:
Samples and wording lean to materials science and engineering (tensile tests, Arrhenius plots, calibration lines, spectra)

Why: The user's background.

nodes.label: 0.3.0 = the full check, not 1.0 (the user: "we are still not…
nodes.text:
0.3.0 = the full check, not 1.0 (the user: "we are still not completed"): FAMILY §11 completed. Core: ID_LIMIT 1<<30 with renumber() (on load for duplicate/zero/huge ids, and when take_id reaches it), graph settings clamped in normalize, write_atomic for every save, Table has a hand-written PartialEq (empty row titles fast; destructures every field so new ones must be compared), Paste uses saturating positions. Shell: panic = "unwind", guard() around edits/open/import/formulas + crash.log panic hook, poisoned locks recover (PoisonError::into_inner), read_small (8 MB) for options/recent/meta, updater safe_name + private download folder + 600 MB cap, the FAMILY CSP. Python: files.atomic for every export, xlsx formula cells forced to text, CSV readers turn csv errors and bad workbooks into plain messages. CI: platforms job (core release tests + Python tests on Windows and macOS), npm audit --omit=dev, the engine smoke test; SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md

Why: The user asked for a complete check before 1.0, as done for Datum Plan.

nodes.label: Publisher "Datum" for the whole family (bundle.publisher…
nodes.text:
Publisher "Datum" for the whole family (bundle.publisher; copyright stays "© 2026 Edgar Mendonca")

Why: The user's family-wide rule (FAMILY §9 in the hub).

nodes.label: Session 1 (brainstorm)
nodes.text:
· The user started Datum Plot as the second Datum app and asked to follow FAMILY.md exactly, brainstorm, write docs/PLAN-0.1.md, and create CLAUDE.md and this file before building.
· Read Datum Plan (read-only): FAMILY.md, CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, CHANGELOG.md and the reference code (styles, sprite, ribbon, backstage, print, selection/cells/fmt, update.rs, workflows, UI tests) and the draft logo.
· Wrote PLAN-0.1.md: Prism vs Origin, architecture, 15 ideas, 0.1.0 scope, release plan to 1.0, 14 questions.

nodes.label: Session 1, continued (0.1.0)
nodes.text:
· The user approved the plan, icon and colours, wants to see the app before answering the questions, and decided Python goes inside the app (numpy, SciPy, matplotlib; Rust as the shell, SolidJS as the window; 200–300 MB is fine). Recorded in PLAN-0.1 §9 and the decisions above.
· Built: Rust core (model, ops, undo, files, templates; 11 tests), Python engine (stats, Prism-style matplotlib graphs, exports, worker protocol; 12 tests against R values), shell (commands, Python worker manager with cache and restart, updater, recovery), UI (navigator, XY grid on Plan's grid engine, graph view with hover and double-click hits, docked Format Graph, ribbon, File page, Options, Print, help), CI and release workflows with the bundled Python.
· Checked in the real app under Xvfb: Home, opening each sample, typing and Ctrl+E (the excluded value leaves the graph), range selection with Sum/Average/Count, double-click on the X axis → Format Graph › X Axis, live "Connect the points", log X dose-response. Fixed: missing base grid-cell CSS (headings were shifted one column); Format Graph hid the graph (now docked right); docked overlay class clashed with the sidebar's .side; dialogs without inputs or OK did not close on Escape (focus fallback).
· 23 Playwright checks pass, with a real Python render. Screenshots in docs/images/. Also fixed: fast typing lost characters (and Enter) pressed before the edit box had the focus.
· Released 0.1.0 with release.yml (workflow_dispatch): CI green; the release build's smoke test started the bundled Python on Windows and got the versions back; installer 55 M

nodes.label: Session 2 (review of 0.1.0, feature brainstorm)
nodes.text:
· Feedback on 0.1.0 (one screenshot: Growth graph with Format Graph docked): first start 3–6 s, install under a minute, the app is fast and should stay so; graph text is in Arial as intended; Copy Picture does not work; updates are slow (the whole 55 MB installer each time); too little to evaluate yet, so brainstorm the full feature set first, then build in steps; asked how graphs are made.
· Diagnosis: Copy Picture uses the browser clipboard, which WebView2 disables because the window's address (http://tauri.localhost) is not a secure origin (the Linux test browser allowed it, so tests passed); same for Paste Special's fallback and the Print page's code copy. Updates: 50 of the 55 MB is the Python runtime, re-downloaded every time.
· Wrote PLAN-0.2.md: how a graph is made (diagram), diagnosis, feature catalogue A–J (data tables, analyses with their Python libraries, results, graphs, on-screen editing, layouts, export, Python scripting, speed, help), libraries and sizes (pandas, openpyxl, statsmodels, scikit-posthocs, lmfit, lifelines, pybaselines, python-pptx/docx; not pingouin: GPL), architecture changes, release plan 0.1.1 → 1.0, 10 questions. Roadmap above replaced by its summary. No code changed. Waiting for the answers.

nodes.label: Session 3 (answers, 0.1.1)
nodes.text:
· The user answered PLAN-0.2: no Prism files, nothing missing; background materials science R&D (lots of linear regression and statistics on many data points), now project management; "build the app first: lay out the whole UI, then build feature by feature"; keep tracking everything in memory. Decisions and the new order are in PLAN-0.2 §10 and the decisions table.
· Built 0.1.1:
· Engine: Import op (+ test); Python io.py (CSV/TSV/TXT with delimiter sniffing and decimal commas, XLSX with openpyxl) + 2 tests; worker read.
· Shell: runtime.rs (runtime pack, unzip test), update.rs download/asset helpers and -update.exe preference, py.rs reader thread with timeouts and restart(), clipboard commands, import_file, restart_engine.
· UI: features.ts (99-feature catalogue), roadmap.tsx (Roadmap page, planned-command cards, New Table / Analyze / Graph Type galleries, Import dialog), planned commands across Data, Analyze, Graph, Format and the new Layout and Tools tabs, Copy Picture via Rust, engine status while the runtime unpacks or downloads.
· Release: runtime zip + update installer + full installer. Released 0.1.1 (CI green): setup 89 MB, update 2.3 MB, runtime-1.zip 87 MB.
· Checked in the real app (Xvfb): Analyze tab and gallery; Import through the real file dialog of a tensile-test CSV (2 replicates guessed from the headings) → table and graph; Copy Picture put a 944 × 708 PNG (80 × 60 mm at 300 dpi) on the clipboard (xclip); ribbon folds the Item group at 1440 px. 31 UI checks, 14 Python tests, 12 + 1 Rust tests pass.

nodes.label: Session 4 (one installer, 0.2 plan)
nodes.text:
· Feedback on 0.1.1: updated from the app (~87 MB), installed quickly, opened fast; wants one file per release (no separate update installer or runtime pack, it confuses people); import "kind of works"; Copy Picture works now; the app misses many features: list what comes next, brainstorm, then start.
· Changed the release to a single installer: release.yml builds one -setup.exe with runtime.zip; update.rs downloads -setup.exe; runtime.rs no longer downloads a runtime (always in the installer); catalogue I1 reworded. Not released yet (goes out with 0.2.0).
· Wrote PLAN-0.2.0.md: what 0.2 adds (results sheets with Explain, descriptive, normality, outliers, linear regression with fit range/Deming/compare lines/bands/equation, curve fitting with a model library and own equations, data tools, styles), materials ideas B27 tensile, B28 Arrhenius, B29 Weibull, B30 S–N, B31 DSC/TGA (added to features.ts and PLAN-0.2), build notes (Analysis items, py/datum/analyses/, second worker, statsmodels + lmfit, runtime 2), split 0.2.0/0.2.1/0.2.2, 6 questions. Waiting for the answers.

nodes.label: Session 5 (answers, roadmap, 0.2.0)
nodes.text:
· The user: combine the first two parts into one 0.2.0, then small consecutive releases 0.2.1, 0.2.2 … up to 0.3 (no jumped numbers); Arrhenius yes; the rest as proposed; keep updates small and quick to save tokens; keep memory and CLAUDE.md complete. Recorded in PLAN-0.2.0 §9, the roadmap above, features.ts (releases per feature) and CLAUDE.md.
· Built 0.2.0: Analysis items and overlays in the core (+ test), py/datum/analysis.py + models.py (+ 12 tests against R/NIST), curves on graphs with bands and equations, result/models commands, results.tsx (options dialogs, results sheet with Explain), Analyze gallery and ribbon buttons made real, Tensile and Arrhenius samples, statsmodels + lmfit (runtime 2), single-installer release.
· Checked in the real app (Xvfb): Tensile sample graph with both modulus lines over 0–0.003 and equations; the results sheet (summary per alloy, comparing the lines, residual plots, answer, checks, methods). Fixed: samples lost their fit overlays when opened (the shell rebuilt graph settings from Options); 2.034e+05 → 203400 in labels; equation labels placed in the emptiest corner with a light background; "DFn = 1.0".
· 26 Python tests, 13 + 1 Rust tests, 38 UI checks pass. Released 0.2.0 (CI green): one installer, 113 MB (statsmodels, lmfit and pandas added to the Python pack).

nodes.label: Session 6 (0.2.1, ? help)
nodes.text:
· User: every Datum app gets a small ? beside its tools that says what the tool is for and how to use it (built first in Datum Atlas 0.1.1); no separate teaching mode.
· Built: ui/src/help.tsx copied from Atlas with 35 Plot topics; G (ribbon group) takes h, the navigator Head takes h, Dialog and Gallery take help; ? on the table head, graph footer, results head and Info sheet; Help › What Is This Tool?; i-help icon; .help/.helpcard styles. Catalogue J5 added (PLAN-0.2, features.ts); 0.2.1–0.2.5 renumbered 0.2.2–0.2.6 in features.ts, PLAN-0.2.0 §9 and the roadmap above.
