nodes.label: Session 7 (the big build, 0.2.2)
nodes.text:
· User (after testing 0.2.0: "works very well… loads in a few seconds"): list what is pending and propose a big build of 10–15 features. Proposed seven big builds; the user: "complete 0.2.1 and 0.2.2 together, as one version… optimise as we do it… keep everything in memory". Another session had meanwhile released 0.2.1 (? help) on this branch, so the big build was merged with it and became 0.2.2; features.ts, PLAN-0.2 §11 and the roadmap renumbered (0.2.3–0.2.7, 1.0).
· Built (28 features): Python groups.py and tools.py (all checked against R); global fit + model comparison in analysis.py (make_model, start, fit_one, global_fit, compare_models; new kinds load lazily via more_kinds() to avoid a circular import); graph.py palettes, column graphs, bee swarm, brackets, shaded areas; io.write_excel; worker excel. nodes.label: Datum Atlas
nodes.text:
Choose the right material: property charts, selection and referenced data, in one app for Windows.

For: Design and materials engineers, and students.

Stack: Rust engine (crates/core) + Rust shell (src-tauri), Tauri 2, WebView2, SolidJS + Vite UI in strict TypeScript, plain CSS tokens, IBM Plex. Own SVG chart engine (geometry in Rust). Chart.js later for bar/radar, GridCraft later for expressions. No Python.

nodes.label: Own Rosenbrock 2(3) stiff solver instead of diffsol's BDF for…
nodes.text:
Own Rosenbrock 2(3) stiff solver instead of diffsol's BDF for now

Why: The block system is a black box stepped by our loop (hits, zero-crossings, streaming, stop/pause); a one-step method with a finite-difference Jacobian and dense output fits that loop with no dependency. Robertson and Van der Pol (μ = 1000) pass. diffsol stays the candidate for DAEs in 0.4

nodes.label: Signals are vectors with inferred widths; most blocks work…

nodes.label: Piecewise-constant sources use the step's start time inside a…
nodes.text:
Piecewise-constant sources use the step's start time inside a step (Ctx::tseg) and the solver lands on every jump (next_hit)

Why: A step input never smears across a solver step: the step time is hit exactly with every solver

nodes.label: Machines in their natural frames: induction in the stationary…
nodes.text:
Machines in their natural frames: induction in the stationary αβ frame with flux linkages as states (no speed-dependent frame, wound-rotor voltages turned by p·θ); synchronous machines in the rotor dq frame with Park inside; three-phase signals are width-3 vectors; transforms amplitude-invariant

Why: Exact steady states against the equivalent circuit; one signal type; inductance matrices inverted once at build

nodes.label: Typical ratings live in the engine (motors::presets, served…
nodes.text:
Typical ratings live in the engine (motors::presets, served with the library) and the Inspector applies one as a single Batch of SetParam

Masks are on the subsystem block (Block.mask: params, icon text, help, presets); values live in the block's params like any block's. Flattening opens a scope per masked subsystem; scope_vars evaluates each mask's values in the scope around it, so inner names hide outer ones and the model's variables

Why: One evaluation path for every block; errors point at the subsystem

nodes.label: Cursor values, step marks and the probe's values come from the…
nodes.text:
Cursor values, step marks and the probe's values come from the engine (value_at, step_marks in measure.rs); the window only draws

nodes.text:
Log all signals is a run setting (SimSettings.log_all); probe channels carry probe: true and the block (or subsystem) and port the wire leaves from

Why: One logging path; sinks and the probe never mix

nodes.label: The shell keeps the last five runs (plus the current) for…
nodes.text:
The shell keeps the last five runs (plus the current) for Compare; channels are matched by name

Why: Small, enough to compare a few tunings

nodes.label: Discrete blocks keep their own state inside the block (not the…
nodes.text:
Discrete blocks keep their own state inside the block (not the solver's state vector) and change only at sample hits; at a hit the output is computed from state and input, then update moves the state on

Why: Same pattern as ZOH and unit delay; no solver changes; exact difference equations

nodes.label: Rates worked out in the compiler (Rt::rate, fixed point over…
nodes.text:

nodes.label: The shell, ribbon, backstage, options, help, roadmap, updater…
nodes.text:
The shell, ribbon, backstage, options, help, roadmap, updater, workflows and tests are copied from Datum Plan and renamed

Why: FAMILY §12: copy, don't reinvent

nodes.label: Regions are a flat list in reading order (no free x/y placement)
nodes.text:
Regions are a flat list in reading order (no free x/y placement)

Why: A calc is read top to bottom; order is the evaluation order; simpler editing, printing and tests

nodes.label: Each region keeps the text the user typed; results, LaTeX and…
nodes.text:
Each region keeps the text the user typed; results, LaTeX and errors are computed from it, never stored

Why: What is printed is always what the engine computes from the text

nodes.label: Calc's parser is its own small Pratt parser, not Plan's…
nodes.text:
Calc's parser is its own small Pratt parser, not Plan's GridCraft formula engine

Why: GridCraft evaluates spreadsheet formulas without units; Calc needs units on numbers, assignments, ranges and user functions. Plan's lesson kept: the engine computes, errors stay on their own line

nodes.label: The .dcalc reader opens damaged files field by field and drops…
nodes.text:
The .dcalc reader opens damaged files field by field and drops only the regions it cannot read; ids are renumbered when duplicated

Why: FAMILY §11 hardening: damaged files open as far as possible

nodes.label: Printing packs regions measured at the printed width into…
nodes.text:
Printing packs regions measured at the printed width into pages, never cutting a region; references (style Reference) print at the end

Why: A calc sheet must look professional; equations split over pages are hard to check

nodes.label: The region editor stays open when the ribbon is clicked (Math…
nodes.text:
The region editor stays open when the ribbon is clicked (Math and Units keys type into it)

Why: The symbol keys would otherwise end the edit before typing

nodes.label: Page text stays dark on a light page in the dark theme
nodes.text:
Page text stays dark on a light page in the dark theme

Why: The page is paper; it prints black on white

nodes.label: Angle is a soft tag: it never makes values incompatible, but…
nodes.text:
Angle is a soft tag: it never makes values incompatible, but picks rad/s, rpm or degrees for display

Why: An angle is a ratio; rpm ↔ rad/s works with rad = 1, and sin(30 deg) needs no special case

nodes.label: °C and °F values are absolute temperatures (abs); a difference…
nodes.text:
°C and °F values are absolute temperatures (abs); a difference of two is plain kelvin; adding a difference keeps it absolute; a mean stays absolute; a difference asked in °C shows as Δ°C

Why: Engineers mix both; the classic mistake (°C × factor with the offset) must not happen

nodes.label: After a number, the first word is a unit if it is one; after…
nodes.text:
After a number, the first word is a unit if it is one; after that * and / continue the unit only for units that are not names on the sheet; 2*t is never a unit

Why: Readable input (120 m^3/h) without surprises when a name is also a unit symbol

nodes.label: σ is not a built-in constant (it is the usual name for…
nodes.text:
σ is not a built-in constant (it is the usual name for stress); Stefan–Boltzmann is σ_SB. Constants (g, π, e, R, σ_SB, N_A, k_B, c_0) give way to names on the sheet

Why: The brief lists σ; a silent constant behind an undefined stress would be dangerous

nodes.label: Utilisation is demand over capacity: lhs/rhs for ≤ and <…
nodes.text:
Utilisation is demand over capacity: lhs/rhs for ≤ and <, rhs/lhs for ≥ and >

Why: A check reads the same whichever way it is written

nodes.label: Solve and plot exist already in 0.1.1 (the engine had them)…
nodes.text:
Solve and plot exist already in 0.1.1 (the engine had them); 0.1.2 brings tables, pictures and the units list

Why: Engine first; the cut order (image, table, plot) still holds

nodes.label: The window shows results only from the engine (calc in every…
nodes.text:
The window shows results only from the engine (calc in every Out); the whole sheet is worked out after every change

Why: Simple and fast enough (1,500 lines well under a second in release builds; a speed gate tests it)

nodes.label: KaTeX and Plex fonts are bundled as woff2 only (a Vite…
nodes.text:
KaTeX and Plex fonts are bundled as woff2 only (a Vite transform drops woff/ttf)

Why: Smaller installer; WebView2 reads woff2

nodes.label: A table is columns (name, unit, optional formula) over rows of…
nodes.text:
A table is columns (name, unit, optional formula) over rows of typed cells; each column becomes a vector; formula columns are evaluated with the columns to their left

Why: Pump curves and data-sheet values are tables; vectors plug into interp, sum, max and plots

nodes.label: The table editor keeps its edits local and saves them as one…
nodes.text:
The table editor keeps its edits local and saves them as one change when it closes

Why: Every save re-renders the sheet; typing from cell to cell must not lose focus, and undo should undo the whole edit

nodes.label: After a unit, * and / never read the constants (g, e, R, c_0)…
nodes.text:
After a unit, * and / never read the constants (g, e, R, c_0), a function's parameters or a for variable as units

Why: 0.1.1 read kg/m^3*g as grams (found when checking the table formula in the real app)

nodes.label: Packs are plain .dcalc files embedded with include_str!, each…
nodes.text:
Packs are plain .dcalc files embedded with include_str!, each with a test comparing its results with hand values worked out independently (in the test comments) before running

Why: The brief: every pack is a test; the files stay editable in the app

nodes.label: Text after # on a line is its description (shown beside it…
nodes.text:
Text after # on a line is its description (shown beside it, printed)

Why: A calc sheet describes its inputs; packs needed it

nodes.label: Pack units are set per region where the automatic choice would…
nodes.text:
Pack units are set per region where the automatic choice would mislead (kN·m for moments, N·m for torque, kVA/kvar)

Why: Energy and torque share a dimension; apparent power shares watts

nodes.label: Pack references cite textbooks and standards (White, Karassik…
nodes.text:
Pack references cite textbooks and standards (White, Karassik, Colebrook, Brown, Incropera, Roark, Gere, Shigley, Chapman; IAPWS-IF97, ASME VIII-1 UG-27, ISO 898-1/724, IEC 60034-1)

Why: The brief: each pack cites its textbook or open standard

nodes.label: An input literal shows in its typed unit when that unit…
nodes.text:
An input literal shows in its typed unit when that unit belongs to the sheet's system (or to both); otherwise the ladder converts it

Why: 8356 cm⁴ must not read 83.56×10⁶ mm⁴; a US sheet should still show US units

nodes.label: Numbers ≥ 10⁴ are rounded to the significant figures and…
nodes.text:
Numbers ≥ 10⁴ are rounded to the significant figures and grouped with thin spaces

Why: 274863 showed six figures with digits = 4

nodes.label: Getting Started is a sheet (like a pack), not only a dialog
nodes.text:
Getting Started is a sheet (like a pack), not only a dialog

Why: People learn by changing a working example

nodes.label: Doc::save writes name.dcalc.saving and renames it over the…
nodes.text:
Doc::save writes name.dcalc.saving and renames it over the sheet; Doc::open refuses files over 64 MB and reads bytes lossily; normalize cuts regions (5,000), text (20,000), pictures (8 MB), table rows (2,000) and columns (50); edits beyond them fail

Why: A crash mid-save must never damage a sheet; a hostile file must not exhaust memory

nodes.label: ErrorBoundary around each region, the sheet view, the…
nodes.text:
ErrorBoundary around each region, the sheet view, the Variables panel and each printed region; utilisation formatted by ratio() that accepts anything

Why: A UI test with malformed engine output showed the panel's toFixed could blank the whole window

nodes.label: A check's left side reads in the unit its name is shown in…
nodes.text:
A check's left side reads in the unit its name is shown in (Env::shown)

Why: 0.0095 ≤ 0.03 for a percentage check

nodes.label: An input keeps its typed unit when the other system has no…
nodes.text:
An input keeps its typed unit when the other system has no ladder for it; electrical units and cP/cSt are neutral; US head is BTU/lb

Why: ohm/km became SI base units on a US sheet; cP became Pa·s

nodes.label: The print summary of checks is a pseudo-region (id −1)…
nodes.text:
The print summary of checks is a pseudo-region (id −1) measured and packed like the others, saved in sheet.ui.print.summary

Why: Reuses the page packing; a long summary moves the sheet down instead of overlapping

nodes.label: Lines are limited to 60 nested levels and 1,000 symbols, trees…
nodes.text:
Lines are limited to 60 nested levels and 1,000 symbols, trees deeper than 400 are refused, and the sheet is worked out on its own 64 MB-stack thread

Why: Thousands of brackets overflowed the stack (an abort on any build); the release build aborts on any panic, so limits come first and the thread is a second guard

nodes.label: Results must be finite and unit powers within ±60; unit powers…
nodes.text:
Results must be finite and unit powers within ±60; unit powers in a unit expression above 60 are not read as units

Why: 1e308×10 showed nothing; m^999 was silently m^127; i8 saturation made −128 whose abs() panicked (found by the new fuzz test)

nodes.label: The angle tag is dropped by roots and fractional powers when…
nodes.text:
The angle tag is dropped by roots and fractional powers when it does not divide evenly

Why: ∛ of a torque from P/n (rad⁻¹) failed in the shaft pack

nodes.label: Substituted values use the unit each name is shown in on its…
nodes.text:
Substituted values use the unit each name is shown in on its own line (Env::shown)

Why: Base units (m²·kg/s²) for a torque read badly next to its N·m line

nodes.label: The fuzz test builds random sheets from the grammar (numbers…
nodes.text:
The fuzz test builds random sheets from the grammar (numbers with units, names, operators, functions, checks, solve, plot, ranges, tables), 600 sheets per run in CI; 6,000 × 3 seeds and a release run before this release

Why: Random characters rarely reach the evaluator; grammar-shaped input found two real panics at once

nodes.label: release.yml ran once on a push trigger to register it (tag…
nodes.text:
release.yml ran once on a push trigger to register it (tag pushes are blocked from the session); later releases use workflow_dispatch

Why: A workflow needs one run before GitHub lists it

nodes.label: Windows publisher "Datum"; copyright stays "© 2026 Edgar…

Windows publisher "Datum"; copyright stays "© 2026 Edgar Mendonca"

Why: Family-wide rule (FAMILY §9)

nodes.label: model.rs
nodes.text: The model: analysis kind, nodes, members, sections, materials, shapes (polygons with bulge arcs, circles, holes), supports and loads with targets (node, member, edge, point, body), mesh settings; check (every invariant); .dmesh read item by item with migration and repair (damaged files open as far as possible, with warnings) and write

nodes.label: doc.rs
nodes.text: Edit operations (Add, Set, AddMember by points, Move, Delete with cascade, InsertCorner, RemoveCorner, JoinCrossings, SetSettings, SetMeta, Batch) on a copy, kept only if check passes; snapshot undo/redo; changed = differs from the saved snapshot

nodes.label: sections.rs
nodes.text: Section properties (A, I, c) for rectangle, round bar, tube, box, I, channel, angle and custom

nodes.label: sparse.rs
nodes.text: The shared linear solver: triplets, supports by elimination, prescribed values, faer sparse Cholesky, a probe solve that catches mechanisms, residual

nodes.label: mesh.rs
nodes.text: Meshing parts: outlines (arcs split by the local size) into a spade constrained Delaunay triangulation inside a frame round the part, refined for angle and size; local sizes from refined edges and points grow into the global size (a size field: too-large triangles get a point at their centre, then refinement again); triangles kept where there is material (centroid test); 6-node triangles with midside nodes on true arcs; boundary edges tagged with their shape edge; quality

nodes.label: plane.rs
nodes.text: Plane stress and plane strain: T3/T6 elements, edge pressure (× thickness) and edge forces (whole force or per length, for the whole thickness), gravity, point loads, fixed/pinned/roller/symmetry supports (rollers on sloping or curved edges by a stiff spring along the normal), reactions, the equilibrium check (forces, and moments against forces × reach), stresses recovered and averaged at nodes, per-element values, von Mises, principals, safety factor

nodes.label: heat.rs
nodes.text: Steady heat conduction: T3/T6, fixed temperatures, flux, convection, generation; heat flux recovered at nodes and per element; heat flows at every support and load and the heat balance

nodes.label: materials.rs
nodes.text: The materials library: 54 metals and plastics from Datum Atlas with sources (E, ρ, k, α the middle of the range, yield the low end, ν typical for the family); the script rebuilds the JSON from an Atlas checkout

nodes.label: lib.rs
nodes.text: Results (frame, plane or heat, tagged by kind) and solve() for any analysis; tests that every example solves, balances and agrees with hand checks

nodes.label: wire.rs
nodes.text: Results packed for the window: long numeric arrays as base64 (f32 values, u32 indices), everything else unchanged; the window's unwire (ui/src/api.ts) unpacks them

nodes.label: bigpart.rs
nodes.text: A 25 000-element bracket's results as JSON, for timing the window by hand (not a test)

nodes.label: solid.rs
nodes.text: 3D solids (0.3.0): the section's 2D mesh swept into layers (Swept), 18- and 6-node wedges (triangle × line shape functions), faces for loads and supports (side faces from edges, end faces), penalty rollers on sloping faces, nodal stresses averaged by volume, principal stresses, the outer surface for the window (Surface), MAX_UNKNOWNS

nodes.label: space.rs
nodes.text: 3D frames: local axes (axes), the 12×12 beam (axial, torsion, bending both ways) and truss bars, member loads in any direction, supports and springs in six directions, results along members (N, Vy, Vz, T, My, Mz, 3D deflection), six-way equilibrium

nodes.label: plane3.ts
nodes.text: Working planes of a 3D frame: the projected model the canvas edits (planeModel), faint members off the plane, depths, and lift turning canvas edits into 3D

nodes.label: space3.tsx
nodes.text: 3D frames without three.js: the colour-by choice and range, the deflection scale, the 3D legend and the plane bar (loaded at startup)

nodes.label: fonts.css

nodes.label: size.cjs

nodes.label: view3d.tsx
nodes.text: Loaded lazily (the only module importing three.js). The three.js 3D view: members, nodes, supports, loads, the deflected shape coloured by a result, picking and placing, the probe, the plane bar and the 3D legend

nodes.label: modal.rs
nodes.text: Natural frequencies and buckling (subspace shared, Kind): subspace iteration on one sparse Cholesky of K, Rayleigh–Ritz with a small dense Cholesky and Jacobi eigen solve; mode shapes scaled to a largest movement of 1

nodes.label: modes.tsx
nodes.text: Modes on the drawing (frames along members; parts through the contour canvas, 16 cached swing steps), the mode list, the animation, the frequency table

nodes.label: frame.rs
nodes.text: Frames and trusses: beam and truss stiffness, linear member loads as consistent nodal loads, self-weight, springs, reactions, equilibrium sums, exact N, V, M and deflection along each member (41 stations), stress and utilisation

nodes.label: bench.rs
nodes.text: The verification benchmarks as data (run() → rows with result, reference, error, source); the test fails on any row over its tolerance

nodes.label: verify.rs

nodes.text: FAMILY §11: failed edits change nothing, random edits keep the model valid and round-trip, damaged files, speed gate

nodes.label: PLAN-0.1.md
nodes.text: The plan, the public summary and roadmap, the change log

nodes.label: Everything in the brief §1 (name, crimson accent, identifier…
nodes.text:
Everything in the brief §1 (name, crimson accent, identifier, .dmesh, stack, own Rust solver, 12-band blue-to-red contours with viridis in Options, ribbon tabs, logo)

Why: Made with the user in the hub, session 13

nodes.label: The shell and window are copied from Datum Sim, which is…
nodes.text:
The shell and window are copied from Datum Sim, which is Plan's skeleton already adapted to a canvas app, without Sim's Python and run thread

Why: The brief says copy, don't reinvent; Sim's copy is the closest to a drawing app

nodes.label: Model in SI base units; display units in one window module…
nodes.text:
Model in SI base units; display units in one window module; frames show m (ft), parts mm (in)

Why: One owner for conversions; no rounding when the user switches units

nodes.label: One id counter for every item; supports and loads point at a…
nodes.text:
One id counter for every item; supports and loads point at a Target (node, member, edge of a shape, point, body)

Why: Edits and deletes cascade simply; one support or load type for frames and parts

nodes.label: Plane geometry as polygons whose segments may bulge into arcs…
nodes.text:
Plane geometry as polygons whose segments may bulge into arcs (bulge = tan(θ/4), as in DXF), plus circles; holes are shapes with hole: true

Why: Fillets, rounded lugs and slots without a CAD kernel; maps directly to DXF import in 0.2

nodes.label: Every edit is checked by Model::check on a copy and refused if…
nodes.text:
Every edit is checked by Model::check on a copy and refused if it breaks anything; the reader repairs damaged files item by item and lists what it dropped

Why: FAMILY §11: failed edits change nothing, damaged files open as far as possible

nodes.label: serde_json with float_roundtrip
nodes.text:
serde_json with float_roundtrip

Why: The hardening test found coordinates changing in the last digit after save and open

nodes.label: Atlas has no Poisson's ratio: Mesh's library (0.1.3) adds ν…
nodes.text:
Atlas has no Poisson's ratio: Mesh's library (0.1.3) adds ν from typical values with its own source

Why: Atlas data checked in session 1

nodes.label: Nodes take clicks before the load arrows drawn on them
nodes.text:
Nodes take clicks before the load arrows drawn on them

Why: The UI test found the wind load's arrows on the portal frame's eave node stealing the drag

nodes.label: faer 0.24 (MIT) sparse Cholesky with its own fill-reducing…
nodes.text:
faer 0.24 (MIT) sparse Cholesky with its own fill-reducing ordering, no default features (no rayon, rand, npy)

Why: The brief's choice; 200 000 equations factor in 0.1 s here

nodes.label: A probe solve (a load equal to the diagonal) alongside every…
nodes.text:
A probe solve (a load equal to the diagonal) alongside every solve; an answer over 1e11 means a mechanism

Why: faer factored an exactly singular matrix when rounding left a tiny positive pivot (found by the spring-chain test)

nodes.label: Member results are integrated exactly (with linear loads M is…
nodes.text:
Member results are integrated exactly (with linear loads M is a cubic): deflection v = v_a + θ_a s + ∫∫M/EI, stretch from N/EA

Why: Step-by-step integration missed the mid-member deflection by 5e-4 (found by benchmark 2); exact now to 1e-9

nodes.label: Distributed loads in global x or y are per length of the…
nodes.text:
Distributed loads in global x or y are per length of the member, not projected

Why: The simplest rule to explain; stated in the help and the Inspector

nodes.label: Moments drawn on the tension side; N and V on the member's…
nodes.text:
Moments drawn on the tension side; N and V on the member's local +y

Why: Common practice for moments; one fixed rule for the others, stated in the legend

nodes.label: After an edit results stay drawn but faded and marked out of…
nodes.text:
After an edit results stay drawn but faded and marked out of date; Solve is F5 (no automatic re-solve)

Why: Clear about what the picture shows; solving is instant for frames, but meshed parts will not be

nodes.label: A fixes release after a review of 0.1.1 (the user's request)…
nodes.text:
A fixes release after a review of 0.1.1 (the user's request): 13 findings, each with a test; meshing moves to 0.1.3, heat/materials/report to 0.1.4, polish to 0.1.5

Why: The user: "make 0.1.2 a fixes release for 1–13"

nodes.label: Every edit joins geometry: added or moved nodes merge into a…
nodes.text:
Every edit joins geometry: added or moved nodes merge into a node already there and split members they land on; added or moved members are split at nodes along them (distributed loads split linearly); Model::check refuses coincident nodes; repair merges them in old files

Why: A member drawn to the middle of another was not connected (misleading "mechanism" error, or a column carrying nothing); arrow-key moves could stack nodes

nodes.label: Corners are added and removed by engine ops (InsertCorner…
nodes.text:
Corners are added and removed by engine ops (InsertCorner, RemoveCorner) that renumber edge targets; a split edge's loads cover both halves (a total edge force is shared); a corner in an arc splits the arc

Why: The window's own corner editing moved loads to the wrong edge

nodes.label: The equilibrium check is judged against the size of the loads…
nodes.text:
The equilibrium check is judged against the size of the loads (forces summed without signs; moments about the origin likewise), forces and moments both; computed in the engine (imbalance)

Why: Dividing by the net force gave 6.8e19 % for a moment alone

nodes.label: Mechanism probe limit 1e15 plus two steps of iterative…
nodes.text:
Mechanism probe limit 1e15 plus two steps of iterative refinement in every solve

Why: A cantilever in 500 pieces was called a mechanism (probe ≈ 3n⁴); at 1 000 pieces rounding cost 6e-5, refinement recovers 1e-9

nodes.label: Results drawing reads the view inside JSX or memos only
nodes.text:
Results drawing reads the view inside JSX or memos only

Why: Diagrams and utilisation lines were computed once and stayed behind after pan or zoom

nodes.label: Display values below 1e-9 of their scale are shown as 0…
nodes.text:
Display values below 1e-9 of their scale are shown as 0 (clean); typed numbers go through parseNum ("−", "1,5", "1,200", empty refused)

Why: Noise like 1.5e-14 kN·m; negative corners could not be typed; empty became 0

nodes.label: Switching units picks a round grid step in the new units…
nodes.text:
Switching units picks a round grid step in the new units (niceGrid); member lengths use the drawing's unit

Why: 0.5 m showed as 1.6404 ft

nodes.label: Open, New, an example or a recent file ask to save unsaved…
nodes.text:
Open, New, an example or a recent file ask to save unsaved changes first

Why: Work was lost without a question

nodes.label: The user asked for 0.1.4's work (heat, materials library…
nodes.text:
The user asked for 0.1.4's work (heat, materials library, report) inside 0.1.3: one release with meshing, plane stress and strain, heat, the library and the report; polish becomes 0.1.4

Why: The user: "carry on with 0.1.3 and add 0.1.4 part too in 0.1.3"

nodes.label: A frame of four points round the part before triangulating…
nodes.text:
A frame of four points round the part before triangulating; minimum area for refinement from the finest local size

Why: Near-collinear points on a sloping edge made hull slivers spade could never refine; a minimum area from the global size skipped the small triangles near a refined hole

nodes.label: Local sizes are a size field (local size + 0.2 × distance…
nodes.text:
Local sizes are a size field (local size + 0.2 × distance, capped by the global size), applied by inserting centroids of too-large triangles and refining again

Why: Refining only the points on an edge let the mesh coarsen within one element of a hole; the plate-with-a-hole error jumped about (1 %, 0.1 %, 0.4 %) instead of falling. Now 1.1 % → 0.5 % → 0.1 % → 0.04 %

nodes.label: Benchmark 4 is a quarter plate 200 hole diameters wide with…
nodes.text:
Benchmark 4 is a quarter plate 200 hole diameters wide with the hole's edge refined, against Kirsch's 3.0

Why: A plate 20 diameters wide converged to 3.018 (its own finite-size answer), not 3.0

nodes.label: Pressure acts per area (× thickness); an edge force is per…
nodes.text:
Pressure acts per area (× thickness); an edge force is per length of edge for the whole thickness, or the whole force

Why: Found in the app: the L-bracket's 1.5 kN edge force was multiplied by the 10 mm thickness, giving 2.9 MPa instead of 287 MPa; now a test, and a hand check of the bracket

nodes.label: Stresses: nodal averages (smoothed) and each element's own…
nodes.text:
Stresses: nodal averages (smoothed) and each element's own average (per element), both sent to the window

Why: Comparing the two shows where the mesh is too coarse, without a separate error estimate

nodes.label: Contours as 12 band paths (Path2D) in model coordinates on a…
nodes.text:
Contours as 12 band paths (Path2D) in model coordinates on a canvas under the SVG; polygons closed with lineTo, never closePath

Why: closePath on 100 000 sub-paths took 10 s in Chromium; now 0.2 s to switch result, 0.8 s to draw 25 000 elements

nodes.label: The safety factor's colours run red (low) to blue, capped at…
nodes.text:
The safety factor's colours run red (low) to blue, capped at 10; nodes with no yield strength are grey

Why: A factor of 10⁶ in a lightly loaded corner would otherwise squash the scale

nodes.label: Moments in the equilibrium check of parts are judged against…
nodes.text:
Moments in the equilibrium check of parts are judged against forces × the model's reach (as frames)

Why: A bore pressure centred on the origin has no moment of its own: the flange showed a 110 % "imbalance" of rounding noise

nodes.label: Model::check looks members' nodes up in a map
nodes.text:
Model::check looks members' nodes up in a map

Why: Each edit of a 10 000-member frame took 52 ms (a linear search per member); now 14 ms

nodes.label: Long result arrays go to the window as base64 f32/u32…
nodes.text:
Long result arrays go to the window as base64 f32/u32 (wire.rs); drawing triangles are rebuilt in the window

Why: 22 MB of JSON for 25 000 elements; now 6.2 MB. Seven significant digits are more than any display shows; equilibrium sums stay in full precision

nodes.label: A pin load (Bearing): pressure p₀ max(0, −n·F̂) on the edge…
nodes.text:
A pin load (Bearing): pressure p₀ max(0, −n·F̂) on the edge, scaled so the push along F̂ is the whole force

Why: The lug's pin was an even traction all round the hole, pulling on the far side too

nodes.label: Crossing members join only on request (Format › Join Where…
nodes.text:
Crossing members join only on request (Format › Join Where They Cross, Op::JoinCrossings)

Why: Automatic joining would connect X-bracing that passes without a joint

nodes.label: The document is "changed" when it differs from the saved…
nodes.text:
The document is "changed" when it differs from the saved snapshot; saving writes a temp file then renames

Why: 0.1.1 review: undo to the saved state stayed changed; a crash mid-save could corrupt the file

nodes.label: A drag snaps the grabbed point (node, member start, first…
nodes.text:
A drag snaps the grabbed point (node, member start, first corner) to the grid, not the offset

Why: 0.1.1 review: items off the grid stayed off it

nodes.label: Each top-level setting is read on its own; one that cannot be…
nodes.text:
Each top-level setting is read on its own; one that cannot be read falls back to its default with a warning

Why: 0.1.1 review: an unknown analysis or a negative counter refused the whole file

nodes.label: The user asked for a big update toward 3D FEA for simple…
nodes.text:
The user asked for a big update toward 3D FEA for simple problems; plan in docs/PLAN-0.2-0.3.md. Answers: 3D parts by extruding or revolving 2D parts; analyses first (thermal stress, axisymmetric, frequencies, buckling, 3D frames), then 3D solids, then DXF and Calc/Plot; three.js for the 3D view; small numbered releases

Why: The user's answers, 2026-10-29

nodes.label: Thermal stress inside a stress model: fixed temperatures and…
nodes.text:
Thermal stress inside a stress model: fixed temperatures and convection in a stress or strain model are solved as heat conduction on the same mesh first; a uniform Warming body load adds to it; t_ref is the stress-free temperature

Why: One model, one mesh, no linking of two files

nodes.label: A solve whose residual is over 1e-8 warns that the supports…
nodes.text:
A solve whose residual is over 1e-8 warns that the supports barely hold the part

Why: Rollers on curved edges are stiff springs, so a part free to turn about an arc's centre was not caught as a mechanism (found by the random parts)

nodes.label: Points moved onto arcs are moved back when a triangle would fold
nodes.text:
Points moved onto arcs are moved back when a triangle would fold

Why: A hole crossing the outline folded a sliver (found by the random parts)

nodes.label: Axisymmetric solids share plane.rs: B and D carry a fourth…
nodes.text:
Axisymmetric solids share plane.rs: B and D carry a fourth (hoop) strain, used only by Axi; weights 2πr; edge forces and pressures are totals round the circle; nodes on the axis are held radially without a support; the equilibrium check sums axial forces only

Why: One element code for plane and turned solids

nodes.label: The automatic element size is also capped at √(area / (0.43 ×…
nodes.text:
The automatic element size is also capped at √(area / (0.43 × 800)) (about 800 triangles)

Why: The vessel's 10 mm wall got one element through it at a twenty-fifth of the part's height

nodes.label: Datum Mesh does not become CAD or a pre-processor; sketch…
nodes.text:
Datum Mesh does not become CAD or a pre-processor; sketch tools (0.3.1) before the cutting plane; Gmsh bundled in the installer from 0.4 (separate program; app itself stays under 5 MB, installer grows by Gmsh's size)

Why: The user's answers 2026-10-30 (docs/PLAN-0.3-0.4.md)

nodes.label: 3D solids are the 2D mesh swept through the thickness into…
nodes.text:
3D solids are the 2D mesh swept through the thickness into wedges (18-node from quadratic, 6-node from linear), not a tetrahedral mesher

Why: Robust (the 2D mesher's quality), no new mesher, exact layers through the thickness; arbitrary 3D shapes wait for an outside mesher (0.4+)

nodes.label: End faces are a target of their own (Target::End { front })…
nodes.text:
End faces are a target of their own (Target::End { front }); side faces are the part's edges

Why: No face picking in 3D needed to load a solid; old files unchanged

nodes.label: The sparse system can store only its lower half…
nodes.text:
The sparse system can store only its lower half (System::lower), and faer runs on every core (rayon, MIT/Apache)

Why: A 3D solid of 178 000 unknowns took 22.7 s and 3.1 GB on one core; on four, 15 s; 90 000 take 6 s and 1.2 GB

nodes.label: A 3D solid is refused beyond 200 000 unknowns, with how to…
nodes.text:
A 3D solid is refused beyond 200 000 unknowns, with how to coarsen

Why: 500 000 needed 9.9 GB; one test run was killed out of memory: a crash in the app

nodes.label: The window gets a solid's outer surface only (nodes…
nodes.text:
The window gets a solid's outer surface only (nodes, triangles, fields there); extremes over every node

Why: A 90 000-unknown solid's surface is a small part of its nodes

nodes.label: Budgets: installer under 5 MB (release.yml), window startup…
nodes.text:
Budgets: installer under 5 MB (release.yml), window startup code under 400 kB and whole window under 1.6 MB (tools/size.cjs, CI); speed: typical models under 1 s, large ones (about 100 000+ unknowns) under 10 s, timed in the verification record (bench::timings)

Why: The user asked that the app stay small and optimised; budgets that fail the build keep it so

nodes.label: three.js is loaded only when a 3D frame is shown (lazy…
nodes.text:
three.js is loaded only when a 3D frame is shown (lazy view3d.tsx); fonts as woff2 only

Why: Startup code 863 → 282 kB

nodes.label: 3D buckling is flexural only: the geometric stiffness has no…
nodes.text:
3D buckling is flexural only: the geometric stiffness has no twisting term

Why: Without warping stiffness an I-section twists under axial load at a small fraction of its real load (the portal gave λ = 0.25); flexural-torsional and lateral-torsional buckling need a warping degree of freedom, later

nodes.label: 3D frames reuse the plane frame's modal solvers…
nodes.text:
3D frames reuse the plane frame's modal solvers: space::assemble(m, pieces) with beams cut in 8, consistent masses (polar mass for twisting), geometric stiffness both ways

Why: One path for supports and loads in static, modal and buckling solves

nodes.label: Datum Mesh's purpose written down (top of this file); frames…
nodes.text:
Datum Mesh's purpose written down (top of this file); frames stay in the app but stop short of building design (no code checks or code combinations)

Why: Keeps one clear purpose: analysis of parts and structures, verified, not code design

nodes.label: The Windows publisher is "Datum" (bundle.publisher), as for…
nodes.text:
The Windows publisher is "Datum" (bundle.publisher), as for the whole family (FAMILY §9); the copyright stays "© 2026 Edgar Mendonca"

Why: One publisher name across the family's installers

nodes.label: 3D frames are a separate analysis (Space) with y up and z as…
nodes.text:
3D frames are a separate analysis (Space) with y up and z as depth; the plane model gains z, roll, fz, mx, my, gz and six-way springs as serde defaults

Why: Old files open unchanged; a plane frame is the 3D frame with z = 0 (benchmark 13 checks the portal to 1e-13)

nodes.label: Member axes: local y = z × x (the plane frame's local y), or…
nodes.text:
Member axes: local y = z × x (the plane frame's local y), or global y for a member along z; roll turns y and z about x

Why: Plane frames keep their signs and moments in 3D; beams along z have their depth upright

nodes.label: Members are drawn on working planes (Front, Side, Plan at a…
nodes.text:
Members are drawn on working planes (Front, Side, Plan at a depth) by the existing canvas through a projected model, and seen in a separate three.js view

Why: Reuses every 2D tool (snap, draw, move, supports, loads); no 3D drawing tool to learn; the 3D view only views, picks and places

nodes.label: three.js 0.185.1 (MIT) for the 3D view, pinned exactly
nodes.text:
three.js 0.185.1 (MIT) for the 3D view, pinned exactly

Why: The 3D solids of 0.3 will use the same view

nodes.label: Buckling solves B φ = μ K φ for the largest μ = 1/λ, so K…
nodes.text:
Buckling solves B φ = μ K φ for the largest μ = 1/λ, so K (positive) stays the matrix factorised and the small problem stays well posed when B has both signs

Why: Members in tension make K_G indefinite; λ ≤ 0 (buckling with the loads reversed) is dropped

nodes.label: Beams are cut into 8 pieces (frame::SPLIT) for modes and…
nodes.text:
Beams are cut into 8 pieces (frame::SPLIT) for modes and buckling, not for the static solve

Why: One cubic element is exact statically but 21 % high for a pinned column's buckling; 8 pieces give 3e-5 to 5e-4

nodes.label: Truss bars are checked on their own as pinned struts rather…
nodes.text:
Truss bars are checked on their own as pinned struts rather than cut

Why: A pin-jointed bar has no bending unknowns; π²EI/L² is its exact answer

nodes.label: Natural frequencies by subspace iteration (p = max(2q, q + 8)…
nodes.text:
Natural frequencies by subspace iteration (p = max(2q, q + 8) vectors, one factorisation of K) rather than a Lanczos code

Why: Simple and robust for the few lowest modes asked for; checked against a mass-spring chain to 1e-9

nodes.label: Frame assembly (frame::assemble) and the plane solver's…
nodes.text:
Frame assembly (frame::assemble) and the plane solver's assembly (plane::run with a modes request) are shared by static and modal solves

Why: One place for supports and held unknowns

nodes.label: Help › Verification runs bench::run() in the app, so the…
nodes.text:
Help › Verification runs bench::run() in the app, so the report is always true for the version running; the same rows are tests and the dated record

Why: The brief's headline feature, earlier than planned because it was cheap

nodes.label: Session 1 (day 1: plan, skeleton, 0.1.0)
nodes.text:
· Read the brief, the hub's CLAUDE, MEMORY, FAMILY and brand; Plan's and Sim's code; Atlas's data (31 metals with sources; no Poisson's ratio).
· Wrote PLAN-0.1, CLAUDE.md, this memory, docs/site.json, README, CHANGELOG, NOTICE, SECURITY, CONTRIBUTING; drew the icon (L-bracket mesh with a darker hot spot, amber diamond).
· Engine: model, check, repair, edits with undo, sections, six examples; 14 tests including hardening. The hardening tests found two real faults on their first run (float round-trip in the file; the id counter going backwards on repair).

nodes.label: model.rs
nodes.text: The model: nodes (number and position), elements (From, To, DX/DY/DZ, pipe, material, line conditions, component, extra load), pipes, materials (tables against temperature), line conditions (T1–T3, P1–P3, hydrotest), supports, nozzles, loads, load cases, title block, settings; layout (positions from the deltas, loops must close); check (every rule); .dpipe read item by item with migration and repair (damaged files open as far as possible, with warnings), and write

nodes.label: doc.rs
nodes.text: Edit operations (Add, Set, Delete with cascade, SetStart, Split, Renumber, Loop (expansion loop wizard), Duplicate (copy or mirror a section with its supports), SetSettings, SetMeta, SetCases, RecommendCases, Batch) on a copy, kept only if layout and check pass; snapshot undo/redo

nodes.label: library.rs
nodes.text: Pipe sizes ½"–24" and schedules (ASME B36.10M/B36.19M dimensions); five materials (carbon, 1¼Cr-½Mo, 304, 316, duplex 2205) with E and α against temperature and typical allowables min(Su/3, 2Sy/3), with sources; interp

nodes.label: units.rs
nodes.text: Calc's unit table (NIST SP 811) with unit expressions and the display table for SI and US

nodes.label: cases.rs
nodes.text: Which operating cases are used; the recommended load cases (OPE1–3, SUS, EXP1–3, EXP ranges between cases, HYD); rebuild keeps ids by name

nodes.label: sparse.rs
nodes.text: Mesh's sparse solver: triplets, faer Cholesky, probe solve for mechanisms, iterative refinement, residual; solve_many (every load case with one factorisation, prescribed values per case)

nodes.label: mat.rs
nodes.text: 3-vectors, 6×6 matrices (inverse, move a force to another point), local axes of a pipe, 4-point Gauss

nodes.label: geom.rs
nodes.text: The analysis geometry: bends trimmed by R·tan(θ/2) into arcs (near, middle = the bend's node, far points), shared points, tees with their plane; bend radii from NPS; sent to the window for the 3D view

nodes.label: elements.rs
nodes.text: The 3D pipe element from its exact flexibility ∫ Bᵀ C B ds (axial, shear with κ = 0.5, torsion, bending with the bend's k), inverted and moved to 12×12; uniform loads and thermal growth as equivalent nodal loads; end forces and section resultants

nodes.label: code.rs
nodes.text: The process piping code's equations: pressure design thickness and hoop stress, minimum wall with corrosion and mill tolerance, bend and tee SIFs and flexibility (h, pressure correction), reducer SIF, sustained stress, displacement stress range, allowable range (basic and liberal), f from cycles

nodes.label: solve.rs
nodes.text: The analysis: parts (sections, weights, strains, SIFs), assembly, supports (rigid axis-aligned ones held exactly with imposed displacements as prescribed values; skewed or flexible ones as springs), basic loads, every case solved together, ranges as differences, forces in local axes, reactions, code stresses per segment end, nozzle loads in nozzle axes, minimum wall, the equilibrium check

nodes.label: iso.rs
nodes.text: The isometric: the 30° projection (x = (X − Z) cos 30°, y = (X + Z) sin 30° − Y), lines per segment (arcs sampled), node labels, a dimension per element offset away from the middle, symbols for supports, nozzles and tees, sheets of at most n elements in table order with their joins

nodes.label: worked.rs
nodes.text: Hand-worked cases for every component and support kind (spring, settlement, guide, line stop, rest, skewed restraint, valve weight, constant support, reducer taper and SIF, tee SIF, nozzle axes, liberal allowable and f)

nodes.label: Support.one_way (rests) and Support.gap (rests, guides, line…
nodes.text:
Support.one_way (rests) and Support.gap (rests, guides, line stops, restraints); new rests from the window and the examples are one-way, files without the field stay two-way

Why: Lift-off is the realistic default, and old files keep their results

nodes.label: Each Sum case is solved by iteration with its own support…
nodes.text:
Each Sum case is solved by iteration with its own support states (start: touching for a one-way rest without a gap, open for a gap; change every wrong state each solve, at most 100); ranges stay OPE − SUS of the settled results

Why: The usual practice; ranges as differences keep the code's displacement range meaning

nodes.label: A touching rigid support along a global axis is held exactly…
nodes.text:
A touching rigid support along a global axis is held exactly at its gap (prescribed value); flexible or skewed ones are springs with an offset

Why: Same exactness as linear supports, so the benchmarks match to rounding

nodes.label: When open gaps leave a mechanism, the open supports get 1 N/mm…
nodes.text:
When open gaps leave a mechanism, the open supports get 1 N/mm and the case is solved again, with a warning; the small loads are reported

Why: A straight run held sideways only by gapped guides is common and must solve

nodes.label: Linear-only models keep the one-factorisation path, bit for bit
nodes.text:
Linear-only models keep the one-factorisation path, bit for bit

Why: No change to results or speed for models without one-way or gapped supports

nodes.label: The Windows publisher is "Datum" (bundle.publisher in…
nodes.text:
The Windows publisher is "Datum" (bundle.publisher in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json); the copyright stays "© 2026 Edgar Mendonca"

Why: A family-wide change (FAMILY §9 in the hub); nothing else in the repo names the publisher

nodes.label: Public words about the code: "calculates using the published…
nodes.text:
Public words about the code: "calculates using the published equations of ASME B31.3", "contains none of the code's text, tables or figures", "not affiliated with or endorsed by ASME", ASME and B31.3 named as trademarks; Help › Sources (SOURCES in ui/src/help.tsx) lists each equation with an open-literature reference, and says plainly where an equation is the code's own (reducer SIF, the 1.25/0.25 range factors, Ts)

Why: The owner asked to be safe from any use of copyrighted material: equations and physical facts are not protected, the code's wording, tables and figures are, and none is in the app. Citations were checked against library and journal records before use; Lorenz (1910) was left out as unconfirmed, the bend factor is derived from the torus instead

nodes.label: Bend wall: an extra check per bend at its intrados with I =…
nodes.text:
Bend wall: an extra check per bend at its intrados with I = (4R/D − 1)/(4R/D − 2); the extrados (I < 1) is not listed, the straight check covers it

Why: The intrados governs; one line per bend keeps the table short

nodes.label: t ≥ D/6 fails the wall check, with a warning, rather than…
nodes.text:
t ≥ D/6 fails the wall check, with a warning, rather than switching to a thick-wall equation

Why: The code asks for special consideration there; the app says so instead of guessing

nodes.label: Ze = π r₂² Ts at a tee's branch end (setting branch_ze, on)…
nodes.text:
Ze = π r₂² Ts at a tee's branch end (setting branch_ze, on), for both sustained (corroded walls) and expansion (nominal)

Why: The earlier editions' rule; editions that use the branch pipe's own Z turn it off

nodes.label: Pressure elongation (setting pressure_elongation, off) is…
nodes.text:
Pressure elongation (setting pressure_elongation, off) is added to the thermal strain of straight, non-rigid, non-reducer segments in cases 1–3, so it is in OPE and in EXP = OPE − SUS, never in SUS; bends' Bourdon opening is not modelled

Why: Off keeps every earlier model's results unchanged; the strain-in-OPE convention is the usual one

nodes.label: Two rigid supports holding one direction at a node share its…
nodes.text:
Two rigid supports holding one direction at a node share its reaction equally, with a warning

Why: The split between rigid supports is statically indeterminate; equal shares keep each support's load plausible and the sum right

nodes.label: The 0.2 stage is split into the small releases 0.1.5–0.1.11…
nodes.text:
The 0.2 stage is split into the small releases 0.1.5–0.1.11; 0.2.0 is a milestone release with no new features

Why: The owner asked for many small steps instead of one big 0.2 release

nodes.label: Everything in the brief §1 (name, moss accent, identifier…
nodes.text:
Everything in the brief §1 (name, moss accent, identifier, .dpipe, stack, own Rust solver, three.js, units, ribbon tabs, logo, codes as published equations, public words)

Why: Made with the user in the hub, session 16

nodes.label: The shell and window are copied from Datum Mesh (Plan's…
nodes.text:
The shell and window are copied from Datum Mesh (Plan's skeleton by way of Sim, already adapted to an engineering-analysis app)

Why: The brief: copy, don't reinvent; Mesh is the closest app

nodes.label: Y is up; X east, Z south (right-handed). The first node of…
nodes.text:
Y is up; X east, Z south (right-handed). The first node of each connected piece starts at the origin unless moved

Why: The usual piping convention; one rule for the table, the 3D view and the isometric

nodes.label: Bends and tees are components on the element that ends at…
nodes.text:
Bends and tees are components on the element that ends at their node (a bend turns into the element leaving the node)

Why: One column in the table; matches how a stress sketch is marked up

nodes.label: Line conditions are named sets (T1–T3, P1–P3, hydrotest) that…
nodes.text:
Line conditions are named sets (T1–T3, P1–P3, hydrotest) that elements reference, rather than six columns per row

Why: A table that fits the screen; one place to change a line's conditions

nodes.label: Temperatures are kelvin in the file (SI base), shown in °C or °F
nodes.text:
Temperatures are kelvin in the file (SI base), shown in °C or °F

Why: SI base units in the file, as every Datum app

nodes.label: Typical allowables are worked out from typical strengths as…
nodes.text:
Typical allowables are worked out from typical strengths as min(Su/3, 2Sy/3) at temperature, up to the family's usual limit (creep range not covered)

Why: The brief forbids copying code tables; this is the published basis of the process piping code's allowables below the creep range, and gives the familiar 138 MPa (20 ksi) for carbon steel

nodes.label: Modulus and expansion against temperature: Atlas's room values…
nodes.text:
Modulus and expansion against temperature: Atlas's room values with trends typical for each family, marked with their sources

Why: Atlas has room-temperature values only

nodes.label: The display table comes from the engine (Calc's units), not…
nodes.text:
The display table comes from the engine (Calc's units), not from factors in the window

Why: One owner for conversions; the brief says copy Calc's units engine

nodes.label: SI lengths in mm everywhere; US lengths along the pipe in ft…
nodes.text:
SI lengths in mm everywhere; US lengths along the pipe in ft, sizes and displacements in in; pressure in bar (SI) or psi

Why: What piping engineers use in each system

nodes.label: Load cases are rebuilt after every edit while "automatic" is…
nodes.text:
Load cases are rebuilt after every edit while "automatic" is on (ids kept by name); editing a case turns it off

Why: Always right for a new model; the user stays in control

nodes.label: Every element (straight, arc, reducer, rigid) from its exact…
nodes.text:
Every element (straight, arc, reducer, rigid) from its exact flexibility by quadrature along the centreline, then inverted and moved by equilibrium

Why: One path for every component, exact for straight pipe and for arcs (16 × 4 Gauss points); reducers taper naturally; matches the hand flexibility method to 1e-14

nodes.label: Shear deformation with κ = 0.5 (thin tube); the beam-theory…
nodes.text:
Shear deformation with κ = 0.5 (thin tube); the beam-theory benchmarks include the shear term

Why: Short spans near nozzles are common in piping; the references say so

nodes.label: Rigid supports along global axes hold their degree of freedom…
nodes.text:
Rigid supports along global axes hold their degree of freedom exactly (imposed displacements as prescribed values); skewed or flexible ones are springs, a skewed rigid one 1e12 N/m

Why: Exact anchors and rests keep the benchmarks at 1e-14; a penalty only where it is needed

nodes.label: The modulus at the installed temperature for every case…
nodes.text:
The modulus at the installed temperature for every case; thermal strain from mean coefficients from 21 °C: α(T)(T − 21) − α(T₀)(T₀ − 21)

Why: The process piping code's practice for displacement stresses; the library's tables are mean coefficients

nodes.label: Bend flexibility and SIF pressure corrections use the highest…
nodes.text:
Bend flexibility and SIF pressure corrections use the highest operating pressure of the line

Why: One stiffness for every case keeps one factorisation; conservative for the SIF in lower-pressure cases (k is lower)

nodes.label: Rigid elements are 1000 × the pipe's stiffness; their weight…
nodes.text:
Rigid elements are 1000 × the pipe's stiffness; their weight replaces the pipe's metal, the contents and insulation stay

Why: Stiff enough to be rigid, soft enough for a well-conditioned solve

nodes.label: Tee SIFs apply at every segment end on the tee's point, with…
nodes.text:
Tee SIFs apply at every segment end on the tee's point, with each leg's own section modulus

Why: Simple and on the safe side; the branch's effective section modulus can come later

nodes.label: The equilibrium check is judged against the larger of the…
nodes.text:
The equilibrium check is judged against the larger of the loads, the reactions, the model's weight and 1 N

Why: The hardening test found a thermal range on a model with one anchor (no reactions at all) reported as 79 % "imbalance" of rounding noise

nodes.label: The window gets the analysis geometry (arcs, points) with…
nodes.text:
The window gets the analysis geometry (arcs, points) with every model, so the 3D view never works out bends itself

Why: The engine is the one owner of geometry and results

nodes.label: Releases follow the brief's steps, but 0.1.1 already shows…
nodes.text:
Releases follow the brief's steps, but 0.1.1 already shows code stresses and the results tables (the engine had them)

Why: Cheap once the solver was there; 0.1.2 is then about the remaining components, results polish and nozzle checks

nodes.label: The isometric and the full report (brief step 6) came in…
nodes.text:
The isometric and the full report (brief step 6) came in 0.1.2, with the four other examples; 0.1.3 is their polish and more checks, 0.1.4 the brief's step 7

Why: They were built while 0.1.1 was releasing; releasing them at once gives the user more to try

nodes.label: Example supports chosen like a designer would: a line stop…
nodes.text:
Example supports chosen like a designer would: a line stop instead of a second anchor on the rack, a spring next to the settling tank

Why: The first drafts gave a 3 MN axial load on the rack and 4.7 × the tank nozzle's allowable: correct numbers for poor layouts, but examples should show good practice

nodes.label: An independent review of the engine (a separate agent, told to…
nodes.text:
An independent review of the engine (a separate agent, told to report only) before the last release; every confirmed finding fixed with a regression test in worked.rs

Why: Two real bugs no test had caught: an expansion range between cases took Sh at the higher-numbered case, not the hotter one (unsafe), and a line stop or guide at a tee averaged the branch into its direction

nodes.label: A guide or line stop takes the run through its node (two…
nodes.text:
A guide or line stop takes the run through its node (two opposite directions), or the only segment at an end; at a corner it warns and uses the first element

Why: There is no single axis at a corner; saying so is better than guessing silently

nodes.label: Tees take their SIF from the run's pipe and their plane from…
nodes.text:
Tees take their SIF from the run's pipe and their plane from the run and branch (from the first two legs, with a warning, when there is no straight run)

Why: A tee marked on its branch element used the branch size (unsafe for a small branch)

nodes.label: Bend SIF pressure correction with the lowest operating…
nodes.text:
Bend SIF pressure correction with the lowest operating pressure, flexibility with the highest

Why: The SIF correction lowers stresses, so the lowest pressure is safe for every case; one stiffness keeps one factorisation

nodes.label: A flexible anchor's stiffness is translational; its rotations…
nodes.text:
A flexible anchor's stiffness is translational; its rotations stay rigid

Why: One number in N/m cannot also be a rotational stiffness

nodes.label: The equilibrium help says what the check proves (loads…
nodes.text:
The equilibrium help says what the check proves (loads applied, equations solved) and what it does not (stiffness, SIFs, axes)

Why: The review pointed out that a self-equilibrated element always balances; the benchmarks are what test the physics

nodes.label: The element table keys its rows by position (Solid's Index)…
nodes.text:
The element table keys its rows by position (Solid's Index), not by item

Why: Every edit returns a new model, so keyed rows were all rebuilt and the cursor was lost after each cell (found by a UI test that types across a row)

nodes.label: The loop wizard puts the loop in the middle of a straight…
nodes.text:
The loop wizard puts the loop in the middle of a straight element, sideways (horizontal plane) or upwards, with long-radius bends, and refuses a loop that does not fit its bends

Why: The common case in one dialog; anything else is typed in the table

nodes.label: Copy Section joins the copy's first node to a chosen node and…
nodes.text:
Copy Section joins the copy's first node to a chosen node and numbers the rest after the largest node; Mirror flips one axis of every delta (and of skewed restraints)

Why: Simple to explain; covers repeated runs and symmetric layouts

nodes.label: Iso tags: one per element, on its longest line; dimensions…
nodes.text:
Iso tags: one per element, on its longest line; dimensions node to node (centre to centre), offset away from the drawing's middle

Why: Bends have two arc segments and drew two tags each

nodes.label: file.rs
nodes.text: The project file: SQLite tables (meta, nodes, objects, attributes, sheets, items, lines, notes, issues (datasheet revisions with their snapshot), history, and an object_attributes view), atomic write, table-by-table read with repair, JSON fallback for 0.1 files and recovery copies

nodes.label: model.rs
nodes.text: The project: plant objects (Obj: id, uid, class, tag, hierarchy node, data; line numbers are PipingNetworkSystem objects) and the hierarchy (Node: plant › unit › area); items and line pieces are views with obj; the 0.1 JSON migration (migrate_1); sheets (number, title, size A3/A1/ANSI B/ANSI D, revisions, legend flag), items (symbol, position, quarter turns, mirror, scale, tag, data, off-page partner), lines (type, ends on a port, on another line or free, bend points, flow flip, data), notes (note, leader, Hold cloud), settings (line number format, rules off, hydraulic limits, roughness, grid); .dschema read part by part with normalize (damaged files open as far as possible, with warnings), and write

nodes.label: symbols.rs
nodes.text: The symbol library (about 80 of our own drawings in a small drawing language: polylines, outlines, fills, dashes, circles, arcs, ellipses, rectangles, text), ports with directions, categories, tag prefixes, in-line and terminal flags; placement (turn, mirror, scale); primitives and their SVG

nodes.label: classes.json
nodes.text: The class library (83 classes, DEXPI-style names, inheritance from PlantItem, symbols, prefixes, attributes with quantity, type, choices, DEXPI name, required) and its reader: attrs(project, class) merges inherited, own and project (settings.user_attrs) attributes

nodes.label: datasheets.rs
nodes.text: Datasheets: per instrument, primary element, control valve and relief device; General, Process conditions (from process_source: its line, a primary element it is tapped to, the equipment it is mounted on, else its loop's measurement), the class's own attributes, Specification (group), company attributes; Excel with one worksheet each. Revisions: build_in marks rows changed (Δ) against the last Issue snapshot (SI display units), next_rev (A… before purchase, 0… from purchase on), snapshot

nodes.label: import.rs
nodes.text: Datasheet import from Excel (calamine): read (sheets as text grids, capped), plan (match by tag; a table with a Tag header, or one datasheet per worksheet; labels by norm; units by unit_expr/quantity; kinds set, same, conflict, bad; unmatched tags, unknown labels). The window applies the "set" rows as one Op::Batch of SetData

nodes.label: loops.rs
nodes.text: Loop diagrams: all (loops of ≥ 2 members by first letter and number, relief devices left out), diagram (A3 sheet with the frame: field devices with their own symbols, JB terminal block, I/O box, control-system functions; wiring from the "Wiring" attributes jb, jb_terminals, cable, system, io; a To complete list)

nodes.label: cause.rs
nodes.text: Cause and effect: matrix (each interlock symbol: the items signalled to it, effects = valves, drives, equipment, final elements; the rest are causes; a switch wired straight to a final element is its own group, cell "X"); actions from the fail position (FC close, FO open, FL hold), drives stop, trip_action overrides; xlsx

nodes.label: dexpi.rs
nodes.text: DEXPI (Proteus XML) import (read: element tree with limits, units and fit-to-sheet, symbols from DatumSchemaSymbol, the class or a stand-in, nozzles matched by position, segments as pieces From → components → To, branches onto segments, flows as signal or impulse lines, attributes back to keys in SI) and export of a sheet: Equipment with Nozzles, PipingNetworkSystem per line-number object, PipingNetworkSegment per piece with CenterLine, PipingComponent (each once) and Connection; ProcessInstrumentationFunction; InformationFlow for signal and impulse lines; GenericAttributes (DEXPI names in SI, the rest in DatumSchemaAttributes); y up

nodes.label: pipes.rs
nodes.text: Pipe's sizes ½"–24" and schedules (ASME B36.10M/B36.19M dimensions); inside diameters
