nodes.label: The Tell Me overlay was class="ov top"; the title bar's .top {…
nodes.text:
The Tell Me overlay was class="ov top"; the title bar's .top { background } rule, later in the stylesheet, made it opaque and hid the window. Renamed the overlay's class to high (the same clash exists in Datum Plan's stylesheet but is harmless there)

Why: The user saw the window vanish behind Ctrl+K

nodes.label: DEXPI round trip: our export writes DatumSchemaSymbol…
nodes.text:
DEXPI round trip: our export writes DatumSchemaSymbol, LineKind, FlowDirection and the turn (Reference) and mirror (Axis Z = −1); numbers at full precision; impulse lines carry their line object's data. The import uses them when present, else the class, else a stand-in by kind

Why: A file we write must come back exactly; tested on every example (tags, line numbers, connections, positions, data, check results)

nodes.label: Check 8: a check valve counts only when the pump's flow…
nodes.text:
Check 8: a check valve counts only when the pump's flow reaches its inlet (port 0); reached at its outlet it is reported on the valve. Op::TurnRound mirrors an in-line item and swaps the lines on its two process ports

Why: Lines drawn by hand can meet a check valve backwards; splitting always orients it

nodes.label: The canvas's drag overlay is a keyed Show: a non-keyed Show's…
nodes.text:
The canvas's drag overlay is a keyed Show: a non-keyed Show's child ran once, so the line under the mouse (and the selection box) never followed the mouse. A click on a port (no drag) leaves the wire "sticky" until the next click

Why: The user saw lines appear only when finished

nodes.label: Quick insert is a popover at the point with a transparent…
nodes.text:
Quick insert is a popover at the point with a transparent backdrop, not a modal over the window

Why: The drawing must stay visible while choosing where a symbol goes

nodes.label: Cause and effect is derived from the drawing only: interlocks…
nodes.text:
Cause and effect is derived from the drawing only: interlocks are the interlock logic symbol (and switches wired straight to a final element); classification of each neighbour by category, not by line direction

Why: Nothing to keep in step; robust to lines drawn either way

nodes.label: DEXPI: one sheet per file (as DXF); components placed in the…
nodes.text:
DEXPI: one sheet per file (as DXF); components placed in the first segment that ends at them, loose ones in a "PNS-UNCONNECTED" system; signal connections to equipment refer to the equipment, process ones to its nozzle. Tested for well-formed XML, unique IDs and resolving references (examples and random projects); not yet validated against the schema or other tools — said so in the help

Why: Honest first step; references must never dangle

nodes.label: Import reads with calamine (MIT; NOTICE lists its crates)…
nodes.text:
Import reads with calamine (MIT; NOTICE lists its crates): writing an xlsx reader of our own would be weeks for no gain, and hostile files are its job. Rows that live on the line, vessel or drawing (key empty) are never written; a disagreement is a "conflict" row naming the source. Blank cells never clear. Numbers take the cell's own unit, else the header's "(unit)", else the project's display unit; gauge marks (psig, barg) are read as the pressure the datasheet shows

Why: The P&ID stays the one source for process data; imports must be safe to run twice

nodes.label: The datasheet layout is project data (Settings.ds_layout)…
nodes.text:
The datasheet layout is project data (Settings.ds_layout), filtering the datasheet view only: hidden rows keep data, are imported and are in issue snapshots; Δ counts only shown rows. The shell copies the default layout into every new project, examples too

Why: A company form is a view; hiding must never lose data

nodes.label: Loop = instruments with the same first letter and number…
nodes.text:
Loop = instruments with the same first letter and number (ISA-5.1), at least two, relief devices excluded. Wiring is five text attributes in the class library group "Wiring" (not on the datasheet). Primary elements are drawn without wiring. The diagram is engine prims on an A3 sheet with the standard frame, so print and (later) DXF draw the same thing

Why: Loop diagrams come from the same objects as the P&ID; nothing to keep in step

nodes.label: An issue (model::Issue, project-level issues, SQLite table…
nodes.text:
An issue (model::Issue, project-level issues, SQLite table issues) keeps the whole datasheet as text per "Section › Label" in SI display units; Δ compares the current SI datasheet to the last issue. Issues of a deleted object go with it (dropped silently in normalize). Undo withdraws an issue; there is no other way to delete one

Why: A snapshot of what was issued is what a revision means; SI display text survives unit switches and class changes; issued records should not be edited

nodes.label: File format 3: 0.1.8 refuses 0.1.9 files ("update Datum…
nodes.text:
File format 3: 0.1.8 refuses 0.1.9 files ("update Datum Schema") rather than opening them and dropping the revisions on save

Why: Losing issued revisions silently is worse than asking to update

nodes.label: Revisions: letters (A, B… Z, AA) for Preliminary and Issued…
nodes.text:
Revisions: letters (A, B… Z, AA) for Preliminary and Issued for Enquiry, numbers (0, 1…) for Issued for Purchase and As-built; suggested, the user may type another (unique per datasheet, at most 12 characters). Bulk issue gives each datasheet its own next revision

Why: Common practice in process plant documents; companies differ, so it is a suggestion

nodes.label: Datasheets are a view built by the engine from the object, its…
nodes.text:
Datasheets are a view built by the engine from the object, its class (attribute group places a row in a section) and its process source; derived rows carry their source and are not editable on the datasheet

Why: One copy of every value: the datasheet can never disagree with the P&ID

nodes.label: Process source order: a process line on the instrument; a…
nodes.text:
Process source order: a process line on the instrument; a process line through an in-line element it is tapped to; equipment it is tapped to by an impulse line; else its loop (same first letter and number), measurement first. Signal lines are never followed

Why: LT-101 on a vessel must show the vessel, not the vent; LIC-101 its transmitter, not PVSV-101

nodes.label: Delete { ids, keep }: deleting views only purges the objects…
nodes.text:
Delete { ids, keep }: deleting views only purges the objects of those views (and only when no other view shows them and keep is off); DeleteObjects removes objects with all their views. The window asks only when a deletion would leave an object drawn nowhere

Why: Objects kept on purpose (not drawn) must survive later edits; a question on every delete would be noise

nodes.label: Attribute keys stay the short internal keys (design_p, size…)…
nodes.text:
Attribute keys stay the short internal keys (design_p, size…) with the DEXPI name alongside (dexpi); class names are DEXPI-style and will be checked against the DEXPI specification when export is built

Why: No migration of existing data; DEXPI export maps names in one place

nodes.label: The class library replaces fields.rs; the window gets each…
nodes.text:
The class library replaces fields.rs; the window gets each used class's attributes (with the project's additions) in derived().attrs

Why: One owner of "what data a thing has"; project attributes show at once

nodes.label: The release workflow's Windows tests found that saving failed…
nodes.text:
The release workflow's Windows tests found that saving failed on Windows (flushing the new database through a read-only handle); fixed before 0.1.5 was published

Why: Windows refuses FlushFileBuffers on a read-only handle; Linux allows it

nodes.label: Objects own tags and data; items and line pieces point at them…
nodes.text:
Objects own tags and data; items and line pieces point at them (obj). A process line joined to an in-line symbol or a paired off-page connector whose other side has a line continues that line's object; otherwise it gets a new one with the sheet's next sequence number; NewLineObject splits a piece off

Why: The user's "objects are the master"; a line number is a real object, so the run inference (and its bugs) is gone

nodes.label: Objects no view shows are deleted with their last view (until…
nodes.text:
Objects no view shows are deleted with their last view (until 0.1.7 offers "remove from sheet only")

Why: No orphans until the Plant panel can show them

nodes.label: The history is kept in the document (not in the undo…
nodes.text:
The history is kept in the document (not in the undo snapshots) and saved in the file; undo and redo are recorded as changes too

Why: An audit trail must not disappear with an undo

nodes.label: SQLite via rusqlite (bundled); objects and attribute values…
nodes.text:
SQLite via rusqlite (bundled); objects and attribute values are real tables (queryable); geometry rows keep JSON columns; recovery copies stay JSON

Why: The user's single-database file; JSON for the parts nobody queries keeps the writer small

nodes.label: Ids stay u32 inside the file; every object also has a uid…
nodes.text:
Ids stay u32 inside the file; every object also has a uid (UUID form) for exchange and later merging

Why: Small ids keep the engine and window simple; the uid carries identity across projects

nodes.label: Versions stay consecutive (0.1.4 released, then 0.1.5…); the…
nodes.text:
Versions stay consecutive (0.1.4 released, then 0.1.5…); the object core order and defaults are in docs/PLAN-0.2.md §7; no reverse engineering of commercial software, only public documentation and open standards

Why: The user's answers after the proposal

nodes.label: Datum Schema becomes an object-based plant engineering tool…
nodes.text:
Datum Schema becomes an object-based plant engineering tool, not a drawing tool: objects are the master and symbols are views of them; a plant hierarchy (project › plant › unit › area); classes and attributes as data (a JSON class library, user attributes in Options); the project as one SQLite database with a history of every change; DEXPI names. The proposal and open questions are in docs/PLAN-0.2.md; 0.1.4 is held until they are discussed

Why: The user's direction after 0.1.3: an open-source tool in the class of the enterprise object-based plant engineering suites, for students, researchers and engineers

nodes.label: Everything in the brief §1 (name, magenta accent, identifier…
nodes.text:
Everything in the brief §1 (name, magenta accent, identifier, .dschema, stack, units, ribbon tabs, layout, own symbols after ISO 10628-2 and ISA-5.1, logo, public words)

Why: Made with the user in the hub, session 22

nodes.label: The shell (main.rs, styles, ribbon, File page, print, help) is…
nodes.text:
The shell (main.rs, styles, ribbon, File page, print, help) is copied from Datum Pipe, the newest copy of Plan's shell; the updater, guard, crash.log and atomic writes from Plan 0.4.3 itself

Why: Pipe's shell is already adapted to an engineering app; Plan carries the latest safety rules (FAMILY §11) and Pipe's release profile still aborts on panic

nodes.label: Symbols are data in the engine (a small drawing language)…
nodes.text:
Symbols are data in the engine (a small drawing language), turned into SVG for the window and into blocks for DXF

Why: One drawing per symbol; the window, print and DXF always agree

nodes.label: Positions are sheet millimetres (y down); text primitives are…
nodes.text:
Positions are sheet millimetres (y down); text primitives are placed by the middle of their height

Why: Prints at true size; one rule for SVG (dominant-baseline: central) and DXF (middle alignment)

nodes.label: Undo keeps the whole project before each edit (bounded to 200)…
nodes.text:
Undo keeps the whole project before each edit (bounded to 200) rather than inverse operations

Why: The brief asks for undo as operations; edits are operations, and a snapshot per operation is the simplest exact undo for a project of this size (Plan does the same)

nodes.label: A run (one pipeline) is the process lines joined through…
nodes.text:
A run (one pipeline) is the process lines joined through in-line items and off-page pairs whose line numbers agree; a size change at a reducer starts a new run

Why: The line list lists pipelines, not drawn pieces; the number carries the size, so it changes at a reducer

nodes.label: Data typed on a line goes to every drawn piece of its run…
nodes.text:
Data typed on a line goes to every drawn piece of its run; hydraulics are per run, from its first piece

Why: The pieces of one pipeline always agree, so the line list, badges and checks agree

nodes.label: Lines are drawn and routed by the engine (Sim's router, ports…
nodes.text:
Lines are drawn and routed by the engine (Sim's router, ports facing four ways); bend points the user drags are kept

Why: The brief: Sim's wires with bends you can drag

nodes.label: Instrument presets (PT, LIC, FIC…) in the palette; a new…
nodes.text:
Instrument presets (PT, LIC, FIC…) in the palette; a new instrument given only its letters takes the next free loop number on its sheet

Why: The brief lists the tag letters; loops share numbers (LT-101, LIC-101, LV-101)

nodes.label: Tags number 101 … on sheet 1, 201 … on sheet 2 (line sequence…
nodes.text:
Tags number 101 … on sheet 1, 201 … on sheet 2 (line sequence 1001 …, 2001 …)

Why: "Automatic numbering per prefix and sheet" in the brief

nodes.label: Manual valves take the prefix HV (hand valve), not V
nodes.text:
Manual valves take the prefix HV (hand valve), not V

Why: V is the vessels' prefix; the first test placed a valve tagged V-103 among vessels V-101 and V-102

nodes.label: The build ran ahead of the brief's step plan (checks, lists…
nodes.text:
The build ran ahead of the brief's step plan (checks, lists, hydraulics, DXF and examples were ready with the canvas), so 0.1.1 carries brief steps 3–6 and the next releases are speed, polish and the exhibition build; each CHANGELOG section says what its release really contains

Why: Releases stay small and true; holding finished work back to match a plan would only delay it

nodes.label: An independent review of the engine before the exhibition…
nodes.text:
An independent review of the engine before the exhibition build, as Datum Pipe did: run joining by number at items with 3+ lines, one new sequence per pasted pipeline, checks 8/10 walk through off-page pairs, merge skipped in loops and keeps the other half's data, running out of ids is an error, CSV quotes CR, no apostrophe in Excel text, DXF letters upright outside blocks and no 5-digit escapes

Why: Every confirmed finding fixed with a regression test; bend points on split left as a known limit

nodes.label: The DXF was read back with an independent reader (ezdxf…
nodes.text:
The DXF was read back with an independent reader (ezdxf 1.4.5): all four examples open with 0 errors and 0 repairs, blocks and TAG attributes intact, and render the right way up

Why: "Opens in any CAD program" should be checked by a reader we did not write

nodes.label: The router marks cells and edges inside symbols by index…
nodes.text:
The router marks cells and edges inside symbols by index ranges (binary search on the grid lines) and keeps distances in arrays, and its second search window is 120 mm

Why: Routing was 5 s on a crowded 500-symbol sheet; now 0.07 s with the same routes

nodes.label: One line number label and one hydraulic badge per run per…
nodes.text:
One line number label and one hydraulic badge per run per sheet, on its longest straight segment

Why: Labels on every short piece between valves cluttered the examples

nodes.label: A process-type line with an end on an instrument bubble or a…
nodes.text:
A process-type line with an end on an instrument bubble or a thermowell is an instrument connection: no number, not in the line list, not checked as a pipeline

Why: Impulse lines are part of the instrument, not the piping

nodes.label: Final elements for check 11 are control valves and regulators…
nodes.text:
Final elements for check 11 are control valves and regulators only (by symbol), not relief devices

Why: PSV and breather tags end in V too, and hid a missing control valve in Find the faults

nodes.label: The UI tests drive the real engine: examples/serve.rs answers…
nodes.text:
The UI tests drive the real engine: examples/serve.rs answers the shell's commands over a local HTTP port and serves the built window; api.rs holds what both return

Why: The brief's UI tests (place, connect, split, see a check appear and clear, export a list) need the real engine, not a canned fixture

nodes.label: Session 1 (0.1.0)
nodes.text:
· Read the brief, the hub (CLAUDE, MEMORY, FAMILY, BRAND, BRAIN) and the reference apps (Plan's shell and updater, Sim's canvas and router, Calc's units and pipe pack, Pipe's sizes and shell).
· Wrote CLAUDE.md, this MEMORY, PLAN-0.1; the logo (vessel, line with flow arrow and instrument bubble, pump, amber diamond) and the Windows icons.
· Engine: model and file with repair, symbols (82 definitions), fields, units, pipe sizes, routing, frame, graph, tags, edit operations with split and merge, view, hydraulics (tested against a hand calculation and Datum Calc's pipe pack); 23 tests.
· Window: ribbon, File page, Options (with the check rules and hydraulic limits), canvas, palette, inspector, bottom panel, print and SVG writer, help cards; the test server and 16 UI checks against the real engine.

nodes.label: Session 1, summary (0.1.0 → 0.1.4)
nodes.text:
· Released: 0.1.0 (shell, sheet, symbols, lines, updater), 0.1.1 (checks, hydraulics, lists, examples, print, DXF), 0.1.2 (fast routing, coloured badges, line number highlight, screenshots), 0.1.3 (fixes from an independent engine review), 0.1.4 (the exhibition build: final check, README demo). Each as DatumSchema-x.y.z-setup.exe + SHA256SUMS.txt from release.yml.
· Works: about 80 own symbols; lines port to port with routing, hops, flow arrows and signal marks; in-line symbols split lines and join them again when deleted; off-page connectors with jump; sheets A3/A1/ANSI B/ANSI D with zones, title block and revisions; legend sheet; notes, leaders, Hold clouds; tags and loops numbered per sheet, renumber, copy with the next free tag; the 13 checks with the Checks panel; line hydraulics with badges and editable limits; the four live lists with sort, filter, group, edit, CSV and Excel; print (sheets, lists with title block, legend), SVG, DXF (read by ezdxf with 0 errors); SI/US units; undo/redo; recovery; the updater. 55 engine tests (hardening, every check, hydraulics against a hand calculation and Datum Calc's pack, DXF read back, examples) and 47 UI checks against the real engine.
· Cut or not done: nothing from the brief's cut list was cut (the Hold cloud, line hops, ANSI sizes and the rarer symbols are all in). Not done: bend points are dropped when a line is split; check 8 does not look at a check valve's direction; the real shell was only started on Linux (Xvfb), the installer is built and published by the release workflow on Windows.
· The 2-minute exhibition demo: ope

nodes.label: Session 1, course change
nodes.text:
· The user changed direction after 0.1.3: an object-based plant engineering application, not a drawing tool (objects master, views on sheets, plant hierarchy, class library as data, SQLite with history, DEXPI names). 0.1.4 is committed but not released.
· Read the public documentation of the enterprise suites (object database across the lifecycle, base objects and classes, rules with real-time consistency and propagation, task lists, claims and working layers, revisions, 3D comparison) and of DEXPI (Proteus XML, specification CC BY 4.0, pyDEXPI). Wrote docs/PLAN-0.2.md with the proposal, the release order and seven questions for the user.

nodes.label: Session 1, 0.1.5 (the object core begins)
nodes.text:
· 0.1.4 released as agreed. Built 0.1.5: objects and views, line-number objects, the plant hierarchy model, the history, the SQLite file with 0.1 conversion. Engine 58 tests (new: SQLite round trip with history, 0.1 conversion, damaged databases); 48 UI checks including the SQLite file read back.
· Did not use the reverse-engineering toolkit the user pointed to: it is for inspecting other software, and the rule is to build from public documentation and open standards only.

nodes.label: Session 1, 0.1.6 → 0.1.8, and where we are
nodes.text:
· Released: 0.1.5 (objects, SQLite file with history; re-released after the Windows save fix), 0.1.6 (class library, Options › Classes, required attributes), 0.1.7 (Plant panel, delete the object or only the drawing, objects on several sheets), 0.1.8 (instrument datasheets).
· 0.1.8: datasheets.rs builds each datasheet; Specification attributes for Instrument, PrimaryElement, ControlValve and ReliefDevice in classes.json (group: "Specification"); datasheet and datasheets_all commands and the datasheets export kind; datasheet dialog (editable own values, grey derived rows), Print (one or all, A4 portrait with title block), Excel export; Inspector and Plant panel entries; help card. Tests: engine (line, vessel and loop sources; company section; Excel), hardening on random projects, UI (sections, vessel source, typing, printing one page).
· Found while building: the first loop fallback matched PVSV-101 for LIC-101 (same number, other loop) and followed a controller's signal line to its valve; both fixed and covered by the engine test.
· Next (to discuss): datasheet revisions and status, a company datasheet layout, loop diagrams; DEXPI export; datasheet import from Excel.

nodes.label: Session 1, 0.1.9 (datasheet revisions)
nodes.text:
· Built and released 0.1.9: Op::IssueDatasheet (one or many, rev suggested per status, by from the document's user), model::Issue with the snapshot, the issues table (format 3), Δ marks and was per row, revision block, next_rev, the Datasheet index list (fifth list kind) with bulk issue, Excel and print with revisions, history entries issue / undo withdraw.
· Tests: engine (revision sequence incl. Z → AA; issue, Δ for an own value and a line value, US units do not mark changes, duplicate and bad statuses refused, index row, undo, save and reopen, delete takes issues; format 2 files open cleanly; newer formats refused), hardening (random hostile issues), UI (not issued, suggested A, issue, Δ, index row, bulk issue of the shown rows).

nodes.label: Session 1, 0.1.10 (import, company layout…
nodes.text:
· The user asked for the three planned steps (Excel import, company layout, loop diagrams) as one release, 0.1.10.
· Engine: import.rs (calamine reader; table and one-sheet layouts; unit conversion; conflicts for line, vessel and drawing values), datasheets::full/all_full/layout_rows and the layout in build_in, model::DsLayout with logo checks, loops.rs, the Wiring attributes on Instrument and ControlValve. Shell and test-server commands import_datasheets, loops, loop_diagram, layout_rows; the default layout goes into every new project.
· Window: import preview dialog (tick, import as one Batch), Options › Datasheets (form, logo, footer, rows, order, use for new projects), logo, form and footer on datasheets and their print, loop diagrams dialog (list, preview, wiring table, print), Print with loop diagrams, ribbon Lists › Loop Diagrams and Import Excel, Inspector Loop diagram…, help cards.
· Tests: engine 74 (import table and read-back of our own export, units as typed, hostile bytes; layout; loops on every example; hardening runs import, layout and loops on random projects); UI 77 (import preview and apply, layout, loop diagram, wiring, print).
· Looked at the rendered loop diagrams: moved device text under the symbols (it crossed the wiring), drew primary elements without wiring.

nodes.label: Session 1, 0.1.11 (the user's two drawing…
nodes.text:
· The user reported: the symbol search popup covers everything; a line being drawn does not show until it is finished. Root cause of the second: the drag overlay in canvas.tsx was a non-keyed <Show> whose child read the drag once, so the preview stayed a zero-length stub at the start port (the selection box was affected too). Fixed with a keyed Show; added click-to-start lines that follow the mouse (Escape or right-click cancels) and a ringed snap target. The search is now a popover at the point.
· Added the cause-and-effect matrix (cause.rs, an interlock UY-202 in the compressor example), the DEXPI export (dexpi.rs) and loop diagrams in DXF (dxf::write_prims, sharing head with the sheet writer).
· Tests: engine 79 (matrix from the example and a direct switch; DEXPI well-formed with unique IDs and resolving references on every example, classes and attributes on the pump; loop DXF read back; hardening runs all three on random projects and found a byte-slicing panic on an emoji tag in the matrix code and a dangling DEXPI reference for branches onto signal lines, both fixed); UI checks for drag and click line drawing, the popover, the matrix, its print, DEXPI and loop DXF.
· The disk filled with build output during the session; cleared target/debug/incremental.

nodes.label: Session 1, 0.1.12
nodes.text:
· The user showed Ctrl+K hiding the whole window (and compared with Datum Plan). Reproduced in the test browser: the overlay's top class picked up the title bar's opaque background. Fixed, with a UI check that the overlay is translucent and the ribbon visible.
· Built the planned items: DEXPI import (with round-trip additions to the export), check 8 direction with Turn round (menu), bend points kept on split and join, the logo in Excel datasheets (base64 decoding moved into the engine).
· The round-trip test found two real export bugs, both fixed: attribute values rounded to 4 decimals (a gas viscosity became 0) and impulse lines losing their line-number data.
· Tests: engine 84 (DEXPI round trip on every example, a foreign file in metres with an unknown class, damaged XML; check 8 both ways; bend points; Excel logo; hardening imports every random project's export); UI checks for Tell Me, DEXPI import and Turn round.
